https://hyperallergic.com/who-gets-remem.title: Who Gets Remembered in Art History? New Free Online Course Explores Women Who Shaped Indonesian Art
https://hyperallergic.com/who-gets-remem.author: National Gallery Singapore
https://hyperallergic.com/who-gets-remem.text:
Who Gets Remembered in Art History? New Free Online Course Explores Women Who Shaped Indonesian Art
Co-developed by National Gallery Singapore and independent curator Alia Swastika, the course foregrounds women’s contributions to Indonesian art.
How have women artists shaped Indonesia's cultural, social, and artistic histories? National Gallery Singapore's new free online course, Art and Women in Indonesia: Stories that Empower, co-developed with independent curator Alia Swastika, explores this question through the practices and perspectives of leading contemporary artists.
“The absence of women [in historical accounts] does not necessarily indicate a lack of participation.” — Alia Swastika
The course underscores the importance of recovering women’s contributions and bringing overlooked figures and landmark events into view.
Through the work of artists from different generations, regions, and artistic backgrounds, Art and Women in Indonesia highlights a plurality of experiences and perspectives, offering new ways of understanding Indonesia’s histories and their continued resonance in the present.
Structured over five weeks, the course explores the practices of six artists and one collective whose work spans painting, sculpture, installation, performances, and collaborative forms. Together, they illuminate the diverse ways women have contributed to Indonesia’s cultural landscape while engaging questions of memory, power, gender, spirituality, and resistance.
Featured artists include Arahmaiani and Dolorosa Sinaga, whose works confront authoritarianism, censorship, conservatism, and the politics of the female body in public space. Through distinct artistic approaches, they expose the mechanisms through which women’s lives are regulated while fostering critical engagement with urgent social and political issues.
Art and Women in Indonesia: Stories that Empower also examines how Nunung WS, Titarubi, and Bakudapan Food Study Group navigate the relationship between individual experience and collective histories. Through installation, abstraction, and collaborative practices, they explore motherhood, cultural memory, care, and everyday labor as ways of engaging with broader social and political structures.
Drawing on Balinese cosmologies and visual traditions, Citra Sasmita and Mangku Muriati foreground female protagonists and goddesses, reworking inherited narratives and transforming painting into a site for feminist interpretation and historical reflection.
Accompanied by exclusive video interviews, readings, and discussion activities, the course provides deeper insight into the artists’ practices and the contexts from which they emerge. It also invites participants to reconsider the role of women in art history and to reflect on how art shapes the histories we remember, the narratives we inherit, and the futures we imagine.
Art and Women in Indonesia: Stories that Empower is part of National Gallery Singapore’s series of Online Courses on Southeast Asian Art. Join a growing global community of learners in exploring stories of women, art, and social change in and beyond Indonesia.
Register for free at nationalgallery.sg.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Em Lula 4, governo deve escolher ‘ministros com bom trânsito no Congresso’, avalia cientista política
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: José Bernardes
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
De volta ao Brasil, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) se reuniu com o senador Camilo Santana (PT-CE) e o governador reeleito do Piauí, Rafael Fonteles (PT), para falar sobre as tratativas da transição para a formação do novo governo.
A cientista política Mayra Goulart alerta que possíveis indicações de Rafael Fonteles ou mesmo Geraldo Alckmin para o Ministério da Fazenda são um tanto delicadas, porque é uma posição que deve ser ocupada por uma pessoa “passível de ser demitido”.
Na avaliação dela, o governo Lula 4 precisa conseguir escolher ministros de partidos dispostos a oferecer bancadas inteiras para votar com o governo. “O que foi feito no Lula 3 foi usar os ministérios para rachar os partidos. Foi uma estratégia usada para impedir que esses partidos votassem em sua totalidade com a oposição”, pondera em entrevista ao Conexão BdF, da Rádio Brasil de Fato.
Goulart considera que a estratégia foi bem-sucedida, mas precisa ser repensada porque, no próximo governo, Lula vai precisar conseguir mais. Nesse sentido, ela vê com bons olhos o nome de Camilo Santana para a Casa Civil. “É importante escolher ministros com bom trânsito no Parlamento. Me parece mais útil ter um ministro que tenha experiência no diálogo com os parlamentares que estão tendo cada vez mais protagonismo”, aponta.
A cientista política também observa que a oposição, neste momento, é menos atrativa. Por essa razão, é um momento interessante para Lula usar seu poder de negociação. “Eles saíram de uma derrota e estão acéfalos. A sua principal liderança, Flávio Bolsonaro, se encontra fora, retraída. Escolheu não exercer uma liderança parlamentar, pelo menos não presencialmente”, avalia.
Sobre a manifestação convocada pela União Nacional dos Estudantes (UNE) e realizada na Faria Lima nesta terça-feira (17), em repúdio à pressão do mercado financeiro por ajuste fiscal, Mayra Goulart considera que “é uma demonstração de que governos social-democratas são mais abertos e estimulam a sociedade civil com seus diferentes grupos a participar”.
“A gente tem que estar feliz que estamos com um governo que estimula a participação”, avalia. Goulart é bastante crítica à pressão do mercado financeiro, que, segundo ela, está fazendo “uma espécie de sabotagem” contra o governo federal, usando a Bolsa de Valores como arma.
“E o campo progressista, os movimentos estudantis estão reagindo em defesa de posicionamentos [do governo] mais à esquerda”, pontua.
Para ouvir e assistir
O jornal Conexão BdF vai ao ar em duas edições, de segunda a sexta-feira: a primeira às 12h e a segunda às 17h, na Rádio Brasil de Fato, 98.9 FM na Grande São Paulo, com transmissão simultânea também pelo YouTube do Brasil de Fato.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: O fio da tesoura: o ajuste fiscal, os limites do reformismo e a urgência da luta de classes
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Lucas Assumpção de Oliveira
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Enquanto o Congresso Nacional avança a passos largos para aprovar o Projeto de Lei Complementar (PLP 299/2026) (encabeçado pela base governista para endurecer as travas do arcabouço fiscal e comprimir o crescimento real das despesas federais a 2% ao ano), o cenário político exibe uma contradição gritante.
Em meio a uma maratona diplomática internacional que estende a agenda presidencial pela Ásia, o Executivo federal opta pelo silêncio estratégico e adia manifestações diretas sobre o tesauraço orçamentário. Ao mesmo tempo, nos estados, assiste-se ao espetáculo desconectado de celebrações institucionais de gabinete, como os festejos programados na Praça da Matriz, no coração de Porto Alegre.
O abismo entre o ritmo festivo da cúpula partidária e a dureza material da vida da classe trabalhadora evidencia o esgotamento histórico da conciliação de classes. O pacote fiscal em tramitação, longe de ser um mero erro de percurso ou um ajuste técnico neutro, é a expressão imperativa da subordinação do Estado burguês na periferia do capitalismo aos ditames do capital financeiro e das agências de risco.
A anatomia da austeridade: o que diz o PLP e quem realmente paga a conta
Para compreender a gravidade do PLP 299/2026, é preciso ir além da retórica tecnocrática da “estabilidade macroeconômica” alardeada em Brasília. O projeto altera as engrenagens da Lei Complementar nº 200/2023 para impor um travamento severo: em períodos de contenção fiscal, o crescimento real das despesas federais fica engessado a um teto máximo de 2% ao ano. Mais do que isso, o texto restringe compensações de créditos tributários e autoriza manobras de desvinculação orçamentária, blindando o superávit primário exigido pelo rentismo. Na prática, o que se desenha é um mecanismo de asfixia programada.
Enquanto o serviço da dívida pública (que drena centenas de bilhões de reais do orçamento da União para os cofres dos grandes bancos e detentores de títulos) segue inviolável, o Estado retrai sua capacidade de investimento e compromete a previsibilidade dos pisos constitucionais de saúde e educação. Trata-se do clássico estelionato orçamentário: a gestão da ordem burguesa impõe que o governo progressista faça exatamente o oposto de suas promessas de campanha, transformando o orçamento público em um duto de extração de riqueza para alimentar a especulação financeira.
O fetiche do Estado neutro e os limites do reformismo institucional
A aposta recorrente da esquerda institucional na negociação de gabinetes e na correlação de forças parlamentar revela uma incompreensão estrutural sobre a natureza do Estado. Como nos ensina a tradição marxista, o Estado não é um instrumento neutro ou um “espaço vazio” a ser ocupado por qualquer projeto político, mas sim um comitê gestor dos interesses da burguesia, estruturado organicamente para garantir a reprodução ampliada do capital. Tentar administrar a crise econômica na periferia do sistema dentro das amarras da ortodoxia fiscal é aceitar o “consenso passivo” imposto pelos donos do dinheiro.
Na periferia, onde a acumulação se apoia na superexploração do trabalho e na expropriação contínua, governar sem romper com os marcos do capital financeiro significa inevitavelmente gerir a miséria alheia. A ilusão de que a pressão parlamentar isolada ou o debate virtual nas redes sociais conseguirão constranger o bloco no poder ignora a materialidade da luta de classes: o parlamento sob o jugo do Centrão e dos lobbies da Faria Lima não negocia concessões estruturais; ele consagra a derrota dos trabalhadores antes mesmo que a tinta da lei seque.
A fuga institucional e o divórcio com a base
O timing desastroso da tramitação legislativa (empurrada a toque de caixa enquanto o comando do Executivo cumpre agendas internacionais na Turquia e nas Filipinas) expõe a estratégia de blindagem da cúpula. Ao prometer manifestações “apenas na volta”, o poder central afasta-se momentaneamente do desgaste imediato, deixando o conjunto da militância e dos movimentos sociais aturdidos e desarmados.
Enquanto isso, a burocracia partidária nos estados prefere a estetização da vitória eleitoral e o festejo burocrático em praças públicas ao enfrentamento da conjuntura. Essa desconexão paralisante entre o palanque festivo e o massacre cotidiano da classe trabalhadora (que acumula o peso do tesouraço federal e o encarecimento de tarifas urbanas) revela a urgência de resgatarmos a autonomia política de classe.
Conclusão: da ilusão parlamentar à agitação de base nas ruas
A conjuntura de novembro de 2026 nos impõe uma conclusão sem espaço para ilusões reformistas: esperar que a cúpula institucional revogue sua própria obra de austeridade é um erro tático fatal. A correlação de forças desfavorável no Congresso não se inverte com notas de repúdio, petições virtuais ou lives de gabinete. A única força material capaz de fazer contrapeso à chantagem do capital financeiro é a intervenção preventiva, capilarizada e consciente da classe trabalhadora.
É preciso romper com a paralisação institucional, abandonar os festejos vazios e retomar a agitação de base nos locais de trabalho, de estudo e de moradia: em Porto Alegre, no Rio Grande do Sul e em todo o país. A resistência ao arrocho fiscal precisa ser construída nas ruas antes que a austeridade se cristalize como a condenação irrevogável do nosso futuro.
** Este é um artigo de opinião e não necessariamente expressa a linha editorial do Brasil de Fato.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Caso Master: PF entrega a Fachin, nesta quarta, relatórios refeitos sobre ministros após afastamento de delegados por ‘quebra de confiança’
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), ministro Edson Fachin, deve receber nesta quarta-feira (18) os relatórios da Polícia Federal (PF) com menções a ministros da Corte e a parentes deles no caso Banco Master. Os documentos foram refeitos por determinação do comando da PF, depois do afastamento dos delegados que coordenavam as investigações e preparavam a versão original.
A entrega acontece quando a primeira fase da Operação Compliance Zero, que investiga as fraudes do Master e suas conexões, completa um ano. Fachin havia requisitado o material ao diretor-geral da PF, Andrei Rodrigues. Segundo o presidente do STF, o documento deveria conter uma descrição dos fatos e o nome de cada ministro mencionado, para que o caso possa ser julgado pelo plenário da Corte.
Os delegados Wedson Cajé Lopes e Daniel Mostardeiro Cola perderam os cargos de chefia após uma reestruturação da Coordenação de Inquéritos nos Tribunais Superiores (Cinq), setor responsável pelos inquéritos que tramitam no STF. Os dois foram os responsáveis pelos relatórios que identificaram conversas entre o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, fundador do Master, e o ministro Alexandre de Moraes. Na semana passada, o Ministério da Justiça enviou ofício à PF pedindo explicações sobre o afastamento. Na resposta, enviada na sexta-feira (13), Rodrigues alegou quebra de confiança.
“Em razão de critérios de conveniência e oportunidade administrativa, tendo em vista que a dinâmica de fatos recentes demonstrou que houve uma quebra na fundamental relação de confiança mútua que deve existir entre as funções de chefia direta e hierarquicamente relacionadas, optou-se por não se dar prosseguimento ao processo que designava os servidores Daniel Mostardeiro Cola e Wedson Cajé Lopes para as novas funções de confiança criadas”, diz o ofício.
Audiência no Senado
Nesta quarta, às 14h, as comissões de Constituição e Justiça (CCJ) e de Segurança Pública (CSP) do Senado realizam audiência pública conjunta sobre a modificação dos relatórios e o afastamento dos delegados. Os requerimentos foram apresentados pelo senador Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) e aprovados na quarta-feira passada (11). O ministro da Justiça e Segurança Pública, Wellington César Lima e Silva, confirmou presença. Até a noite de terça-feira (17), Rodrigues não havia respondido ao convite.
Primeiro relatório
O primeiro relatório da PF sobre ministros no caso foi produzido por determinação do ministro André Mendonça, então relator das investigações, e abriu uma crise institucional no Supremo. O documento apontou Moraes como interlocutor de 52 mensagens de Vorcaro, que demonstravam apreensão com as investigações e traziam pedidos de interferência. A PF também apontou uma suposta análise e edição, por parte do ministro, de um contrato de R$ 130 milhões firmado entre o Banco Master e o escritório Barci de Moraes, de Viviane Barci, mulher de Moraes.
Mendonça retirou o sigilo do relatório em 1º de setembro, em plena campanha eleitoral, e pediu que o plenário decidisse sobre a investigação do colega. Moraes nega ter dialogado com Vorcaro e afirma que o relatório foi produzido a partir de uma ordem ilegal de Mendonça. A Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) já se manifestou no Supremo pelo arquivamento do documento, sob o argumento de que sua produção foi irregular. Diante da crise, Fachin afastou Mendonça e assumiu a relatoria da petição que trata das suspeitas envolvendo Moraes.
Outros citados
Há citações, em graus diferentes, a pelo menos seis ministros do STF ou a parentes deles, além de referências a ministros do Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ) e do Tribunal Superior do Trabalho (TST).
As ligações de ministros com o caso começaram a vir à tona em abril de 2025. Naquele mês, a colunista Malu Gaspar, d’O Globo, revelou a contratação do escritório da mulher de Moraes pelo Master. Depois, surgiram negócios envolvendo fundos do banco e um resort da família do ministro Dias Toffoli no Paraná, o que levou Toffoli a deixar a relatoria do caso e a se declarar suspeito.
Em setembro deste ano, vieram a público mensagens que citavam o ministro Nunes Marques e que sugeriam suposto favorecimento ao filho dele e ao filho do ministro Luiz Fux. Em relação a Mendonça, foram divulgados um encontro com o banqueiro, confirmado pelo próprio ministro, uma foto com um advogado de Vorcaro e um pedido de investigação sobre possível relação entre o Master e o Instituto Iter, ligado ao ministro. Também foi identificada a contratação, por Vorcaro, de Chiquinho Feitosa, ex-cunhado do ministro Gilmar Mendes.
Todos os ministros e familiares negam irregularidades ou envolvimento com Vorcaro.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/podcast/.title: Sociedade vive ‘pacto da impunidade’ e prova é que Elon Musk está solto, avalia sociólogo Jessé Souza
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/podcast/.author: BdF Entrevista
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/podcast/.text:
Em seu livro “O Pacto da Impunidade” (Editora Record), o sociólogo e escritor Jessé Souza defende que o mundo enfrenta um processo de “brasilianização”, no qual os pilares da cidadania construídos nos últimos séculos são desmantelados em favor de um sistema duplo de justiça. Nesse contexto, os super-ricos conseguem transgredir leis sem qualquer consequência e a distância entre ricos e pobres emula na sociedade contemporânea as dinâmicas históricas de dominação e servidão.
Ao BdF Entrevista, o escritor afirma que a impunidade se consolidou no topo da estrutura social. “Tem um novo nível em que se criou uma impunidade, ou seja, tem uma justiça para os ricos e uma justiça para os pobres”, aponta. “O Brasil tem classes que são senhores e classes que são condenadas a uma escravidão moderna.”
A desconstrução da noção de igualdade também se manifesta nas interações cotidianas por meio de distinções simbólicas que naturalizam a hierarquia de classes. Ao mencionar a teoria de Pierre Bourdieu como referência, Souza explica que o estilo de vida da elite serve para legitimar uma suposta superioridade moral e intelectual frente à classe trabalhadora. “No nível das interações intersubjetivas, do cotidiano, existe uma hierarquia invisível, que é a mais importante. É aquela que vai dizer que esses caras que vão para restaurante francês são um tipo distinto, superior de ser humano do que o trabalhador que vai lá e pega um pratão com batata frita, gordura, bifão e tal, e come animalisticamente porque ele está com fome”, exemplifica.
“Isso vai para todas as dimensões da vida. Como você se veste, como você fala, como você anda, quem você vai querer que seja seu amigo, com quem você vai casar, tudo isso é decidido nessa esfera invisível”, pontua. Essas barreiras invisíveis, destaca o sociólogo, geram uma captura ideológica e fazem com que “uma parte significativa dos trabalhadores hoje se identifique com o opressor”.
Nesse mundo simbólico é que se dá o avanço das grandes corporações de tecnologia, as big techs, e da dominação do mercado financeiro, na direção de privatizar tudo que é público e corroer as dinâmicas democráticas. “São os caras que vão efetivamente destruir a democracia, destruir a esfera pública. Mostra a desconstrução daquilo que é público e que vai passar a ser privatizado pelos ricos”, aponta, ao criticar que o mercado financeiro funciona apenas na base do acúmulo e da especulação e não produz riqueza.
“O que esse pessoal faz é roubar. Esse pessoal não produz um parafuso. É só especular com juro, exigindo isenções fiscais. Retiram todo o dinheiro que poderia mudar a sociedade”, avalia.
Diante de todo esse cenário, Jessé Souza usa o exemplo de Elon Musk, que é considerado por muitos uma referência, mas que não passa “de um completo idiota, imbecil, racista, uma pessoa horrorosa”. Nesse mundo da impunidade, o trilionário é visto como bem-sucedido porque seria mais esperto que os outros. O escritor rebate essa narrativa. “O fato de você ser rico não significa que você seja mais inteligente do que os outros. Pode significar, na maior parte das vezes, que você é o mais inescrupuloso”, define. “Um cara como Elon Musk já devia estar na cadeia há muito tempo, e a chave jogada no mar. [Mark] Zuckerberg idem. Mas eles estão acima da lei”, critica.
Souza também fala do atual cenário político brasileiro, em que o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), reeleito em virada histórica, agora sofre forte pressão do mercado financeiro por um ajuste fiscal. O sociólogo critica o plano, aponta ausência de um projeto político alternativo na esquerda que enfrente o poder econômico e sustenta que é preciso disputar narrativas e conscientizar a população sobre os reais mecanismos de dominação. “A primeira coisa é mostrar ao povo quem é o seu inimigo, dizendo quem rouba: ‘Olha, o seu inimigo ali é a Faria Lima. Esse pessoal que é o ladrão do seu futuro’. Explicar como isso se dá. Você tem que acreditar na inteligência popular. O povo está imbecilizado, mas ele não é imbecil. Se você contar a história para ele, ele recupera a inteligência dele”, aposta.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Annoying Trump and dodging Flock: inside MapQuest’s contrarian comeback
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Andrew Lawrence
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
I am among the legion of former PC desk occupants with warm memories of MapQuest, the Y2K-era travel website that kept millennial drivers on course with sheaves of printed-out directions – a quantum leap over the ungainly glovebox map. But I assumed it had long since gone the way of AIM and Skype, its manual turn-by-turn guidance made obsolete by big tech.
Proof of life came in January 2025, when Donald Trump issued an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America – a change Apple Maps and Google Maps promptly adopted, while MapQuest … did nothing. Not only had it never signed off, MapQuest was reinventing itself as a plucky oppositional hero, the app most likely to uphold your geographical beliefs.
“I think the question that was posed internally was exactly that,” said MapQuest’s general manager, Doug Berger, who took over during the Gulf of America mishigas. “What if we didn’t …?” In a subsequent tweet, the company joked that it was retaining the Gulf of Mexico name “not because of politics but because we haven’t updated our maps in like 15 years and don’t remember how to do it”. The irreverence clearly resonated: MapQuest, which still attracted 35 million monthly website visitors despite having been largely supplanted by more convenient GPS options, saw a roughly 10% jump in traffic over a month. In February 2025, it doubled down, tintroducing a new feature allowing users to pick their own name for the gulf or let the app “surprise me” with options such as Gulf of Gumbo and Gulf of Something.
All of that was just a warmup for the executive order that came this past August, when Trump renamed Lake Ontario as Lake America – and MapQuest declared: “We’re not changing it.” While competitors scrambled to update their maps again, MapQuest said it added more than 2 million mobile users in the span of a week, a surge that temporarily made it the top free navigation app on iOS and Android. Canadians accounted for about half of the new following. “Our stance, while it can be interpreted as political, really is about giving people familiar names,” Berger said. “People who live near Lake Ontario, on either side of the US-Canada border, aren’t going to call it something else.”
MapQuest didn’t have much to lose by playing the contrarian. Spawned from the cartographic services division of printing giant RR Donnelley & Sons, it has spent the past 30 years changing hands: from AOL (which paid $1.1bn for it in 1999) to Verizon (which acquired AOL for $4.4bn in 2015) before the digital ad firm System1 snapped it up for an undisclosed but surely discounted sum in 2019.
Now a Los Angeles-based operation of about 40 people, MapQuest makes money selling banner ads and premium subscriptions instead of data. It is also licensing tools built around user engagement that other companies can put to their own mapping purposes.
The app user experience will be familiar to anyone who navigates with Apple Maps, Google Maps or Waze, just with more obvious pixeling. That’s all by design that leans hard into nostalgia, with interchangeable personal location markers called “questies” that evoke the 32-bit video game characters of yore. Berger is at pains to point out that questies are handcrafted. “Trust me, it would be very easy to create them with AI,” he said.
Since the Lake Ontario executive order, requests for new features have poured in from social media, email and even snail mail. Berger welcomes the feedback so readily that MapQuest created an online suggestion box for people to propose ideas and put them up for a vote. That’s how it wound up adding a polling places tool, which came in especially handy earlier this month. “There’s a button right here that says ‘vote’,” Berger demonstrates on our video call. “When you tap it, it shows a little unicorn in red, white and blue and tells you exactly where to go for early voting, ballot drop-off and on election day.”
But that’s not what had me booting up MapQuest again for the first time since the iPhone consigned it to the internet’s suspended animation wing alongside Go.com and LiveJournal.
Dodging Flock in Atlanta
Last month, as part of a Halloween-themed app update, MapQuest introduced a user-requested feature for tracking surveillance cameras on the road. Prominent in the new MapQuest layer are Flock cameras, the AI-driven, solar-powered devices that capture images of passing vehicles, logging license plates and other identifying details, often without drivers’ knowledge. The cameras are represented by blinking red eyes that beam red cones in the direction their lenses face. The real-life implications are considerably less cartoonish.
Over the past five years, Flock license-plate readers have grown into a nationwide network of 120,000 cameras spanning more than 6,000 communities, according to the company. They turn passing cars into searchable records for law enforcement agencies – and potentially others with network access – of who was where and when. Their spread has drawn criticism from civil-liberties groups concerned about the surveillance of non-suspects: research from Electronic Frontier Foundation shows that less than 1% of vehicles scanned with automatic license plate readers, or ALPRs, are ever connected with a public safety issue or crime.
Some residents are beginning to challenge their use in communities, too. James Hayes, a community activist, frames mass surveillance as a fourth amendment issue – that it’s tantamount to unlawful search. Two years ago, he says police showed up at his house unannounced at 1am, sniffing around for a car involved in a chase. “They didn’t have the plate on the car, but they had a description through the cameras,” Hayes said. “They had no arrest warrant, no anything.”
Metro Atlanta, where I live, isn’t just where Flock Safety is headquartered. It’s a humming doomsday laboratory for surveillance, with more cameras per capita than any other city in the US and perhaps any city in the world outside China, many of them ALPRs. I never really stopped to consider this while sitting in Atlanta’s notoriously bad traffic, trying my best not to cuss out other drivers and city planners in front of my young sons. (We all fall down.) But then I spent a week using Mapquest.
My sons watched gleefully as our rainbow unicorn questie inched along the road and dissolved into laughter whenever the British grandma-voiced navigator chimed in with our next move, sounding like a Speak & Spell that had been left to drown in the Thames. But what really held their attention, and mine, were the eyes. They were everywhere – bracketing our main routes to and from home, all along the highway, boring in on the road to grandma’s house. “I feel like we could break a record for the most cameras ever seen on MapQuest in history!” my oldest said when 17 eyeballs dotted the screen on a morning school run earlier this month.
Tapping an eye in the app lets you see the type of camera, its location coordinates and the direction it’s facing. I imagine it won’t be long before there’s a feature that lets you flag a camera the app missed, like the one just yards from my kid’s school. (Could be another one for the suggestion box.) The data is drawn from OpenStreetMap, a cartographical Wikipedia of sorts that has taken to mapping surveillance cameras, which include Flock’s hardware as well as machines from Motorola Solutions, spun off from the people who gave the world the brick cell phone; and Axon Enterprises, which has experimented with using AI to marry police body cameras with facial recognition tech. “Flock has given people a name to put around them,” said Chris Fleming, a UK-based OpenStreetMap volunteer, about the recent US backlash to surveillance. “In the UK you don’t associate with a company or anything like that.”
He continued: “Personally, I think it’s important to know how prevalent these are, because if we don’t know that they exist how can we debate about what level of surveillance is taking place, what is appropriate and who has access to it? It seems that using these cameras is easier than getting a warrant for a phone, and that’s wrong to me.”
Hayes, the activist, lives just outside the Atlanta metro perimeter in Cherokee county. Last month, the county’s five-member commission board considered a 10-year, $37.3m contract with Axon to become Cherokee law enforcement’s one-stop shop for body cameras, in-car cameras, drones and license-plate readers. Over Halloween weekend, local watchdog groups ran a “trick or treat” email campaign urging concerned residents to contact commissioners before the vote. At the same time, a viral DeFlock America campaign urged Halloween revelers nationwide to cover or disable Flock cameras and the like, at their own considerable legal risk. On 3 November, while people were at the polls on election day, the Cherokee county commissioners voted unanimously to approve the measure – one in a number of worrying deals made between private surveillance firms and local governments across the country.
The timing of the Cherokee county decision, however routine – the commissioners meet on the first and third Tuesday of each month – still left a bad taste. “It’s dirty, so dirty,” said Hayes, adding that it won’t be much longer before surveillance cameras become a major ballot issue. “The datacenter thing was big this past midterm, but Flock is related to it. The more datacenters, the more Flock. I’ve talked to a lot of people about this – Republican, Democrat. Nobody’s good with this.”
Cherokee county still trails in ALPR investment behind my metro Atlanta home jurisdiction. Last September, Dekalb county commissioners signed off on the nation’s largest documented surveillance contract with Flock, $18.9m over 10 years, and followed that up last week by rejecting a proposal for a civilian oversight committee to stand sentry for rights abuses. Troublingly, Flock video is shared among thousands of law enforcement agencies, giving rise to a surveillance network that makes it possible for them to build cases on protestors, abortion seekers, immigrants and others even as they cross in and out of jurisdiction.
All that is to say: you could see why someone might want to know where the Flock cameras and other ALPRs are and potentially even steer clear while they still can.
Is MapQuest here to stay?
I tend to approach navigation apps like a gameshow host, calling on Apple, Google or the in-car GPS based on which one pipes up first. But after a week with MapQuest, I found it difficult to go back to the others without feeling like something was missing – those eyeballs. Surveillance state aside, it was as if I was picking up where I left off, back when MapQuest was a companion to young drivers just starting out on the road, its printouts taking pride of place on the dashboard and front seat.
These days MapQuest integrates easily enough into the CarPlay setup, and while its maps lack the environmental textures Apple and Google offer, that matters less to me than making time. Like many Atlanta locals who yearn for light rail expansion, I spend a distressingly large chunk of my life behind the wheel, ferrying my sons to school (an hour-long commute each way, at best), extracurricular activities and a never-ending slate of playdates. Nothing irks my soul quite like the sight of red congestion lines and an ETA that climbs with every idle moment.
As a driving aide, MapQuest is as competent as any – even as it still lacks full operating system integration and freezes up on the dashboard at times. It’s also more optimistic than I would prefer. Apple tends to provide a more generous ETA, giving me the satisfaction of “beating” it. My MapQuest routes, though, often started with earlier ETAs that gradually ticked upward as the reality of gridlock set in. One afternoon school run lasted nearly 20 minutes longer until our “quest” was complete, our destination rendered on an exaggerated location pin with a big “B”, as in point B.
Sometimes on interstate journeys, which account for most of my driving these days, the app would encourage me to ramp-hop (exit and re-enter the main highway) to avoid bottlenecks. Other times, it would send me down roads where I knew more traffic miseries awaited, leaving me to wonder if I was better off going my own way. Maybe the paid versions are better, but who was I to turn down the free version, especially with MapQuest temporarily suspending ads to attract new users?
Waze showed years ago that there was space on the home screen for one more GPS app – that is, before Google swallowed it up. MapQuest would seem to have a fair shot at repositioning itself in the very lane it established, if not for its routing capabilities than for its retro stylings and cheeky contrarianism.
The politics of geography are easy enough to take for granted until a border is disputed or a landmark name is contested. I remember making the drive a few years ago to the big army base in north-west Georgia, entering through a distant back gate and doing a double take when signs for Fort Benning read Fort Moore instead. It was one of nine army bases renamed under the Biden administration to remove references to confederate figures – legislation that the Trump administration would later roll back.
The switch-around had Berger thinking about more alternate routes MapQuest can take: “Now you have my head spinning about feature requests, the concept of synonyms for familiar places,” he said. “That would be interesting.”

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Heavy rain and snow predicted in California as ‘atmospheric river’ moves across state
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Lois Beckett
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Heavy rain or snowfall is predicted across California this week, as an “atmospheric river” dumps precipitation across the state.
Flood advisories have been issued for much of the Bay Area, according to the National Weather Service (NWS), while southern California may see coastal flooding, heavy surf, wave damage to coastal piers and parking lots, and beach sand erosion.
Areas of the state still recovering from recent wildfires are at risk for flash flooding, with specific warnings issued for “burn scar” areas including in Big Sur and the Napa valley.
The heaviest of the rainfall is expected north-east of San Francisco, from Santa Rosa to Chico and Redding in the state’s Central valley, and in the southern part of the Bay Area, along coastal mountain ranges from Santa Cruz to San Jose and Palo Alto, according to the NWS.
“Travel delays, localized flooding and hazardous conditions are possible, especially along the coast and on mountain pass roads,” Accuweather warned in an online forecast.
Atmospheric rivers, massive currents of water vapor that can carry as much or even more water than an actual river, have been growing stronger and deadlier in recent years. In the relatively dry western US, atmospheric rivers provide both essential precipitation and flood risk.
In southern California, the NWS predicted 1-3in of rain in many areas, with 3-5in in some mountain and foothill areas, and a 20% chance of thunderstorms on Wednesday and Thursday. As much as a foot of snow was expected in higher-elevation areas above 6,000ft. There was a high risk of “significant road flooding” and a moderate risk for rockslides and mudslides, the NWS said.
The risk of coastal wave damage was expected to peak in southern California on Thursday, with additional risks expected next week, with seasonal high tides overlapping with storm risks during Thanksgiving week.
Waterspouts were spotted over the San Francisco Bay earlier this week, and the NWS flagged the risk of additional waterspouts over the ocean east of San Francisco on Wednesday.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.author: Fleur Hargreaves
https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.text:
Tim Hortons app sending user data to Israeli cybertech company, advocacy group confirms
The Tim Hortons app has been sharing sensitive user data with Forter, an Israeli cybertech company founded by alumni of the Israeli military's infamous intelligence Unit 8200, Canadians for Justice and Peace in the Middle East (CJPME) has confirmed.
An investigation by the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC) published last week found that the coffee chain app sends data to third-party companies overseas as soon as the app is launched.
Joel Reardon, an associate professor in the department of computer science at the University of Calgary who scanned the app's network traffic with his team, said the third party built into the app receives enough information to create a digital fingerprint of each device that can be identified later.
Some of the data includes the device's name and unique identifier, details of the device's camera and sensors, and the names of Wi-Fi routers nearby, which can be used to determine the user's location.
"This was beyond the pale," Reardon told the CBC.
Celeste Rollason, an independent analyst, told the CBC that the third party brands itself as a fraud protection service, but the amount of data collected "seems quite excessive" for simply purchasing a cup of coffee.
In its published investigation, CBC did not identify the third party or its location, saying that "accountability rests with the app developer".

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.title: Xi Jinping rallies against protectionism as he welcomes Trump to Apec summit
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.author: Rebecca Bailey in Shenzhen
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text:
China’s Xi Jinping rallied Asia-Pacific nations against trade protectionism on Wednesday morning before heading to the airport to welcome Donald Trump, whose administration has just further restricted advanced chip exports, with a rare hug.
The Chinese president spent Wednesday’s opening day of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit switching lanes between multilateralist and big-power politics, culminating in a group photo where he stood central among fellow leaders. He was flanked by Trump and Vladimir Putin – whose blockbuster trilateral meeting will dominate Thursday’s proceedings as the summit gets to its business end.
Having all delegates in the photograph was a tightrope feat in itself, with potential Canadian and Australian refusals to stand with Putin over the war in Ukraine shelved out of respect for the host.
The Russian president did not arrive in a conciliatory mood, using his speech at the summit to call western powers “former hegemons”, state that Europe was in “a humiliating decline” and proclaim that sanctions no longer worked.
However, toasting his varied visitors at a welcoming banquet, Xi invoked “the grand plan for Asia-Pacific cooperation”. Thursday would see those gathered “discuss measures to expand mutual openness, explore pathways for innovation-driven growth, [and] broaden opportunities for pragmatic cooperation in various fields,” he said.
Openness was the main theme of his keynote address, presenting China as a stalwart of free trade and technological innovation.
“We find ourselves in a changing and turbulent world. Global growth lacks momentum, and unilateralism and protectionism are rampant,” he told the audience of business executives and Apec leaders. “We should firmly safeguard the WTO-centred, rules-based multilateral trading system, support free and open trade and investment, and keep global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded.”
Critics of Beijing have long accused it of hypocrisy on this point, noting the obstacles many foreign businesses face entering China’s vast market. But Xi’s messaging on open trade was echoed by other leaders who took to the stage after him, including South Korea’s Lee Jae Myung and Malaysia’s Anwar Ibrahim.
Putin meanwhile took aim at sanctions, claiming they had “largely run their course, having lost much of their intimidating power”.
That prompted a rebuttal from Canada’s Mark Carney, who told reporters Putin was “lying”. “Sanctions are very real and they’re going to continue to increase as long as this war goes on,” he said.
When Xi met Putin though, he called for closer political and military ties between Russia and China, in a continued demonstration of a tight relationship that has only deepened since Moscow invaded Ukraine in 2022.
Before Putin’s arrival in China, Russia sent nuclear-capable bombers to an airport in Vietnam, in a rare deployment interpreted as a pointed show of Moscow’s ability to project strength in the region despite being embroiled in the Ukraine war. Russian military aircraft had spooked air forces in both Taiwan and Japan on Tuesday as they flew past them while routeing south from Russia’s Far East region.
It was Xi’s reception of Trump, complete with an embrace, that broke with convention; the reception on the airport tarmac is believed to be the first by a Chinese leader in decades, although during Xi’s state visit to Washington in September, Trump had also taken the unusual step of greeting Xi on the tarmac.
Xi travelled to the airport despite the US announcing on Monday new interim rules to further restrict Beijing’s access to advanced semiconductors. That followed an awkward week of news after the chief executive of US chipmaker Nvidia resigned over an affair, reportedly with a woman some US officials suspect of being a Chinese spy.
Beijing’s “overriding objective” was “extending the fragile calm in the US-China relationship for as long as possible”, Ryan Hass, from the Brookings thinktank, told the AFP news agency. “[The reception] set a positive tone for Trump’s visit, marking a contrast from the swirl of news around the Jensen Huang scandal that preceded Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen.”
The state news agency Xinhua said Xi had noted “China is a nation with a tradition of courtesy that values reciprocating goodwill”, after Trump met Xi at the airport when he visited the US.
Trump and Xi will hold a bilateral meeting as well as talks with Putin on Thursday. On Wednesday, the Associated Press reported that Trump had said he and Putin would meet separately as well, citing an anonymous US official.
These meetings will dominate the day’s schedule and the news cycle, a fact that has at times seemed to bother China.
“The Chinese actually tried to have this meeting not happen … They kind of got jammed into it. Then, when it was going to happen, they just wanted statements,” the former US national security adviser Jake Sullivan said on The Rest is Politics podcast. “They are going to be deeply uncomfortable throughout this because this does not fit their narrative of a country that believes in multi-alignment, the United Nations, everyone around the table.”
Shen Weizhong, a former policy planner with China’s foreign ministry who now works for the Global Governance Institution, a Beijing-based thinktank, told the Guardian he would not be surprised if Sullivan was right and that China was “torn”.
“On the one hand, it will steal the spotlight. The outcome is not clear and there are no immediate deliverables,” he said. “But on the other side, it will help China’s image – it is the only facilitator who could do this, and if it can ease tensions on the world stage, that will be good.” He said he suspected enthusiasm from both Putin and Trump for the meeting could have ultimately swayed Beijing.
China is actively opposing the framing of the meetings as a new Yalta, the 1945 meeting between Stalin, Churchill and Roosevelt that in effect carved up postwar Europe. “The global south will not like having a Yalta 2.0, and China is always taking the smaller countries into consideration,” said Shen.
Also potentially on Thursday’s agenda is an Apec joint statement that, an official told Reuters, delegates were “working around the clock” to find agreement on. “China as host will want something,” said Shen, though even Beijing is “not as obsessed with such deliverables” these days.

https://apache.be/2026/11/03/hoe-zaak-re.title: Hoe de zaak-Reynders ons democratisch bestel op de proef stelt
https://apache.be/2026/11/03/hoe-zaak-re.author: Tom Cochez
https://apache.be/2026/11/03/hoe-zaak-re.text:
Het fraudeonderzoek naar Didier Reynders heeft alles in zich om uit te groeien tot een Belgisch politiek schandaal zonder weerga. Nieuwe documenten tonen hoe verschillende dossiers waarover de schaduw van Reynders hangt, ons democratisch bestel ondermijnen. Om welke dossiers gaat het ook al weer? En wie dreigt meegesleept te worden?
Recent gelekte versleutelde whatsappberichten tussen Didier Reynders, een (toenmalige) topman van de Belgische Staatsveiligheid én een edelman die spioneert voor de Russen en de Chinezen tillen het gerechtelijk onderzoek naar witwas en fraude tegen de gevallen toppoliticus naar een ander niveau.
Ze geven aan dat Reynders niet enkel zichzelf zou hebben verrijkt, maar bevatten ook ernstige aanwijzingen dat een van Belgiës machtigste politici in de afgelopen decennia zeer nauw samenwerkte met vijandige buitenlandse mogendheden.
Reynders zou niet enkel zichzelf hebben verrijkt. Er zijn ook aanwijzingen dat hij zeer nauw samenwerkte met vijandige buitenlandse mogendheden
De mogelijke gevolgen daarvan zijn verregaand. Niet enkel voor de gewezen liberale topman zelf en voor zijn directe entourage, maar mogelijk ook voor andere politieke partijen waarmee Reynders decennialang direct of indirect zaakjes regelde.
Het hoeft dan ook geen betoog dat het onderzoek kreunt onder gigantische druk. De belangen zijn groot en bij een eventuele val dreigt Reynders anderen met zich mee te sleuren. Een overzicht van wat er op het spel staat.
Video-interview met Nicolas Ullens
In 2019 sprak Apache uitgebreid met voormalig inspecteur van de Belgische staatsveiligheid Nicolas Ullens. Bij die gelegenheid maakten we ook beelden van zijn getuigenis. We beslisten toen om de beelden niet te gebruiken en enkel te schrijven over zaken die we na verder onderzoek konden aantonen en hardmaken. Vandaag liggen de kaarten anders.
Didier Reynders en zijn eeuwige rechterhand Jean-Claude Fontinoy zijn in verdenking gesteld voor witwaspraktijken, en gelekte whatsappberichten tonen dat Didier Reynders zijn netwerk gebruikte om de voormalige inspecteur van staatsveiligheid die op kwalijke dossiers rond Reynders en Fontinoy stuitte, het werken onmogelijk te maken.
Daarom stofferen we dit overzicht met korte fragmenten uit het interview van 2019 wanneer die meer duiding geven bij de beschreven feiten.
Hoe kwam Didier Reynders in beeld bij het gerecht?
In 2022 meldde de Nationale Loterij dat Didier Reynders jarenlang spelen van de Nationale Loterij zou hebben gebruikt om zwart geld wit te wassen. De speurders focussen op ruim 1 miljoen euro aan verdachte transacties. Het gaat grotendeels – voor ongeveer 836.000 euro – over cashgeld dat Reynders gespreid over vele jaren stortte op een bankrekening van ING en over ruim 200.000 euro voor kansspelen bij de Nationale Loterij.
Moest ING dergelijke verdachte transacties niet aangeven?
Zeker en vast. Hoewel de stortingen al jarenlang aan de gang waren, meldde de bank de verdachte stortingen pas in 2023 aan de Cel voor Financiële Informatieverwerking, betere bekend als de antiwitwascel. Onderzoek van de Nationale Bank en de Centrale Dienst voor de Bestrijding van Corruptie geeft aan dat de bank effectief medeplichtig was aan witwas. Het parket sloot afgelopen voorjaar een minnelijke schikking af met ING. De bank betaalde 1,6 miljoen euro – het maximumbedrag om betrokkenheid bij witwassen te sanctioneren – om een rechtszaak te vermijden.
Hoewel de stortingen al jarenlang aan de gang waren, meldde ING de verdachte stortingen pas in 2023 aan de Cel voor Financiële Informatieverwerking
Vorig jaar werd de ex-politicus officieel in verdenking gesteld, enkele maanden gebeurde hetzelfde met zijn rechterhand en een bevriende antiquair
Werd Didier Reynders intussen in verdenking gesteld?
Het voormalige kopstuk van de MR werd een jaar terug – op 16 oktober 2025 – officieel in verdenking gesteld. Vier maanden later gebeurde hetzelfde met Jean-Claude Fontinoy en Olivier Theunissen.
Fontinoy was decennialang de rechterhand van Didier Reynders en kreeg in die rol allerlei cruciale posities toegemeten. Vooral binnen de Regie der Gebouwen die het overheidspatrimonium beheert en bij de NMBS zat Fontinoy op de juiste plek om grote vastgoeddeals met overheidsgebouwen en terreinen van de NMBS te overzien.
Olivier Theunissen zou als antiquair een sleutelrol spelen bij het witwassen van geld via antiek en kunst. Fontinoy was jarenlang kind aan huis in de antiekzaak van Theunissen en zou er op zeer geregelde basis antiek hebben gekocht met cashgeld. Er volgden huiszoekingen bij zowel Theunissen als Fontinoy. Eerder getuigden verschillende bronnen aan Apache dat de woning van Fontinoy propvol antiek staat waarbij “alles te koop is” voor bezoekers.
Maar het onderzoek gaat verder dan enkel witwas via spelen van de Nationale Loterij, cashstortingen en witwas via antiek en kunst?
Waar de speurders exact naar kijken is onduidelijk. Wel zeker is dat ze de hand wisten te leggen op de eerder vermelde whatsappberichtjes tussen Reynders, een (toenmalige) topman van de Belgische Staatsveiligheid en een edelman die spioneert voor de Russen en de Chinezen.
Waarom zijn die belangrijk?
Omdat ze erop wijzen dat Reynders mogelijk decennialang zeer nauw samenwerkte met vijandige buitenlandse mogendheden.
Verschillende bronnen vertelden aan Apache dat de woning van Fontinoy propvol antiek staat waarbij 'alles te koop is' voor bezoekers
Waarom wijzen ze in die richting?
Daarvoor moeten we terug naar verklaringen die Nicola Ullens al in 2019 aflegde. Ullens was inspecteur van 2007 tot 2018. In essentie komen zijn verklaringen erop neer dat Didier Reynders verschillende onderzoeken die binnen de Belgische Staatsveiligheid liepen in de kiem smoorde.
Het gaat om onderzoeken die gebeurden zowel binnen de afdeling economische contraspionage als binnen de afdelingen Rusland en China, waarin Reynders en zijn rechterhand Fontinoy opdoken. Meer informatie over de concrete dossiers volgt verderop.
Reynders creëerde een nieuwe directeursfunctie bij staatsveiligheid en dropte daar een voormalige kabinetsmedewerker
Reynders creëerde een nieuwe functie – een soort derde directeur – binnen de staatsveiligheid en plaatste er zijn voormalige kabinetsmedewerker Hugues Brulin. Een andere vertrouweling van Reynders kwam aan het hoofd te staan van de eerder genoemde afdelingen waar het bezwarend materiaal rond Reynders circuleerde.
Finaal werd de dienst economische contraspionage opgedoekt. Nicolas Ullens werd het werken onmogelijk gemaakt en stapte op.
En hij getuigde over de mistoestanden?
Ullens klopte eerst, nog als dienstdoend inspecteur, aan bij het Comité I – dat toeziet op het correct functioneren van de inlichtingendiensten – om de mistoestanden aan te kaarten. Toen hij na twee bezoeken een derde keer terugkwam om de verslagen van zijn getuigenissen te ondertekenen, zou er een verregaande intimidatiepoging zijn geweest.
“Tot mijn grote verbazing zei Frank Franceus (chef enquêtedienst van het Comité I en ex-kabinetschef van Geert Bourgeois, red.) me dat het ondertekenen van de verslagen van mijn getuigenis levensgevaarlijk zou zijn”, zei Nicolas Ullens daarover indertijd aan Apache.
“Franceus zei dat ik vier kinderen had en dat het ook voor hen gevaarlijk zou zijn. Net als voor mijn vrouw. Ik was in shock. Die nacht heb ik verschillende brieven geschreven aan een aantal naaste vrienden, met de vraag ze openbaar te maken mocht me iets overkomen.”
Nicolas Ullens diende een klacht in bij het federaal parket wegens doodsbedreigingen door de chef enquêtedienst van het Comité I
Nam Ullens nog andere initiatieven?
Hij diende een klacht in bij het federaal parket wegens doodsbedreigingen door de chef enquêtedienst van het Comité I en wegens belaging binnen de staatsveiligheid door vertrouwelingen van Didier Reynders. Die klacht liep in 2021 af met een sisser.
Ook een ander opsporingsonderzoek tegen onder meer Jean-Claude Fontinoy bij het Brussels parket werd in oktober 2019 geseponeerd. Dat gebeurde vijf dagen voor Reynders als toenmalig kandidaat EU-commissaris voor Justitie en de Rechtstaat, door het Europees Parlement op de rooster zou worden gelegd en hij een hangend opsporingsonderzoek kon missen als kiespijn.
Samen met de seponering leken de getuigenissen van Nicolas Ullens een stille dood te sterven. Didier Reynders en Jean-Claude Fontinoy konden herademen. Daar alludeerde Hugues Brulin duidelijk op in zijn whatsappconversatie met Didier Reynders:
“Goed Nieuws .. Een single malt op uw gezondheid mijnheer de minister en ter uwer beschikking voor de tegenaanval als u dat opportuun acht … Met respect. Hugues”, klonk het op 27 september, de dag van de seponering.
“Veel dank Hughues, ook voor de vriendschappelijke steun deze voorbije dagen, Didier”, appte Reynders terug.
Het is maar een van de berichten die aangeven hoe nauw Reynders – op dat moment nog Belgisch minister – rechtstreeks samenwerkte met een topman bij de Belgische staatsveiligheid.
Tot wanneer stuurden Brulin en Reynders berichtjes naar elkaar?
De gerechtelijke politie heeft minstens berichten onderschept tot april 2023. In de laatste berichten bespreken Brulin en Reynders de dood van Myriam Ullens, de stiefmoeder van Nicolas Ullens die door Nicolas Ullens zelf werd doodgeschoten.
Het sterk gemediatiseerde assisenproces daarover hervat woensdag (4/11). Brulin en Reynders tonen zich opgelucht dat Nicolas Ullens nu definitief van het toneel zal verdwijnen. “Il nous aura quand même fait souffrir l’animal”, schrijft Brulin aan Reynders: “Hij heeft ons erg doen afzien, de smeerlap”.
De mannetjes van Reynders moesten het Nicolas Ullens (en anderen binnen de staatsveiligheid) onmogelijk maken om verder onderzoek te doen in concrete dossiers die richting Reynders of Fontinoy wezen. Over welke dossiers gaat het?
Wellicht het belangrijkste dossier waar Nicolas Ullens als inspecteur bij de staatsveiligheid tegenaan liep, is Kazachgate. België keurde in 2011 versneld de fameuze afkoopwet goed. Die wet liet toe dat verdachten hun proces konden afkopen. Naast een aantal grote diamantprocessen kwam daarbij vooral de steenrijke, in België residerende Oezbeekse oligarch (die vaak onterecht als Kazach wordt omschreven) Patokh Chodiev in beeld. Als een van de eersten maakte hij gebruik van de afkoopwet.
Chodiev betaalde amper een half miljoen euro om een rechtszaak te vermijden over de fameuze Tractebel-smeergeldaffaire. Die draaide rond pogingen van het bedrijf Tractebel om een concessie te verkrijgen voor een gaspijpleiding in Kazachstan. Chodiev zou zijn commissies gebruikt hebben als smeergeld voor politici om de deal te beklinken.
Kazachgate was wellicht het belangrijkste dossier waar Nicolas Ullens als inspecteur bij de staatsveiligheid tegenaan liep.
