https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.title: Hakeem Jeffries on brink of House history as he tells Democrats to ‘fight Maga, not each other’ – US politics live
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.author: Shrai Popat (now); Marina Dunbar and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.text:
Jeffries on brink of House history as he tells Democrats to 'fight Maga extremism, not each other'
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Hakeem Jeffries said it is the job of Democratic lawmakers to “fight Maga extremism” as he stood on the brink of becoming the first ever Black house speaker.
Democrats on Wednesday resoundingly nominated Jeffries to serve as speaker of the House when the new Congress is sworn in next year.
A New York congressman who has served as the Democratic minority leader since 2023, Jeffries is set to become one of Donald Trump’s most prominent opponents for the final two years of his presidency, when Democrats will control both the Senate and House of Representatives and are expected to undertake aggressive efforts to check his powers.
After his nomination was secured during closed-door voting, 251-11, ahead of a full House vote, Jeffries promised to take on the Trump administration’s Maga approach to governing the US. “Our job is to fight Maga extremism, not each other,” he said, “and to get big things done for the American people.”
Democrats nominated Jeffries despite concerns from some progressives that he represents a politically risky status quo for a party that is looking to capitalize on a surprisingly good performance in the midterms, where voters swept them back into power in the House and Senate with significant majorities.
He would become the first Democratic House speaker since Nancy Pelosi, who will retire from Congress at the end of this year.
Meanwhile today, president Trump has left China after hailing his trilateral meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, saying the three leaders were “really making history”. Trump said the US, Russia and China, the world’s largest nuclear powers, were “uniquely positioned” to discuss reducing their nuclear stockpiles.
You can follow the latest from Apec in our live blog here:
In other developments:
- During a fiery House hearing, Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, defended his decision to take a government plane to attend a college football game, while thousands of flights had been cancelled and the airspace closed during the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) nationwide grounding over the weekend. “You want to bring up the fact that I took my family and my great nieces to an [Lousiana State University] game that was scheduled for weeks prior because I wanted to be a good uncle,” Mullin said, following questions from Congressman Bennie Thompson, the homeland security committee’s top Democrat.
- Elon Musk called his midterm political spending “foolish.” After pouring nearly half a billion dollars into the election, in a Wednesday conversation with The New York Times’s DealBook Summit, Musk said: “If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money.”
- US Transportation secretary Sean Duffy blamed contractor L3Harris for last week’s nationwide ground stop. As legislators press for more answers on last week’s outage that caused thousands of flights to be halted, Duffy has continued finger-pointing, telling digital media outlet 2WAY on Wednesday that L3Harris, the aerospace and defense company whose router malfunctioned during an update, did not identify the issue “quick enough.”
- Trump’s contentious triumphal arch continues to face setbacks. A federal judge extended the construction ban for the arch, slated for the Memorial Circle in Washington DC. A group of veterans and members of the Kennedy family members have blasted the project as disrespectful to those interred at the Arlington national cemetery.
Correction: an earlier version of this post said Jeffries would serve as speaker of the Senate, rather than the House .

https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.title: The Guardian view on the international court of justice: the ruling against Myanmar should be only the start for the Rohingya | Editorial
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.author: Editorial
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.text:
The finding of the world’s highest court that Myanmar committed genocide is a landmark in international law. But at the heart of this case are “real people, real stories and a real group of human beings”, as Dawda Jallow, the Gambian justice minister, stressed in bringing it. This was one test of how the world has responded to the persecution of the mostly Muslim Rohingya minority in Rakhine state. The international community’s response to the majority judgment will be another.
This is the first time that the international court of justice (ICJ) has found a state guilty of genocide. Around 10,000 Rohingya were killed in the 2016-17 campaign by Myanmar’s military, in many cases gunned down as they fled, with another 700,000 escaping to Bangladesh. The judges found that the aim was to destroy “a substantial part” of the Rohingya people, with the murder of infants, widespread sexual violence and razing of villages not accounted for simply by military objectives.
The bar is high; in 2007, the ICJ found Serbia responsible for failing to prevent genocide in Srebrenica in 1995, but not for directly committing it. Genocidal intent must be the “only reasonable inference” from a pattern of conduct. Legal scholars have pointed out that that need not preclude its coexistence with other aims. The court has not changed the standard, but shown how it can be applied.
Yet even before the ruling, the US ambassador to the UN, Mike Waltz, had accused Navi Pillay, this year’s Nobel peace laureate, of intending to lower the legal threshold so that it could be “weaponised against American and allied soldiers”. There is grave concern that the US will impose sanctions on Ms Pillay and fellow judges, as it has on the international criminal court, which holds individuals rather than states accountable. Israel is currently before the ICJ on genocide charges, and the relevance of Thursday’s finding to Gaza is obvious.
But this case is first and foremost important as an attempt to bring some measure of justice for the Rohingya, whose suffering began decades ago and continues. Survivors in refugee camps greeted the findings with applause as they watched the session on Thursday. The UN warned in August that human rights in Myanmar had hit a new low, citing the “ever-worsening brutal abuse” of members of the minority. The military has forcibly conscripted those it despises in the civil war – fuelling atrocities against them by one of the junta’s adversaries, the Arakan army. Those who have found safety abroad also face returning to danger. India has repatriated Rohingya refugees, and there are growing concerns that Malaysia may send back many more, following a visit by Min Aung Hlaing, the leader of Myanmar’s junta.
Myanmar now has two years to set out plans for full restitution, including the safe and voluntary return home that survivors still seek. If and when it fails, the court will take up the issue. But governments must play their part. The UK’s expulsion of Myanmar’s military attache was a small but welcome step. It must do much more to step up the pressure on the junta and other parties in Myanmar to ensure the safety of the Rohingya, and urge other governments to do likewise. States that believe in international law must do all they can to back this ruling and ensure that it has real consequences, both to protect the Rohingya and to show support for the court itself.

https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.title: The Guardian view on Grand Theft Auto VI: a game that makes players think twice | Editorial
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.author: Editorial
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.text:
The biggest global cultural event of the year may not be something that millions of people watch together but somewhere that millions of people venture separately. In the video game Grand Theft Auto VI, players inhabit a fictionalised America through the eyes of two lovers turned cons in a rags-to-riches crime epic. On Thursday, when the game was released, workers called in sick and students skipped lectures to play at home. Such is GTA VI’s appeal that it is forecast to rake in billions of dollars within months.
The game has been billed as a satire of American capitalism, and it is undoubtedly a landmark in interactive storytelling and art. The commercial success of its previous titles has rivalled that of Hollywood blockbusters. Playing GTA VI, as the Guardian’s video games editor observes, is like losing yourself in a doorstop novel, with hours of solitary immersion in a vividly conjured place – not a facsimile of modern Miami, but an interpretation, almost the size of Manchester, rendered with astonishing precision by the artists who designed, wrote, coded and soundtracked its virtual world.
The video game portrays a country awash with vice and hypocrisy, where the American dream is alive and well – provided you trample on someone else to achieve it. There is no way to win if you play by the rules. In the game’s main hub, Vice City, lawyers and police are scarcely more honest than drug dealers and thieves, while conspiracy theorists, crypto scammers and narcissistic influencers abound. But it would be wrong to think that the game simply revels in corruption. By giving its two main characters, Jason and Lucia, histories and vulnerabilities, the game asks players to sympathise with people who are both society’s victims and its perpetrators.
The GTA series has long faced criticism for its violence and casual misogyny, treating women as sex objects or punchlines. GTA VI marks a shift. Lucia, its first female lead, confronts the sexism around her, while other women emerge as characters in their own right. Even the violence, reviews suggest, feels less gratuitous. The game portrays a Trumpian America where wealth, spectacle and criminality blend together. But its satire no longer relies quite so heavily on making women its targets.
Why is one of the most culturally important depictions of the US a fantasy in which the American dream can be pursued most freely by breaking the law? This is a question that hangs over GTA VI. It was created by a team of 5,000 people, many of whom are based outside the US (Rockstar, the company behind the game, is headquartered in Scotland). This is an America created largely by outsiders. But then, as one of Rockstar’s lead developers Rob Nelson said: “We’re all outsiders to this version of America.”
Mr Nelson thinks that the game’s real innovation may not be the scale of the world that Rockstar has built, but the morally complex relationship that its developers have created between the player and this imagined world. Reviewers remark on behaving more considerately while playing the game, and how it rewards attentiveness in some of its fictional relationships and encourages players to talk their way out of trouble rather than immediately reaching for a gun. After decades of allowing players to behave badly online with impunity, GTA VI doesn’t necessarily want them to be good, but it asks them to think twice about being bad.

https://www.humanite.fr/monde/europe/gen.title: Génération Gaza : Allemagne, Italie, France… Partout en Europe, les étudiants contre la militarisation et pour la paix
https://www.humanite.fr/monde/europe/gen.author: Lina Sankari
https://www.humanite.fr/monde/europe/gen.text:
Il y a eu une génération Vietnam, il y a une génération Gaza. Ce renouveau du pacifisme s’exprimera dans 25 pays européens, ce vendredi 20 novembre, par une mobilisation inédite contre la militarisation du continent. La jeunesse conteste le retour de la conscription et demande la réorientation des budgets alloués à la guerre.
« Voici que va commencer pour moi le grand inconnu de la guerre. Que m’arrivera-t-il ? Je n’en sais absolument rien. » Il n’a que 20 ans et va partir au front. C’est la Première Guerre mondiale et un jeune Auvergnat va y laisser sa vie. Un de plus. Il y a dans la simplicité de ces quelques mots laissés à ses parents toute l’horreur de la guerre qu’il n’a pas choisie. Quelques jours après les célébrations de l’armistice du 11-Novembre, les jeunes européens sont rattrapés par l’effroi de voir leur continent plongé dans un conflit d’ampleur. Il faut dire que les dirigeants y mettent du leur.
En France, en Pologne, en Finlande, en Italie et en Allemagne, la logique de reconversion des industries civiles vers le militaire est partout la même et sert les plans de licenciements et la réduction des budgets sociaux. Elle est portée par le plan ReArm Europe à 800 milliards d’euros (désormais connu sous le nom de Readiness 2030), monté dans l’urgence à la suite du désengagement pourtant prévisible des États-Unis en Ukraine et en Europe.
« L’escalade constante des guerres, du réarmement et de l’oppression impérialiste, conjuguée au dérèglement climatique, façonne le monde dans lequel nous grandissons et nous prive, en tant que jeunes, de la possibilité d’un avenir digne », affirme le manifeste de 50 organisations de jeunesse qui prévoient, ce 20 novembre, une grève internationale contre la guerre. Manifestations, blocages, assemblées et actions diverses essaimeront...

https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/it.title: Sotheby’s New York Impressionist and Modern Art Sale Rakes in $777.8 M., Italian Exhibition Ordered to Remove Fascist Imagery, and More: Morning Links for November 19, 2026
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/it.author: Hikmat Mohammed
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/it.text:
To receive Morning Links in your inbox every weekday, sign up for our Breakfast with ARTnews newsletter.
Good Morning!
- It was an evening of superlatives at Sotheby’s, whose two auctions of Impressionist and modern art in New York last night raked in $777.8 million in total.
- Italian lawmakers have ordered the removal of imagery containing fascist references from an exhibition in Rome marking the centenary of far-right politician Pino Rauti.
- The collective Artists 4 Artists Miami is calling for an “Art Basel Boycott” that asks the public to refrain from participating in the forthcoming Miami Art Week’s major fairs.
The Headlines
SOTHEBY’S SUPERLATIVES. It was an evening of superlatives at Sotheby’s, whose two auctions of Impressionist and modern art in New York last night raked in a total of $777.8 million, reports ARTnews. The lump sum is the highest for a single night at the auction house, surpassing the $706 million it achieved a year ago at the same time. The highlights from the evening included the unexpected sale of a tiny Claude Monet with a wild backstory, There was also Vincent van Gogh’s Châtaigniers en fleurs (1890), which sold to dealer William Acquavella for $190.4 million with fees, after a week dominated by a Nazi-era restitution dispute. The sum was more than Sotheby’s bargained for and beat the artist’s previous record by just over 62 percent, marking a clear victory for the auction house. But there were hitches, including a Remedios Varo drawing that failed to sell, and three lots were withdrawn while the sale was in progress.
ROUTING OUT PINO RAUTI. Italian lawmakers have ordered the removal of imagery containing fascist references from an exhibition in Rome marking the centenary of far-right politician Pino Rauti, who died in 2012, reports Reuters. The exhibit at the Palazzo Valdina complex, sponsored by the Italian culture ministry, has caused an uproar in Italy, where Rauti is remembered for joining Benito Mussolini’s Nazi-collaborating government during World War II and later becoming a leader of the neo-fascist Italian Social Movement (MSI). The controversial content, which was reportedly removed by Wednesday, included a photograph of Rauti beneath a flag bearing a Celtic cross linked to neo-fascism, while the figure of Mussolini was also given pride of place. Rauti never denounced his past, but that didn’t stop him from being voted into Italy’s lower house of parliament for five terms, until 1992. The order to take down parts of the exhibition was sparked by demands from left-leaning members of parliament, who called the whole endeavor “a disgrace.”
The Digest
Artists 4 Artists Miami is gathering steam for an “Art Basel Boycott” that calls on the public to refrain from participating in the forthcoming Miami Art Week. [The Art Newspaper]
Benin may be the first country to benefit from new legislation in France designed to facilitate the return of artworks looted during the colonial era, and has formally made a request for 35 items, which are housed in the Musée du quai Branly. [Le Monde]
Jeff Koons’ decision to sell parts of his collection at Christie’s this week makes art critic Jerry Saltz sick, and here’s why. [New York Magazine]
The medieval “Ugly Duchess” portrait by Quentin Metsys hanging in London’s National Gallery may depict a famously homely “Old Woman,” but she was not meant to be alone: the companion piece to the painting features a man, and it is heading to auction at Christie’s next month, where it may fetch as much as $10.5 million. [Artnet News]
Phillips names new senior leadership in Asia, and other industry moves. [ARTnews]
The Kicker
BACKWARDS BEAUTY. One might be tempted to think that current beauty standards were whipped into the collective consciousness via modern mass media, but a new study confirms the source goes much further back and can be found glaringly apparent in historic paintings. Research published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B analyzes hundreds of paintings throughout history to demonstrate how Western beauty standards for women have evolved away from the curvy female ideal to straighter and androgynous silhouettes over the past 300 years, reports the Times of London. Authors of the study examined paintings of upper-class women in Western paintings from 1650 to 1950, and asked over 1,500 people to judge them for things like waist-to-hip ratio. Little surprise: Women’s bodies tended to move from the hourglass shape once deemed the ideal beauty associated with fertility to a straighter, “more tubular” silhouette. To Jeanne Bovet, co-author of the study, the artworks are seen as “cognitive fossils,” or relics of vanished societies and their values. “People have always paid attention to appearance,” said Bovet. “And usually it’s because they have wanted to send a signal.” It seems to have worked.

https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.author: Guardian sport
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.text:
After three Premier League defeats on the spin, Manchester City need something or someone to come along and put some pep in their step, and Fulham look like just the thing – after all, in the past 15 years these teams have played 20 times in all competitions, and City have won precisely 20 of those games. Their current run of 17 successive league wins against Fulham is the longest run of victories by one club against a single opponent in English top-flight history. It is a reflection of the changing realities of English football, and the gulf that has opened between the teams that dominate it and those who seek to challenge them, that of the top 10 such runs all but one occurred in whole or in part after 2010 and six of them have been achieved by Sheikh Mansour’s Manchester City, with Chelsea responsible for another two, Manchester United one, and Portsmouth’s postwar, 13-game supremacy over Everton – a wild ride that included two 5-0s, a 5-1, a 6-3 and a 7-0 – the anomaly. Simon Burnton
Positivity surrounds Aston Villa despite them failing to win in four matches, the last of which ended in agonising fashion; they had to settle for a 4-4 draw at Manchester United after twice squandering a two-goal advantage. Villa should have managed the final minutes better, but a home date with Sunderland presents an opportunity to return to winning ways. Unai Emery needs to eliminate the defensive naivety that has blighted some performances and the expected absence of Matty Cash, this time owing to concussion sustained on Poland duty, would deny the Villa manager his preferred defensive lineup. This fixture threw up a classic last season, Tammy Abraham scoring a stoppage-time winner to extend the visitors’ miserable record at Villa Park. Sunderland have won on only two of their past 17 league visits, their last victory coming in 2011 courtesy of the former Villa loanee Phil Bardsley. Ben Fisher
The last time Alex Scott played for Bournemouth, Marco Rose was yet to taste victory in the Premier League. When the 23-year-old returns to midfield he will do so with the team in a totally different place. Bournemouth have racked up eight straight wins in all competitions before hosting Nottingham Forest on Saturday and Scott, who has been able to build his fitness during the international break after a thigh problem, may have to wait his turn owing to the form of Tyler Adams and Ryan Christie. If Rose opts for momentum, then Eli Junior Kroupi, fresh from scoring his first France goal, could make his first start of the season after sustaining a freak foot injury in pre-season. Bournemouth have hardly been short of firepower, though, with Evanilson scoring seven goals in his past eight games. BF
Chelsea left Wearside battered and bruised after being pushed around by Brian Brobbey. The Sunderland forward bullied Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill, who had to be substituted at half-time, and won the game’s decisive penalty with a solo run that left Xabi Alonso angry with his side’s powderpuff defending. Alonso insisted Chelsea had prepared for Brobbey’s threat; the Chelsea manager will hope they are better at putting the plan into practice when they face another target man on Saturday. Leeds head to Stamford Bridge and will look to Dominic Calvert-Lewin, fresh from helping England get over the line against Spain last weekend, to unnerve Alonso’s defenders. Jacob Steinberg
Thomas Frank’s first assessment of his new charges after taking over at Crystal Palace this week included the nuggets that “we’re conceding too many goals … we need to work on the defensive side of things with principles, attitude, everything regarding that”, and in particular “we need to work on the set pieces, that’s key”. If he can’t inspire an immediate improvement this is where this match could be decided, being as it is an encounter between the league’s worst set-piece defenders – no one comes close to the 67 shots and xG of 7.44 coughed up by Palace at restarts – and the best. Though Coventry have let in one goal from set pieces, and neither Brentford nor Liverpool have shipped any, the hosts’ set-piece xG of 1.65 is a league low, and they were equally outstanding from dead-ball situations in the Championship last season. The home side will be boosted by the return of the 6ft 4in defender Bobby Thomas, who, despite a calf injury that meant he missed the last two games and the final third of the one before that, has still made more clearances than any other Coventry player. SB
It may have been a slightly strange week for Tottenham fans. They have watched as their former managers Mauricio Pochettino and Thomas Frank have been installed at Manchester United and Crystal Palace respectively, while their current head coach, Roberto De Zerbi, picked up the Premier League’s manager of the month award for October. That is reflective of the improvement De Zerbi has overseen in recent weeks, with Spurs happy to move forward with the Italian and avoid the chaos enveloping some of their rivals. The long-held assumption among some connected to Tottenham that Pochettino would one day return to save the club must now be banished; De Zerbi needs full buy-in from everyone to build his project. That’s the only way Spurs can ensure they steer clear of future crises. Dominic Booth
With the temperature in Newcastle forecast to dip to 0C at kick-off, Matthias Jaissle is perhaps hoping that his team’s guests from north London (where a balmy 9C is predicted at 5.30pm) freeze in the Tyneside chill. Otherwise it is hard to envisage his young side overcoming a formidable looking Arsenal on a day when Newcastle’s head coach seeks what would be only his second win in seven games. Home fans will not merely be hurt by the sight of their much-missed former captain Bruno Guimarães wearing Arsenal colours but decidedly nervous about a fixture that precedes a run of tricky engagements involving a trip to Brighton and home dates with Manchester United and Sunderland. Jaissle’s cause could be helped should Mikel Arteta name Guimarães in his starting XI and the crowd respond to the once adored Brazilian’s defection by creating the sort of hostile atmosphere that might just galvanise a Newcastle team expected to contain the former Arsenal midfielder Joe Willock. Meanwhile Jaissle’s defence must be mindful of the threat posed by another Newcastle old boy in Mikel Merino. Louise Taylor
Brighton are out to prove their early-season form has been no fluke and the fixture list for November and December looks promising for their chances of retaining their lofty position. Hull, having started the season with back-to-back league victories, now appear vulnerable and have not won since that August burst. Brighton follow the trip to Humberside with a home game against Universitatea Craiova in the Conference League, then host Newcastle, and face none of the big six until a visit to Tottenham on 29 December. With Brighton having won seven of their 10 league games, tentative talk of a title challenge may not seem so fanciful come Christmas. The challenge tactically for Fabian Hürzeler’s men will be to deal with the tag of favourites for most of their upcoming games, with teams perhaps starting to wise up to Brighton’s high-pressing, vertical style. DB
And so it starts all over again. Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager in 13 years – not forgetting the interim spells of Ryan Giggs, Michael Carrick, Ralf Rangnick and Darren Fletcher – was impressively quick to commit to the cause when taking a private jet from Cincinnati to Manchester immediately after his final game as USA head coach. Mauricio Pochettino needs his new, floundering team to reciprocate at Anfield. United have conceded four times in the first four minutes of a game this season, seven goals in the opening 17 minutes in total, and will have had little time to absorb instructions from their latest coach by the time they face an expectant Liverpool. United’s defensive options might tempt many managers to board the next flight out but, as a decent record against the so-called big six since the start of last season demonstrates, the team are capable of showing up when they feel like it. That is just one of the many issues Pochettino has to address. Andy Hunter
Fans of neutral officiating will appreciate the fact that both Brentford and Everton have won six games refereed by Craig Pawson, who will take charge of this match. But where the two clubs’ experiences diverge is that, while Brentford have only danced to the tune of the Pawson whistle 12 times, enjoying a 50% win ratio, Everton have toiled through 33 Pawson-helmed matches for an equivalent figure of 18%. Of Everton’s past 14 Pawson-patrolled matches there has been only one victory, and 10 defeats. Pawson, meanwhile, has taken charge of five Brentford home matches and they have won every one, thanks in part to the two penalties he has awarded them (both converted), compared with the one he gave against them (missed). Jack Grealish is back having sat out Everton’s past four league games because of illness, lack of fitness and a breach of club discipline, but given that, of the three Premier League matches he has missed, Everton won the two most recent – and the other one was at Arsenal – he may not go straight back into the team. Indeed of Everton’s four league wins this season, Grealish has missed three and played only eight minutes in a fourth. SB

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
El Salvador’s Bukele expected to formalise bid for third presidential term
The Salvadoran president has won popularity at home and abroad through a crime crackdown that has granted the state enormous power.
Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele is set to formally register his candidacy for his country’s upcoming presidential race, as he seeks a third consecutive term.
Thursday was the registration deadline for the election, which is slated for February 28, 2027.
The 45-year-old president has been widely expected to seek re-election, a move that would further consolidate his party’s leadership in the Central American country.
Bukele is the founder and leader of the Nuevas Ideas party, which controls El Salvador’s Legislative Assembly by a wide margin.
While El Salvador’s constitution previously prohibited presidents from seeking immediate re-election, the Supreme Court overturned that rule in 2021, paving the way for Bukele to run for a second term in 2024.
Then, in 2025, the Legislative Assembly passed a constitutional amendment allowing Bukele to seek a third term. The amendment also extended the length of a presidential term from five to six years.
Bukele secured his party’s nomination for the 2027 race in July. He is expected to return to the ballot alongside his current vice president, Felix Ulloa.
Bukele’s time in office has been defined by a crackdown on criminal gangs that has won him massive popularity at home and turned him into an icon for the political right across Latin America.
In 2022, his government announced a so-called state of emergency to address high levels of crime in the country.
It empowered the police to make sweeping arrests, but it also heralded the suspension of key civil liberties. Some people were detained without charge. Mass trials have been carried out, with hundreds of defendants being sentenced at a time.
More than 1 percent of the country’s population is estimated to have been arrested as a result, with little due process for those seeking to contest their guilt, according to human rights groups.
Advocates also warn that rights abuses, torture and poor conditions are systematic in Salvadoran prisons.
The state of emergency has been extended for years, although it was initially intended as a temporary measure and the government claims El Salvador’s gangs have been all but dismantled.
The United States Treasury has also accused Bukele’s government of negotiating with the gangs in secret, offering incentives to help lower crime.
But experts say human rights activists and members of the news media have seen their ability to monitor abuses and corruption in the country hampered under Bukele.
Some, like human rights lawyer Ruth Lopez, have allegedly been detained for their work without access to legal support. She has spent more than a year in “incommunicado detention”, according to the group Amnesty International.
Under Bukele, El Salvador has also passed a Foreign Agents Law that allows the government to restrict civil society groups that receive funding from abroad.
Those efforts have prompted allegations that Bukele has weaponised the state against his critics.
But those concerns have done little to dent his popularity, and Bukele is considered the clear favourite to win the election.
A handful of candidates, including Maytee Iraheta of the right-wing Nationalist Republican Alliance and Rafael Aguirre of the left-wing Farabundo Marti National Liberation Front, are also set to contest the presidency.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Four bodies recovered after Senegal boat capsizes amid migration surge
Four bodies have been recovered after a migrant boat capsized off Senegal’s coast, as authorities continue searching for survivors amid fears that the death toll could rise significantly.
Boubacar Seye, president of the nonprofit Horizons Sans Frontieres, confirmed the latest death toll to the Reuters news agency on Thursday, a day after the vessel capsized near the coastal town of Yenne, south of Dakar.
A local official said at least 50 people were aboard the boat, which struck a rock while migrants were being transferred from smaller fishing vessels to a larger wooden pirogue.
The number of people still missing remains unclear.
Canary Islands
The incident comes amid an intensifying wave of attempted Atlantic crossings from West Africa to Spain’s Canary Islands, with migrant boats being intercepted or rescued almost daily.
New figures from Spain’s Interior Ministry show that 24,364 migrants reached the Canary Islands between January 1 and November 15, compared with 14,690 during the same period last year, an increase of nearly two-thirds.
The ministry had recorded just 13,327 arrivals by the end of October, meaning 11,037 people reached the archipelago in the first 15 days of November alone.
The surge has persisted despite extensive maritime operations. Senegal’s navy said it had rescued or intercepted 1,424 people on November 16 and 17, including passengers aboard nine fishing boats, according to the Senegalese Press Agency (APS).
Cheikh Sadibou Senghor, head of Senegal’s National Division for Combating Migrant Smuggling, said authorities had intercepted 6,889 people in operations linked to irregular migration, prevented 107 departures and dismantled 88 smuggling networks between January and November, APS reported.
Just days before the boat capsized, authorities announced the dismantling of a suspected migrant-smuggling network in Yenne itself, arresting 14 people and seizing two boats, three engines and 12.5 million CFA francs ($22,000), according to APS.
Nearly 600 dead
The United Nations refugee agency said nearly 600 people had died trying to reach the Canary Islands from West Africa so far this year, highlighting the dangers of the increasingly busy migration route.
As authorities struggle to contain the surge, Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has called for greater efforts to improve employment opportunities for young people.
At a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, Faye requested a detailed assessment of the challenges facing efforts to curb irregular migration, according to a government statement cited by Reuters.
But Seye warned that tougher enforcement measures alone would not prevent further tragedies.
“We need to wake up to the gravity of the situation. The strategy deployed until now is not working,” he told Reuters.
“We need to fix the root causes of this problem.”

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.title: Fiona the hippo dies after ingesting knitted hat at Cincinnati zoo
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.author: Auzzy Byrdsell
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text:
Fiona the hippo, one of America’s most famous zoo animals, has died after efforts to remove a knitted hat that she swallowed after it fell into her enclosure proved unsuccessful.
“It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo wrote in a post on social media.
With surgery too risky for full-grown hippos such as Fiona, who weighed in the region of 2,500lb (1,113kg), veterinarians tried an alternative method of getting the hat to pass through her system.
The hat fell near Fiona when a visitor to the Cincinnati zoo tossed it in the air, after which it bounced off a ceiling fan and fell into the enclosure, according to the Associated Press. Fiona ate the hat and was initially asymptomatic.
Days later, however, she began to lose appetite and staff at the zoo were forced to feed Fiona more in the hope that she would eventually get the hat through her digestive system.
“Despite multiple attempts to move the hat out of her system, it was ultimately too much to overcome. The team performed necessary supportive care today in an attempt to save her, but it was not successful and she did not recover,” the zoo statement said.
The zoo announced on Wednesday that the animal care team was using a vibration plate from a horse farm to help move things along, according to the Associated Press.
Fiona was sedated a second time on Tuesday for evaluation. After an ultrasound, veterinarians could see her intestines still trying to push the hat through. They also used a 9ft scope colonoscopy to view her intestines.
“The hope is that the vibrations will help encourage movement through her digestive tract and help the object pass,” the zoo had said on social media. Fiona remained out of her enclosure while she was receiving treatment.
Footage from the procedure released by the zoo on Wednesday shows her snorting and moving around her enclosure, which vets said was a sign of progress. Her hydration levels were being monitored.
“Her care team even offered her a sniff of coffee, a scent she has always liked, and they were happy to see her respond. Thank you for your continued love and concern for Fiona and her dedicated care team,” the zoo said.
This wasn’t the first time Fiona’s health had been at risk. She became a global sensation after her premature birth in 2017, when she couldn’t stand on her own.
Hopes for Fiona’s recovery had garnered support from across the country including, apparently, from Timothy, another hippo at the San Antonio zoo. Timothy had sent well wishes via Instagram. “I know you’ve got some amazing people looking after you. We’re sending lots of love from Texas to the most beautiful hippo in the world. Hope you’re feeling more like yourself soon!”
Zoo staff published a message on social media reminding visitors to be careful when near habitats and to secure belongings.
Fiona was born six weeks premature at just 29lb (13.2kgs), falling below the lowest recorded birth weight for her species at the time. Because she was initially too weak to nurse, Cincinnati Zoo staff hand-milked her mother while documenting Fiona’s recovery through photos and videos that captivated the internet.
Her survival then offered a much-needed positive chapter for the zoo following months of intense public backlash over the fatal shooting of Harambe, the silverback gorilla killed after a child breached his enclosure.
Wildlife facilities have long warned of the dangers posed by foreign objects dropped or blown into animal habitats. Past incidents have demonstrated the fatal risks involved, including a rare antelope that choked to death on a plastic cap of a snack pouch at a Tennessee zoo two years ago, and a polar bear at a German zoo that died in 2014 after swallowing a visitor’s dropped jacket.

https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.title: Anthropic closes first day of public trading at $1.3tn valuation after largest-ever IPO
https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.author: Johana Bhuiyan
https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.text:
Anthropic closed its first day of trading on the US stock market about 17% higher than its initial public offering price. At the close of market on Thursday, Anthropic shares were trading at just over $97 with a nearly $1.3tn total market capitalization, $1.75tn fully diluted.
While the final share value was higher than the IPO price of $83, it marked a dip from an early high of $111.50. The firm’s shares initially soared 34% when trading got under way on its US market debut on Thursday, valuing the company at more than $2tn. Nonetheless, Anthropic’s ranked among the biggest stock market flotations in history. The artificial intelligence startup, founded in 2021, became one of the most valuable publicly traded businesses in the world.
“Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing,” said Anthropic’s chief executive, Dario Amodei, who rang the Nasdaq opening bell.
Anthropic announced late on Wednesday that it had sold 980m shares to underwriters, an upsized offering that raised $81.3bn, surpassing the previous record set by SpaceX’s initial $75bn fundraise in June.
US stocks slumped at the end of trading, a potential sign that Anthropic’s mammoth IPO wasn’t enough to alleviate concerns over the AI industry’s volatility. Most of the major chipmakers’ stock prices closed the day lower than they started. While Nvidia hit its sixth day of losses after its latest earnings call, other players like Micron and Broadcom also saw their share prices decline.
The company’s listing serves as a bellwether for the multitrillion-dollar artificial intelligence boom as the first frontier lab to be publicly traded. Wall Street investors and the entire global tech industry are watching closely how it fares on the public market.
Anthropic’s stock market debut makes it the first firm focused entirely on AI “uncluttered by an ad business or a rocket business” to be publicly traded, analysts at Yorkville Ives said.
“Anthropic’s IPO is a big near-term win for the tech sector and should help restore some investor confidence that the AI Revolution growth thesis is not waning,” Yorkville Ives analysts wrote in a memo.
The company has seen explosive growth in revenue every year of its existence – sometimes more than 1,000% – according to its investor prospectus, filed at the end of October. Anthropic brought in $16.2bn in the first six months of 2026, up from $4.6bn in revenue for all of 2025.
“You’ve seen an astronomical growth rate in terms of the top line,” said Evan Schlossman, a principal at Neostellar, a publicly traded venture capital firm. “The question investors are going to be looking at leading up to the IPO, and once it’s public, is what happens to that growth rate.”
Anthropic has also lost an enormous amount of money. In the first half of 2026, the company reported losses of $80bn, though that was largely due to a one-off charge. Losses grew to $104bn in the first nine months of 2026. The firm expects its costs to balloon as it works to secure more compute, which refers to the processing and computational power provided by arrays of semiconductor chips often located in datacenters. It is the resource that powers generative artificial intelligence and Anthropic’s single largest expense, about $18.8bn in the first nine months of 2026.
“The development of frontier AI models requires substantial investments of compute resources, capital, and human capital to conduct large-scale training runs that may span weeks or months and cost many millions of dollars,” the company’s executives wrote in the prospectus.
Anthropic has disclosed in great detail all the ways its AI models may pose a danger to humanity – including being used to develop bioweapons or deepen repression around the world. Amodei has called for a slowdown on the development of the most advanced AI models after employees expressed concerns that the companies were building them irresponsibility.
The company beat competitors like OpenAI to launching on the US stock market. However, the IPO comes amid uncertainty as the industry braces for any additional impact or fallout from the recent Nvidia scandal that led to the resignation of its founder and chief executive, Jensen Huang.
There is “huge volatility in the market”, and investors are going to be looking at how sustainable the company’s AI growth is, said Schlossman. Investors are also keen to see how important Anthropic will be in the larger AI ecosystem. The company has focused primarily on enterprise customers rather than individual consumers. Anthropic’s Claude code product has proved popular with software engineers.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Six killed in suspected gas explosion at Georgia apartment building
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Six killed in suspected gas explosion at Georgia apartment building
Tbilisi Mayor Kakha Kaladze said authorities would temporarily relocate 28 families.
Six people, including a child, have been killed after a suspected natural gas explosion caused part of a five-storey apartment building to collapse in Georgia’s capital, Tbilisi, according to the AFP news agency.
The blast struck the residential building in the suburban Ponichala district on Thursday morning, trapping several residents beneath the rubble.
Georgian Interior Minister Sulkhan Tamazashvili said rescuers had recovered six bodies from the wreckage, including that of a young child.
A three-year-old girl was pulled alive from the rubble after several hours of rescue operations, prompting applause from onlookers gathered at the scene.
Emergency Management Service chief Teimuraz Mgebrishvili said one of the women found dead was believed to be the girl’s mother, according to AFP.
Doctors at Ingorokva University Clinic said the rescued girl was in stable condition and scans had revealed no serious traumatic injuries, Georgian Public Broadcaster (1TV) reported.
An 11-year-old boy was also being treated in intensive care, although his condition was described as relatively stable, according to the broadcaster.
Tamazashvili said preliminary findings indicated that the explosion occurred on the fifth floor when a resident attempted to switch on a gas heater.
However, gas supplier Tbilisi Energy said the apartment identified as the likely source of the explosion had been registered as unoccupied and had recorded no gas consumption over the past year, according to 1TV. The company said it had not yet been able to inspect the damaged property.
Tbilisi Mayor Kakha Kaladze said authorities would temporarily relocate 28 families, comprising more than 100 residents, to hotels after structural assessments found two sections of the building unsafe, according to Georgia’s Interpressnews agency.
Prosecutor Levan Vepkhvadze said a criminal investigation had been launched into possible violations of safety regulations.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.title: Dodgers owner Mark Walter set to sell Los Angeles Sparks for WNBA record $750m
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.author: Guardian sport and agencies
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.text:
Mark Walter, who has a controlling stake in the Los Angeles Dodgers, is set to sell off another sports asset, with Sportico reporting on Thursday that he is close to a deal to offload the WNBA’s Los Angeles Sparks for $750m.
San Diego Padres owners José E Feliciano and his wife, Kwanza Jones, are reportedly set to purchase the Sparks in a record deal for a WNBA team. The previous largest price came when the Connecticut Sun were sold for $300m in March. The Sun plan to move to Houston.
A group let by Walter bought the Sparks for $10m in 2014. Former NBA star Magic Johnson was also listed among the ownership group. WNBA franchises have soared in value in recent years thanks to the popularity of stars such as Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark. And while the Sparks have missed the playoffs for six consective seasons, they are based in one of the US’s largest markets and have bankable stars such as Cameron Brink.
Walter is currently under federal investigation over allegations of tax fraud. He denies any wrongdoing. Since the investigation started, Walter has sold his majority stake in the Los Angeles Lakers in a reported $12.5bn deal in August, and his 13% stake in the Premier League’s Chelsea. Reports indicate he could be looking for a buyer for his stake in the Cadillac Formula 1 team that was recently valued at $3bn.
Walter has a 27% controlling stake in the Dodgers, with the Los Angeles Times reporting earlier this month that he has no plans to sell his investment in the MLB club. Earlier this year, Sportico valued the Dodgers at more than $9bn.
Feliciano and Jones officially purchased the Padres in August for $3.9bn. Feliciano is also part of the ownership group of Chelsea.

https://www.humanite.fr/social-et-econom.title: BNP Paribas, Total, Safran… À CentraleSupélec, des étudiants mobilisés contre les entreprises écocidaires et complices du génocide à Gaza
https://www.humanite.fr/social-et-econom.author: La rédaction
https://www.humanite.fr/social-et-econom.text:
Des étudiants de l’école d’ingénieurs se sont mobilisés durant le forum des entreprises de l’école pour dénoncer la présence en son sein d’entreprises qui contribuent à la destruction de l’environnement. Une action qui s’inscrit dans la suite d’une prise de conscience de plus en plus partagée par d’autres élèves de grandes écoles.
Au tour des étudiants de CentraleSupélec d’interroger leur enseignement et de chercher à s’inventer un autre futur. Quelques semaines après que des étudiants de Polytechnique ont dénoncé l’influence jugée omniprésente des grandes entreprises au sein des grandes écoles et au lendemain du vote du conseil de la faculté des sciences de Montpellier pour cesser son partenariat pédagogique avec TotalEnergies, des étudiants de la prestigieuse école d’ingénieurs ont mené une action symbolique au cours du Forum de l’école, ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026 au parc des Expositions de Paris.
Un « die in » devant le stand de TotalEnergies, pour « refuser de laisser des entreprises destructrices faire leur publicité sans contestation ». Une action en « solidarité avec des morts bien réels, des morts à cause du dérèglement climatique, des morts innombrables à cause de nombreuses famines, maladies et catastrophes climatiques à venir ».
Des firmes écocides et complices de génocide
Le pétrolier n’est pas le seul visé ; BNP Paribas, Société générale, Crédit agricole ou Banque Populaire, « ces entreprises totalisent près de 40 milliards d’euros de financement aux énergies fossiles », dénonce la trentaine de manifestants.
Autre vecteur de colère des étudiants, « MBDA, Thalès, Safran et Dassault Aviation, des entreprises qui arment, notamment, l’armée israélienne » accusée de génocide à Gaza.
Ils ont adressé un « merci » ironique à la direction de l’école pour « avoir poursuivi en conseil de discipline des élèves qui ont interrompu, cinq minutes, une rencontre avec des entreprises de l’armement pour déclamer un discours, pacifiquement ».
Un « merci », encore, « pour avoir retiré de la vidéo de la remise des diplômes les discours d’étudiants trop critiques ». « Nous déplorons que la direction n’incite pas ses étudiants à questionner la place de ces intérêts privés dans l’enseignement supérieur », conclut la déclaration des étudiants.
La Terre de nos batailles
La justice climatique, c’est notre bataille. Celle qui relie luttes environnementales et sociales pour contrer un système capitaliste faisant ventre de tout. Du vivant, de la planète, de notre humanité.
Il n’y a pas de fatalité.
- Nous démasquons les manipulations des lobbies.
- Nous battons en brèche les dénis climatiques mortifères.
- Nous mettons en valeur les initiatives visant à réduire les inégalités environnementales et les fractures sociales.
Soutenez-nous.
Je veux en savoir plus

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120399.title: Zivilgesellschaft | Kürzungen bei »Demokratie leben!«: Schlüsselfertig für die AfD
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120399.author: Hendrik Lasch
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120399.text:
- Politik
- Zivilgesellschaft
Kürzungen bei »Demokratie leben!«: Schlüsselfertig für die AfD
20 Millionen Euro weniger für die engagierte Zivilgesellschaft vom Bund: CDU-Ministerin Karin Prien betreibt das Geschäft der Rechtsextremen.
In Sachsen läuft der Versuch einer »demokratischen Raumnahme«. So heißt ein Projekt, das nicht-rechte Jugendgruppen in kleineren Städten unterstützt, etwa mit Geld und Expertise für die Organisation von Festivals. Man wolle »kleine demokratische Pflänzchen« hegen, erklärte das Kulturbüro Sachsen als Träger des Projekts. Derlei Arbeit ist enorm wichtig in Zeiten, in denen laut der jüngsten Autoritarismus-Studie die Demokratie in immer breiteren Teilen der Gesellschaft rapide an Zuspruch verliert und der Wunsch nach einer »starken Partei, die die Volksgemeinschaft verkörpert«, im Osten mehrheitsfähig ist.
Allerdings wird es die »demokratische Raumnahme« 2027 nicht mehr geben. Grund sind die Kürzungen im Bundesprogramm »Demokratie leben!«, die das von Karin Prien (CDU) geführte Bundesbildungsministerium beschlossen hat. Künftig stehen jährlich 167 Millionen Euro bereit, 20 Millionen weniger als bisher. Die Anzahl der geförderten Träger geht um ein Viertel auf 150 zurück. Betroffen von den Kürzungen sind etwa der Bundesverband Mobile Beratung (BMB) und Projekte wie die »Trialoge«, die nach den Terrorakten der Hamas vom 7. Oktober 2023 den israelisch-palästinensischen Dialog aufrechterhalten wollten. Auch Projekten, die verbreitetem Rassismus gegen schwarze Menschen oder Islamfeindlichkeit entgegenwirken, wird Geld gestrichen.
Es ließe sich sagen: Gespart wird an vielen Stellen; da muss eben auch die Zivilgesellschaft den Gürtel enger schnallen. Die Folgen sind aber fatal. Strukturen, die aufgebaut wurden, seit vor 25 Jahren nach rassistischen Morden zum »Aufstand der Anständigen« geblasen wurde, werden gefährdet, Menschen, die sich dieser Arbeit gegen viele Anfeindungen stellen, vor den Kopf gestoßen, fachliche Expertise wird preisgegeben.
All das geschieht in Zeiten, in denen eine demokratische Zivilgesellschaft so nötig, aber auch so gefährdet ist wie nie. Die AfD erfährt beispiellosen Zuspruch und schickt sich an, in Sachsen-Anhalt erstmals eine Landesregierung zu stellen. Es ist kein Zufall, dass ganz oben auf ihrer politischen Agenda das Austrocknen des angeblichen »NGO-Komplexes« steht. Demokratie-Initiativen und ihre Projekte sind oft die letzten, die sich der rechtsextremen Raumnahme durch die AfD entgegenstellen.
Dass auch die CDU der Zivilgesellschaft an den Kragen geht, geschieht nicht fahrlässig. Wenn »Trialog«-Begründer Shai Hoffmann fragt, ob Prien »noch Förderpolitik oder längst Kulturkampf« betreibe, liegt die Antwort auf der Hand. Die Ministerin begründete den Umbau von »Demokratie leben!« mit dem »Eindruck«, die Ausrichtung des Programms reiche »eher in das linksliberale Milieu« hinein. Dieses »Milieu« ist Teilen der CDU nicht zuletzt deshalb suspekt, weil es nicht mit Kritik spart, wenn sich die Partei mit der AfD gemein macht.
Die Kürzungen bei »Demokratie leben!« haben denn auch eine Vorgeschichte. Dazu gehören die berüchtigten 551 Fragen, mit denen die CDU im Bundestag im Februar 2025 Auskünfte zur Finanzierung und »politischen Neutralität« von »staatlich geförderten Organisationen« begehrte und die der AfD als Blaupause für die Bekämpfung von Demokratieprojekten dienen. Dazu gehört auch die von CDU und AfD gemeinsam beschlossene Ablehnung von Fördermitteln für die Zivilgesellschaft in Bautzen und Salzwedel. Ob derlei Anbiederung der CDU nutzt, ist fraglich. Der Effekt dürfte ein anderer sein, fürchtete nach Priens Kahlschlag bei »Demokratie leben!« der Schriftsteller Max Czollek: »Das Land wird für die AfD schlüsselfertig gemacht.«
Kein Milliardär im Rücken
Andere Medien haben Konzerne oder Milliardäre im Rücken. Wir haben die nd.Genossenschaft und Leser*innen wie dich. Das macht uns unabhängig und genau das wollen wir bleiben. Aber es heißt auch: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro.
Du kannst direkt hier spenden, einmalig oder regelmäßig, damit nd bleibt.

https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/1.text:
US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months
The US House Foreign Committee released the chip export licensing data amid Nvidia’s ex-CEO’s affair with alleged Chinese spy.
The administration of United States President Donald Trump approved exports of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee has said.
The Department of Commerce’s approvals covered exports of 879,000 chips, including 75,000 for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent, 43,000 for Baidu and 4,000 for BYD, the committee said on Thursday.
Companies had sought permission to ship 3.4 million of them to China during the period, committee documents show.
The unusual release of chip export licensing data comes as the Trump administration faces heightened scrutiny following revelations about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which fuelled renewed calls for a tougher stance against Chinese technology threats.
All four of the Chinese companies highlighted in the committee report are on the Pentagon’s list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies.
The committee chair, Brian Mast, has “exercised his authorities under the Export Control Reform Act to publicly reveal export control license application information regarding NVIDIA and AMD’s AI chip licenses for the People’s Republic of China”, the committee said in a statement. It was not immediately clear how many of the approvals resulted in actual China-bound shipments of the chips, which included Nvidia’s H200 and AMD’s equivalent MI325X.
News surrounding Huang has turned a spotlight on instances of Nvidia AI chips being smuggled to China that went unpunished, dialling up pressure on the Trump administration to crack down on Chinese tech threats.
“The fact that over 30 percent of the AI chips sent to China were shipped to companies that the Department of War has designated as Chinese military companies is astonishing, and calls into question whether Commerce conducted any serious national security review before approving these licenses,” said Chris McGuire, a former US official and expert on the US-China technology battle.
Nvidia said in a statement that the approvals were “subject to strict conditions and limited volumes”. It added that “despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China”.
AMD did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Former US President Joe Biden had restricted Chinese access to the prized chips over fears that they would supercharge China’s military and erode the US lead in artificial intelligence.
But Trump in December gave the green light for Nvidia to ship its H200 chip to China, rolling back Biden-era restrictions and drawing fierce criticism from China hawks across the US political spectrum.
Nvidia’s stock ended the day down 3.3 percent, while AMD slumped 7.7 percent and the broader Nasdaq and S&P 500 were down 2.2 percent and 1.8 percent, respectively.

https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.title: Coffee lovers and matcha girlies, rejoice! There’s an abundance of Advent calendars just for you
https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.author: Marian Bull
https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.text:
The holiday season can be exhausting: shopping, hosting, plotting out an elaborate popcorn garland for your annual holiday party, etc. This means that caffeine is really ready for its moment to shine. Enter the caffeinated Advent calendar. This year, there’s a bevy of Advent calendar options for coffee and tea aficionados alike, from the K-cup devotees to the single-origin matcha obsessives. I’ve tried a bunch of them – and have the energy levels to prove it. Here are the best of the year.
Great espresso, without the machine:
Cometeer Advent Calendar
The Cometeer people have pulled off a magic trick: making delicious espresso accessible to the bleary-eyed, just-woken-up person without any fancy equipment. Their (recyclable!) pods arrive frozen, and all you need to do is add hot water, or stir them into a glass of cold milk; they dissolve surprisingly quickly, and taste like a $7 latte from your local shop. Their sleek Advent calendar offers 24 pods, each of them different and many of them limited edition – like First Person Coffee’s ‘Tis the Season Blend on day one – all from roasters across the country. And if you sign up for a refill subscription, you will get $30 off. If you want to encourage your younger brother to upgrade his instant espresso addiction, this is an easy upgrade.
A tea for every mood, part one:
Stash Tea Advent Calendar
If you’re looking to give someone 24 cups of very cozy tea this winter, Stash has you covered. Their sturdy, open-book-shaped Advent calendar reveals a mix of flavored black, green and herbal teas. Wake up with a cup of Christmas Shortbread black tea, sip some (green) Tropical Snowflake during your afternoon slump and turn down with some Blueberry Joy before bed, depending on the day. I loved that these felt boldly flavored without too much artificial edge.
A tea for every mood, part two (and three):
Tea Forté Warming Joy Advent Calendar
Listen, I know that the paper teabags are slightly better for the environment, but I just love the way that the sturdy Tea Forté teabags have a little, bendable leaf at their triangle tip, which can easily latch over your mug’s edge – reminiscent of a Christmas tree, which is festive and appropriate. There are two types of calendars to choose from: because not every tea freak likes (or wants) caffeine, Tea Forté also offers an herbal-only calendar, which is all caffeine-free in addition to their “regular” assorted option. (I’ve gifted the herbal set to a fellow tea-head in the past, to great success.) I particularly loved the Spiced Herbal Mate and Ginger Lemongrass.
A merry Podmas:
Keurig 24 Cups of Cheer Advent Calendar
Perhaps you have a parent, a co-worker or a cousin who is in a co-dependent relationship with their Keurig machine? (Trick question: we all have one.) Here is a no-fail gift for that person (or those millions of people). This box holds 24 pods of various flavors and roasts, all of them meant to evoke a bit of holiday cheer, from Cinnamon Sugar Cookie to a Donut Shop classic roast.
Matcha madness:
The Roasters’ Pack Matcha Advent Calendar
I am a matcha girlie. There is simply nothing like grabbing an iced matcha latte with a friend while walking around your neighborhood, sipping on the verdant, milky, potentially sweetened caffeinated beverage. So really, this is the Advent calendar you should get for me, or for the matcha girlie (gender-neutral) in your life. The Roasters’ Pack, which also sells two coffee calendars, has put together a sampler of matchas from brands across Japan, some of which are exclusive to the Advent calendar. I loved sipping through these various matchas, which range from smooth and savory to vegetal and bright. (The Ikkyu, on day four, was a standout for me for its crisp, pronounced grassiness – that hint of springtime really picked me up post-daylight savings.)
Pourover party:
Pirates of Coffee Advent Calendar
Finally, we have an Advent calendar for the true coffee nerd in your life. Pirates of Coffee, based in Ontario, has collected (and roasted) single-origin beans from around the world, from Ethiopia to Laos. I was struck by the variety of their selection and, of course, the quality of their beans, which work equally well in a pour-over or a shot of espresso. Plus, I love that they really leaned into the brand name: the box opens up like a treasure chest – or maybe a treasure bureau, really – that makes for a gorgeous gift. Each bag holds 20g of coffee, enough for a perfect pour-over coffee or a shot of espresso. Dealer’s choice.

https://www.cartooningforpeace.org/en/pr.author: ADMIN-principal2026
https://www.cartooningforpeace.org/en/pr.text:
Cartooning for Peace / « Propaganda Monitor », le rapport de RSF sur la géopolitique de la propagande du Kremlin, illustré par Cartooning for Peace	
Reporters sans frontières (RSF) lance un nouveau rapport compilant l’ensemble des contenus de son projet “Propaganda Monitor”, un site dédié qui expose les mécanismes de propagande et de désinformation, pour mieux agir face à eux.
“Depuis longtemps, Moscou rêve de réduire au silence toute alternative à sa vision du monde. Et le contexte international favorise cette ambition. La décision du 14 mars 2025 de Donald Trump de démanteler l’Agence américaine pour les médias mondiaux (USAGM), a été accueillie avec satisfaction par le Kremlin : moins de voix indépendantes, c’est plus d’espace pour ses récits. Mais avec le Propaganda Monitor, l’idée est simple : nous devons reprendre la main face à la propagande. L’ambition est claire : donner aux citoyennes et citoyens des clés de compréhension pour ne pas subir un discours obéissant aux intérêts et qui se diffuse et se reproduit avec une agilité déconcertante.”
Thibaut Bruttin, Directeur général de RSF
Cette publication, consacrée aux stratégies du Kremlin en Russie et à l’international, est illustrée par des dessinateurs de presse du réseau Cartooning for Peace. Elle comporte également une interview exclusive du dessinateur de presse russe Denis Lopatin, exilé en France depuis 2018, qui témoigne de la gravité de la situation.

https://medor.coop/magazines/medor-n43-e.title: Les institutions sous perfusion des Big Tech — Belgique

https://medor.coop/magazines/medor-n43-e.text:
Près de 85 % des entités publiques fédérales, plus de 91 % des institutions flamandes et 71 % des communes wallonnes sont liées à Microsoft pour leur messagerie électronique, et un grand nombre de sites gouvernementaux sont hébergés par des entreprises américaines. Cette dépendance n’est pas sans poser certaines questions, en particulier au temps de l’administration Trump.
Au dernier Forum économique mondial de Davos, en janvier 2026, notre Premier ministre Bart De Wever soulignait que nous aurions intérêt, en Europe, à devenir « indépendants sur le plan technologique ». Au même moment, les relations transatlantiques connaissaient une crise sans précédent à la suite des menaces agitées par Donald Trump au sujet du Groenland. Et De Wever d’entrevoir que, dans cinq ans, nous aurions peut-être à remercier le président américain de « nous avoir réveillés juste à temps ».
Le site officiel du Premier ministre belge – premier.be – ne sera-t-il alors plus hébergé sur les serveurs de l’entreprise américaine Akamai ? Et la communication électronique de son administration ne passera-t-elle plus par les logiciels du géant Microsoft ?
Le SPF Chancellerie du Premier ministre est loin d’être le seul de nos services publics à s’en remettre largement aux géants américains du numérique tels que Microsoft et Google. C’est ce qui ressort d’une analyse de 799 sites web d’institutions publiques belges réalisée par Apache.

https://medor.coop/magazines/medor-n43-e.title: Sauvons les sentiers : Les conclusions de notre enquête
https://medor.coop/magazines/medor-n43-e.author: Chloé Andries, Olivier Bailly, Philippe Engels, Céline Gautier, Quentin Noirfalisse, Louis Van Ginneken
https://medor.coop/magazines/medor-n43-e.text:
De juin 2025 à juin 2026, Médor a enquêté avec vous sur l’entrave au passage sur les chemins publics de Wallonie.
Un chemin labouré par ci, bloqué par une barrière par là, bouffé par les ronces plus loin. Des cas isolés ?
Sur notre carte interactive, vous avez déposé des centaines de signalements. En Wallonie, 4 630 kilomètres de chemins publics sont entravés ou difficilement accessibles, sur les 51 000 de la région. Au bout du compte, c’est l’espace public qui se trouve privatisé.
Mais des actions individuelles, collectives et politiques existent pour défendre nos droits à circuler.
L’enquête
Vos signalements ont été les points de départ de nos reportages. Six journalistes de notre rédaction se sont baladés à travers la Wallonie, pour entendre les revendications des usagers, des associations de défense des chemins et (lorsqu’ils ont été réceptifs) les explications des « entraveurs » concernés, des associations de propriétaires ou d’agriculteurs.
Retrouvez ces reportages dans l’onglet «Articles» ou directement sur la carte ci-contre (les pictos jaunes).
Un article de conclusion rassemble nos constats de terrain et fait le point en dix questions, de type «Qui entrave les sentiers ?», «Pourquoi est-il si compliqué de savoir si un sentier est public ?» et «Que fait le gouvernement Wallon ?».
Ressources pratiques pour rétablir le passage
Si d’aventure, vous tombez subitement sur une barrière ou un panneau d’interdiction qui n’a pas la tronche des signalisations du code de la route et ce sur un terrain qui ne vous semble pas être une propriété privée, il s’agit peut-être d’une entrave illégale.
La carte que vous avez sous les yeux a été alimentée par des citoyen·nes constatant des entraves (les cailloux oranges) et complétée par les reportages de nos journalistes (les balises jaunes). La récolte de signalements est clôturée.
Une enquête participative de Chloé Andries, Olivier Bailly, Philippe Engels, Céline Gautier, Quentin Noirfalisse & Louis Van Ginneken avec le soutien du Fonds pour le journalisme.

Ce sentier reliait la chapelle Notre-Dame de Garennes (côté commune d’Enghien) au « bois du lapin » (côté commune de Pajottegem) via un tunnel piéton situé sous la voie de chemin de fer. Depuis plusieurs années, le sentier a été obstrué et le passage empêché par le propriétaire voisin, qui a érigé des barrières pour chevaux (du côté de la chapelle/vers la commune d’Enghien) et des barrières métalliques (du côté chemin de fer/ vers la commune (flamande) de Pajottegem), pour empêcher tout passage de promeneurs sur sa propriété (agricole) - voir photos. Ce chemin est pourtant même indiqué comme accessible sur Google Maps (voir capture d’écran, avec lieu de blocage encadré en rouge). Il semble que le blocage soit bien connu des autorités, mais fasse les frais de la « lasagne institutionnelle » belge : ce sentier relie la Wallonie à la Flandre, mais semble surtout gêner les résidents enghiennois, alors que l’autorité communale compétente (au vu du lieu du blocage du chemin) est celle de Pajottegem (en région flamande). Il se dit que des courriers auraient été adressés, par le passé, par les autorités communales enghiennoises à leurs collègues flamands afin de porter la situation à leur attention, en vain. J’ai, à titre personnel, contacté l’administration communale de Pajottegem à ce sujet voici plusieurs mois, sans suite favorable à ce jour.

TUBIZE: Accès au "chemin des amoureux" obstrué: un entrepreneur local y a déposé plusieurs containeurs pour en bloquer l'accès. La commune est au courant et le tolère (par peur de dépôts sauvages). Le sentier vicinal original (n°83) a été raboté à la construction de la ligne de chemin fer 106 (années 60?), mais l'accès au chemin de halage a continué pour les ouvriers des forges de Clabecq, via une passerelle, jusque dans les années 2000. Il y a eu depuis plusieurs tentatives pour le faire réhabiliter, sans succès. Il est facile pour la Ville de botter en touche puisque le sentier "actuel" ne suit plus le chemin vicinal original (qui n'aura jamais été mis à jour sur les cartes). Auparavant, on pouvait rejoindre le halage depuis la gare en 900m via ce sentier. Désormais, cela prend 2.5km pour y accéder.
Le 13 mai 2024, nous avons interpellé le conseil communal à ce sujet et nous avons remis une pétition de 800+ signatures. La Ville, qui avait d'abord invoqué d'obscures raisons pour éviter de se pencher sur ce dossier, dit désormais avoir l'intention de le réhabiliter. Aux dernières nouvelles, ils n'avaient toujours pas bougé d'un pouce et n'ont même pas de relevé exact du sentier. La Région Wallonne, qui cherche à établir un réseau cyclable structurant (mais qui a, d'un autre côté, financé un énorme boulevard urbain sans pistes cyclables à l'entrée de Tubize) se heurte désormais aux difficultés pour franchir la ville... Aux dernières nouvelles et faute de mieux, la Région envisageait d'intégrer le chemin des amoureux. https://www.chemindesamoureux.be

La vision réductrice des « savoirs situés », c’est la liste de courses identitaire : penser que la légitimité professionnelle d’un·e scientifique, journaliste ou documentariste doit nécessairement se fonder sur un genre, une expérience personnelle ou une couleur de peau.
La philosophe féministe Donna Harraway en appelle plutôt à une réflexion collective sur la façon dont les récits sont produits et par qui. Nous ajoutons volontiers : « et avec quels outils ».
« Je suis une femme, je suis Blanche, je suis de classe moyenne, je suis d’âge mûr, je suis éduquée, je suis d’origine irlandaise… J’ai toutes ces identités, voilà d’où je parle. » Ce genre de préambule énerve un peu Donna Haraway (Le Monde, avril 2026). Qui ? Donna Haraway herself. La philosophe féministe qui a forgé la théorie des « savoirs situés », dont s’inspire cette habitude de décliner son identité avant de s’autoriser un récit sur le réel. Autrefois, comme biologiste, elle observait les grands singes. Ou, plutôt, elle observait les primatologues qui étudiaient les grands singes. Elle remarque alors que, selon les époques, le genre ou la place dans la société, les scientifiques ne voient pas les mêmes choses chez les chimpanzés : certains voient la domination de mâles agressifs, d’autres (Jane Goodall, notamment) des relations sociales fondées sur la coopération. La science n’est pas « neutre ». Les récits que nous faisons de la vie des singes racontent aussi les humains qui les écrivent.
Dans Primate visions (1989), Donna Haraway porte un énorme coup à la conception de l’objectivité, telle qu’elle était alors en vigueur dans la science. Elle a conduit de nombreux auteurs et autrices à s’interroger sur la façon dont leurs identités coloraient leurs récits et à identifier des regards dominants (voir notre enquête « Les journalistes [se] racontent » p. 14). Les centres de données mettent la Belgique sous tension
Texte (CC BY-NC-ND) : Maïté Warland & Quentin Noirfalisse
Photos : Nick Hannes
Texte (CC BY-NC-ND) : Janine Meijer
Publié le
La Belgique se rêve en grand hub numérique, en terre d’accueil idéale pour les centres de données (data centers). Depuis vingt ans, Google a montré la voie, en s’installant à Saint-Ghislain, au nord du Borinage. L’expansion rapide du géant américain soulève des enjeux majeurs : pression sur le réseau électrique, manque de transparence et retombées économiques floues. L’intelligence artificielle (IA) accélère l’implantation de ces usines numériques et met notre pays sous tension.
Du fond de son jardin, Anne More contemple la vue. Devant elle, de l’autre côté de la Rue des Roseaux, de grands bâtiments gris barrent le ciel. Elle vit à 200 mètres du centre de données de Google à Saint-Ghislain, à l’ouest du Hainaut. À 68 ans, elle doit composer avec ce voisin installé ici depuis une vingtaine d’années : « Là, ils sont en train de bâtir une nouvelle extension, ça cause pas mal de soucis. Du bruit d’abord… J’ai même acheté un casque pour ne plus les entendre. » De la rue du Marais, où elle vit, il ne reste aujourd’hui que le nom : « Avant, c’était magnifique, aujourd’hui, il n’y a plus que du béton et ils se rapprochent de plus en plus. » Cette cohabitation forcée, Anne ne la comprend toujours pas : « On ne sait rien. Google construit, agrandit, et on a à peine été consulté. Je ne sais même pas ce qu’ils font alors qu’ils sont presque au fond de mon jardin. »
Ici, Google et sa société faitière Alphabet développent depuis 2007 leur premier data center européen. Vingt-quatre heures sur 24, des dizaines, voire des centaines de milliers de serveurs travaillent pour lancer les vidéos que vous regardez sur YouTube, récupérer une pièce jointe sur votre Gmail, activer le résultat d’une recherche Google. Les journalistes se (la) racontent
Enquête (CC BY-NC-ND) : Chloé Andries & Céline Gautier
Illustrations (CC BY-NC-ND) : Jérôme Degive
Publié le
En 2026, les podcasts parlent de nos grands-mères, les BD de nos vies intimes et les docus de nos photos de famille. Jadis, l’idéal journalistique exigeait que l’auteur s’efface derrière son sujet. Que nous est-il arrivé ?
« Il y a six ans, mon compagnon me dit qu’il ne souhaite plus avoir d’enfant. » La journaliste Lucie Tesnière lance son podcast (Juste une femme) consacré aux femmes qui n’ont pas d’enfants par un témoignage fort. Le sien.
« Ma mère Nathalie mourra dans deux ans. Mon fils naitra dans neuf mois. » La caméra de Caroline Guimbal ne fait pas 50 fois le tour du monde : la documentariste explore la vie de sa mère, avant qu’elle ne meure et que naisse son enfant (L’éclipse de la lune rouge).
« Mon ami Michel me tend un paquet. Cinq carnets. » Les notes de tranchées de son grand-oncle. « C’est toute une famille que j’accueille, sans le savoir, dans ma maison. » L’écrivaine Violaine Lison commence une vaste enquête historique et littéraire (« Lequel de nous portera l’autre ? ») qui mêle sa voix à celle d’un soldat inconnu.
Ces trois exemples sont tout récents (2026). Nous pourrions en trouver plein d’autres. Partout, des auteurs (et surtout des autrices) ne se contentent plus de mener des enquêtes mais nous en dévoilent les coulisses, se positionnent dans leurs récits, voire s’emparent de leurs propres histoires de famille.
Ce mouvement touche depuis plusieurs décennies l’anthropologie, la sociologie, l’histoire ou encore la littérature du réel et, depuis belle lurette, le cinéma documentaire. Mais ce qui est neuf, c’est l’ampleur inédite du phénomène et le fait qu’il touche désormais les journalistes – un métier spécifique, …

L’exil sans sexualité
Faire l’amour dans un centre d’accueil de demandeurs d’asile, ce n’est pas interdit. Mais dans la pratique, c’est presque impossible. Une absence d’intimité qui rend le parcours migratoire un peu plus lourd à supporter.
À leur arrivée en Belgique, les personnes migrantes se cognent à : des procédures administratives sans fin, un logement précaire, les traumas de l’exil et le racisme. Dans ce contexte, la sexualité passe souvent au second plan. Pourtant, l’intimité est aussi un droit essentiel au bienêtre. L’article 8 de la Convention européenne des droits de l’homme stipule que « toute personne a droit au respect de sa vie privée et familiale, de son domicile et de sa correspondance ». Il régit donc le droit pour tous et toutes à une vie affective, intime et sexuelle. Dans le système d’accueil en Belgique, ce droit peine pourtant à être garanti, relégué derrière l’urgence et le manque de moyens.
L’intimité face au collectif
Tamer est un réfugié gazaoui reconnu depuis peu. Durant sa procédure, il a vécu dans quatre hébergements différents : « En fonction du centre, j’ai partagé ma chambre avec trois à douze personnes et les visites étaient toujours interdites, il n’y avait pas d’intimité.
