https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/la.title: Laura Hoptman Wins CCS Bard’s 2027 Audrey Irmas Award for Curatorial Excellence
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/la.author: Anne Doran
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/la.text:
The Center for Curatorial Studies at Bard College (CCS Bard) has given its 2027 Audrey Irmas Award for Curatorial Excellence to Laura Hoptman, executive director of New York’s Drawing Center. She will receive $25,000 and will be honored at CCS Bard’s spring gala in April.
Hoptman joined the Drawing Center in 2018 following eight years as a curator in the department of painting and sculpture at the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA). While at MoMA, she oversaw major traveling exhibitions devoted to Isa Genzken (2013) and Bruce Conner (2016), as well as the museum’s hotly debated survey of contemporary painting, “The Forever Now” (2014–2015).
After beginning her career as an assistant curator at the Bronx Museum, Hoptman worked as an assistant curator in MoMA’s department of drawings from 1996 to 2002. In 2003 she guest-curated “Drawing Now: Eight Propositions,” featuring more than 200 representational works by 26 contemporary artists, at MoMA QNS, and in 2004 she was director of the 54th Carnegie International in Pittsburgh. Between 2006 and 2010 she was senior curator at the New Museum in New York, where she co-organized “Unmonumental: The Object in the 21st Century” (2007–2008) and “The Generational: Younger than Jesus” (2009).
The Audrey Irmas Award has been given annually since 1998 and recognizes “groundbreaking visionaries in the curatorial field,” according to a press release. Past recipients include Adriano Pedrosa, Connie Butler, Carolyn Christov-Bakargiev, Thelma Golden, and Okwui Enwezor.
“Laura’s longstanding curatorial practice has furthered new art historical analysis and international recognition of drawing as a creative medium and social practice,” said CCS Bard executive director Tom Eccles in a statement. “Her international projects have reexamined the legacies of an array of artists through new and creative frameworks. What is often forgotten is how consistently Laura has demonstrated a boldness and bravery in championing artists across many institutional structures.”

https://taz.de/Geldstrafe-fuer-Neonazi/!.title: Geldstrafe für Neonazi: Szenegröße wegen Volksverhetzung verurteilt
https://taz.de/Geldstrafe-fuer-Neonazi/!.author: Joachim F. Tornau
https://taz.de/Geldstrafe-fuer-Neonazi/!.text:
Geldstrafe für Neonazi: Szenegröße wegen Volksverhetzung verurteilt
Der Neonazi Thorsten Heise wurde nach elf Anläufen wegen Volksverhetzung verurteilt. Er hatte Kleidung mit NS-verherrlichenden Aufschriften verkauft.
Katharina König-Preuss konnte eine gewisse Genugtuung nicht verhehlen. „Das Justizwunder Thorsten Heise“, sagte die thüringische Linkenpolitikerin, „ist kein Justizwunder mehr.“ Heise, 57 Jahre alt und Vizevorsitzender der Neonazi-Partei „Die Heimat“ (Ex-NPD), darf als eine der einflussreichsten Figuren des militanten Rechtsextremismus in Deutschland gelten. Als Kameradschaftsführer, Rechtsrockproduzent, Versandhändler, Verleger und international vernetzter Strippenzieher. Strafrechtlich aber blieb er seit vielen Jahren seltsam unbehelligt. Bis jetzt.
Am Donnerstag wurde der braune Multiaktivist wegen Volksverhetzung zu einer Geldstrafe von 4.500 Euro (90 Tagessätze à 50 Euro) verurteilt. Das Amtsgericht im thüringischen Heiligenstadt wertete es als „Bezug auf die Boykottpolitik der Nationalsozialisten“, dass Heise über seinen Onlineshop T-Shirts und Pullover mit dem Logo der NS-Organisation „Arbeitsgemeinschaft deutsch-arischer Bekleidungsfabrikanten“ (Adefa) angeboten hatte, versehen mit dem Slogan „Ware aus arischer Hand“.
Heise behauptete, das habe bloß ein „Gag“ sein sollen, passend zum T-Shirt-Motiv seiner mittlerweile aufgelösten Neonazi-Kameradschaft „Arische Bruderschaft“. Wortreich beteuerte er, nichts vom nationalsozialistischen Hintergrund des Vereins gewusst zu haben. Und überhaupt beziehe sich „arisch“ ja nicht nur auf „diese zwölf Jahre“, wie er die NS-Herrschaft umschrieb, sondern auf die gesamte indogermanische Sprachfamilie: „Auch Perser fallen unter diesen Begriff.“
Richter glaubt Heise nicht
Das nahm ihm Richter Christian Gras nicht ab: „Das Gericht ist überzeugt, dass Sie wussten, was Sie da machten.“ Auch dass Heise die fraglichen Kleidungsstücke zweimal nach Beschlagnahmungen von den Behörden wieder zurückgegeben worden waren, habe der Angeklagte nicht als Freifahrtschein missverstehen dürfen.
Gleichwohl blieb das Gericht deutlich unter der neunmonatigen Bewährungsstrafe, die die Staatsanwaltschaft gefordert hatte. Von „zutiefst antisemitischer Propaganda“ hatte Oberstaatsanwalt Benedikt Ballhausen gesprochen und Heises Treiben als „Diskriminierungsmaschinerie“ bezeichnet. Verteidiger Andreas Wölfel, ein bekannter rechtsextremer Szeneanwalt, plädierte auf Freispruch und kündigte Berufung an.
Die Verhandlung war bereits der elfte Anlauf. Seit 2022 wurden zehn Termine vom Gericht kurzfristig wieder aufgehoben. Nur im November 2024 traf man sich einmal zur Verhandlung – mit der Folge, dass zwei von ursprünglich drei Anklagen eingestellt wurden. So waren etwa Hakenkreuze, die Heise auf seinem Anwesen in Fretterode hatte anbringen lassen, dem Gericht für eine Verurteilung nicht rechtwinklig genug gewesen.
Nicht die einzige Anklage
Unterdessen droht dem vormaligen Justizwunder neues juristisches Ungemach. Eine Anklage wegen des Handels mit volksverhetzender Musik und des unerlaubten Besitzes einer Schusswaffe wartet beim Amtsgericht Heiligenstadt noch auf ihn. Im März soll Heise zudem zusammen mit seinem gleichgesinnten Sohn Thoralf ein Team von „Spiegel TV“ in Fretterode angegriffen haben.
Das Ermittlungsverfahren wegen gefährlicher Körperverletzung und Verstoßes gegen das Waffengesetz steht nach Angaben der Staatsanwaltschaft Mühlhausen kurz vor dem Abschluss. Wegen einer blutigen Attacke auf Journalisten im April 2018 muss sich derzeit bereits Heises älterer Sohn Nordulf zusammen mit einem weiteren Neonazi aus dem Heise-Umfeld in Mühlhausen vor dem Landgericht verantworten.
Gegen Thorsten Heise sind außerdem Betrugsermittlungen anhängig. Es geht um ein dubioses Millionenerbe, das sich der Neonazi-Führer verschafft haben soll, indem er eine mutmaßlich schwer demente 90-Jährige heimlich aus Schweden nach Fretterode geholt und sich dann als Alleinerbe habe einsetzen lassen. Wie die Staatsanwaltschaft Mühlhausen mitteilte, wird noch geprüft, ob die deutsche oder die schwedische Justiz für den Fall zuständig ist.
Gemeinsam für freie Presse
Die taz gehört zu 100 Prozent ihren Leser:innen und ist damit nicht nur konzernfrei, sondern auch kostenfrei zugänglich. Alle Artikel stellen wir frei zur Verfügung, ohne Paywall. Gerade in diesen Zeiten müssen Einordnungen und Informationen allen zugänglich sein. Unsere Leser:innen müssen nichts bezahlen, wissen aber, dass kritischer, unabhängiger Journalismus nicht aus dem Nichts entsteht. Dafür sind wir sehr dankbar. Damit wir auch morgen noch unseren Journalismus machen können, brauchen wir mehr Unterstützung für taz zahl ich. Dank Ihnen haben wir nun die 50.000 erreicht. https://jacobin.com/2026/11/le-pen-far-r.title: The Violent Far-Right Response to France’s Protests
https://jacobin.com/2026/11/le-pen-far-r.author: Olly Haynes
https://jacobin.com/2026/11/le-pen-far-r.text:
The Violent Far-Right Response to France’s Protests
In recent weeks, French far-right militants have carried out several violent attacks. While media focus on young rioters breaking shop windows, they ignore the reactionaries who use deadly force against minorities and left-wingers.
For France’s media-political classes, the recent student movement has prompted a series of searching questions about violence and who has the right to use it. Debates often center on the alleged closeness of protesters to La France Insoumise, implying that Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s left-wing party is somehow responsible for vandalism by protesters and marginal acts of violence by students. Less remarked upon however, is that a wave of violence coming from the far right has also marked the protests and the presidential election campaign. Nor has it been much noted that this violence has killed already, and that Marine Le Pen’s Rassemblement National (RN) is alarmingly close to the violent groupuscules involved.
Already on October 24, far-right militants attacked trade unionists and protesters in Rouen, Nice, and Montpellier. In a video taken by a bystander in Rouen, Normandy, members of local identitarian movement Les Normaux can be seen throwing a man to the pavement before kicking him. None of the men were arrested by the police, although officers were present on the scene. The identitarians attempted to intimidate protesters by yelling far-right slogans such as “Rouen, Rouen is nationalist” and “the street and France belongs to us.”
The group had launched similar attacks on protesters the week before, beating two people to the ground and leaving them bloody. In a video taken before the incident, a man can be seen at the head of their march, a leather belt wrapped around his fist, metal buckle in hand like a makeshift knuckle-duster. Street Press, a news website that closely monitors far-right activity, identified the man as Mathieu Balavoine, who runs a production company that was hired by the Rassemblement National in 2024, and that last year earned over €100,000 for a contract making videos for the party’s group in the European Parliament.
The far right’s propensity for lethal violence has also been demonstrated elsewhere in recent weeks. On October 23, Kevin Tessier, a coked-up fascist armed with an automatic weapon, fired 128 bullets at black and Arab people in the city of Trappes, killing one person and injuring four. Trappes had repeatedly been the subject of a media moral panic about “territories lost to the Republic” because of their large minority populations. Le Pen contributed to this over the years, tweeting in 2018 following a stabbing in the city, that Trappes is “the symbol of those cities and neighborhoods where the French Republic has retreated, making way for communalism and Islamism.” Tessier’s motives were undeniably racist. Whether he was influenced directly by Le Pen’s words is unknown, but stickers found in his house suggest that he was at least a party sympathizer. Among a copy of Adolf Hitler’s Mein Kampf and other items indicative of his far-right ideology, were thirty stickers bearing the words “Long Live France, the RN, proud to be French.”
These were just the most recent instances of a longer story of far-right violence in France. In 2022 Argentine rugby player Federico Martín Aramburú was gunned down in the street by two former members of the Groupe Union Défense (GUD), a fascist youth circle with close ties to the RN. In 2023, a wave of far-right violence was unleashed in reaction to the Nahel Merzouk riots, which followed the police killing of a seventeen-year-old. That year, France became the only European country to see a major increase in the number of violent attacks by far-right groups compared to the 2010–2022 national average, according to a study by the Center for Research on Extremism. Since then, acts of violence by such groups targeting ethnic minorities and political opponents have become increasingly common. According to daily Libération, there was an average of one far-right attack per week in 2025.
The groups perpetrating these attacks — the formations that emerged following the self-dissolution of the GUD and the mandatory dissolution of Génération Identitaire — are alarmingly close to the RN.
According to Thomas Portes, who is president of the National Observatory of the Far Right, and France Insoumise MP for Saint-Denis, “There has been no break between the parliamentary far right and the groupuscules.”
[In France] we have an annual mobilization by the May 9 Committee; it’s a Nazi demonstration in homage to a fascist activist who died. It was banned this year, but two years ago, the paperwork for the demonstration was filed by a parliamentary attaché for the RN, called Maylis de Cibon. There was a parliamentary assistant called Raphaël Ayma, who spoke at a conference of the friends of Léon Degrelle, a Belgian Nazi figure [before Ayma was expelled from the RN]. There is the press secretary of the RN group, Elise Laplace, who has just married a neofascist activist that arranged an attack on a political meeting in Bordeaux that was organized by my fellow [France Insoumise] MPs Louis Boyard and Carlos Martens Bilongo.
“It goes beyond the assistants,” Portes tells Jacobin, pointing to the case of Tiffany Joncour, an RN MP whose husband, a hooligan with a background in the identitarian movement, beat up her parliamentary assistant whom he suspected of having an affair with her.
Portes’s list continues, telling Jacobin about four further examples. Even this list is not exhaustive. While researching another article, in the Eurocom forum that the group organizes through, I found an account of the Save Europe Act, an organization linking identitarian movements across Europe, which includes several groupuscules accused of violence. The account bore the name and location of Philippe Eymery, an RN regional counselor whose party branch was exposed in 2018 for employing Génération Identitaire activists. Eymery recently appeared on a radio show alongside various extreme-right groups that are members of the Eurocom group, promoting remigration. (He did not respond to my message requests on Twitter attempting to confirm if he was the owner of the account with his name.)
At France Insoumise’s own summer university in August, the party’s parliamentary chief Mathilde Panot told journalists that this would be an unusual presidential election campaign because of the level of violence that she and her colleagues expected. Her assessment has already proved prescient, though France Insoumise has in fact long been a target for far-right violence. The Trappes killer had a list suggesting he was intending to target France Insoumise MPs David Guiraud and Aymeric Caron, as well as anti-police-violence campaigner Assa Traoré and Green MP Sandrine Rousseau. France Insoumise canvassers and parliamentary assistants have been beaten up while campaigning for Mélenchon, and even the Quentin Deranque affair, which ended with a neo-Nazi activist dying from injuries sustained in a street fight by antifascist activists, began with fascist activists ambushing the antifascist activists outside a France Insoumise meeting in Lyon.
According to Portes, there is an “operation to reverse society’s moral compass based on falsehoods, which is targeted against us. For example, yesterday the minister of education tried to claim that it was France Insoumise, our activists and officials, who brought fireworks to high school students to allow them to fire them at school buildings. The interior minister was forced to deny it today. . . . As for the far right, we represent everything that they hate. That is to say the imaginary of an anti-racist, anti-colonial, antifascist, egalitarian, New France.”
Part of Marine Le Pen’s strategy of detoxification has been to expel party members associated with openly extreme or violent groups in French politics. However, they only seem to be expelled when the press gets wind of it, and even then those close to the leader can escape unscathed. The Rassemblement National in parliament with the “shirts and ties” is just “decor” and “window dressing” says Portes. “When you look at the list of people who are elected officials for the RN, or their assistants, it’s a nursery of neo-Nazi, nationalist, royalist, and identitarian activists.”
Le Pen may have successfully detoxified the party brand. That doesn’t, however, mean that it has actually changed.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.title: Meninas livres, vivas e sem violência
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.author: Coluna das Inclusivass
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.text:
Hoje começam os 21 Dias de Ativismo pelo Fim da Violência contra as Mulheres e Meninas. São dias de mobilização, memória, denúncia e luta, que nos convocam a refletir sobre as diferentes formas de violência, reafirmar direitos e fortalecer ações para que mulheres e meninas possam viver livres de qualquer forma de opressão.
Para nós, do Movimento Feminista Inclusivass, essa mobilização começa nos territórios, nas comunidades e, especialmente, nos espaços de educação. Porque enfrentar a violência também significa chegar antes que ela aconteça, reconhecer suas manifestações cotidianas e construir caminhos para transformar as relações sociais.
No dia 23 de novembro, realizaremos a Caminhada Elas pelo Fim da Violência contra as Mulheres e Meninas, na comunidade Chapéu do Sol, em parceria com a Escola Municipal de Ensino Fundamental Chapéu do Sol, por meio do projeto Elas em Rede – Escola sem Violência, com apoio do Fundo Elas+.
Essa caminhada tem um significado que ultrapassa a realização de uma atividade comunitária. Ela acontece em um território diretamente atravessado pela violência contra as mulheres. Somente neste ano, três mulheres foram vítimas de feminicídio no Extremo Sul de Porto Alegre, além de uma tentativa de feminicídio na própria comunidade Chapéu do Sol. São acontecimentos que não podem ser tratados como números distantes. São vidas, famílias e comunidades atingidas por uma violência que exige respostas permanentes.
No Rio Grande do Sul, o cenário também é alarmante. O Observatório de Feminicídios Lupa Feminista confirmou 80 vítimas de feminicídio no estado até 11 de novembro de 2026. Seu monitoramento também evidencia diferenças em relação aos registros oficiais, reforçando a importância da atuação da sociedade civil na identificação, visibilidade e análise dos feminicídios.
A violência contra mulheres e meninas não começa no feminicídio. Ela está presente nas desigualdades, no machismo, no controle dos corpos e das escolhas, nas relações abusivas, nas ameaças, na misoginia e nas diferentes formas de violação de direitos. Muitas dessas manifestações também estão presentes na vida das adolescentes e nas relações que estabelecem dentro e fora da escola.
É nesse contexto que nasce o Elas em Rede – Escola sem Violência, uma experiência pioneira na trajetória do Movimento Feminista Inclusivass e uma proposta inovadora de formação e prevenção da violência de gênero no ambiente escolar.
O projeto chega à escola porque compreendemos que a misoginia não está apenas nas ruas, nas redes sociais ou nas relações afetivas. Ela também se manifesta no cotidiano escolar, nas falas, nas atitudes, nas brincadeiras que constrangem, na desvalorização das meninas, nas relações de poder e nos comportamentos machistas reproduzidos por meninos. Muitas vezes, essas manifestações são naturalizadas, tratadas como brincadeiras ou conflitos entre estudantes, sem que se reconheça a violência que carregam.
Não podemos esperar que a violência se agrave para começar a conversar. Precisamos criar espaços de escuta, formação e reflexão, onde meninas reconheçam seus direitos e meninos sejam convidados a questionar comportamentos, rever atitudes e compreender que respeito, consentimento e igualdade também precisam fazer parte das relações dentro da escola.
Por isso, uma das escolhas políticas e pedagógicas do Elas em Rede foi incluir meninas e meninos nos processos formativos. Precisamos conversar com os meninos! O enfrentamento à violência contra mulheres e meninas não pode ser uma responsabilidade exclusiva das mulheres. É necessário discutir masculinidades, questionar padrões machistas, desconstruir comportamentos que reproduzem desigualdades e envolver os meninos na construção de novas relações sociais.
O pioneirismo da experiência está também na amplitude de sua proposta. Não trabalhamos apenas a violência digital. Construímos um processo integrado de prevenção e enfrentamento à violência de gênero, articulando formação, pesquisa, produção de conhecimento, comunicação, participação juvenil, legislação, direitos e incidência política.
Desde julho, o projeto vem desenvolvendo oficinas com estudantes, pesquisas sobre o uso das redes sociais e as percepções sobre a violência, concurso de artes visuais, debates sobre direitos e mecanismos de denúncia e proteção, além da produção de materiais educativos, entre eles a Cartilha Elas em Rede – Escola sem Violência.
A violência digital ocupa um lugar importante nessa construção porque as adolescentes também enfrentam misoginia, cyberbullying, exposição sem consentimento, ameaças, assédio e outras formas de violência facilitadas pelas tecnologias. Essas violências não ficam restritas às telas: atravessam as relações, chegam à escola e afetam a liberdade, a autonomia e a vida das meninas.
O projeto foi conduzido por Carol Santos, ativista, liderança feminista e sobrevivente de tentativa de feminicídio, uma das coordenadoras do Elas em Rede. Sua condução trouxe o desafio de construir um processo educativo com adolescentes a partir de uma perspectiva pedagógica, feminista, antirracista e anticapacitista, reconhecendo que as meninas não vivem a violência da mesma forma e que as desigualdades também atravessam as experiências de cada adolescente.
Já são quase 30 encontros de formação com os jovens multiplicadores. Julio Roberth, Valentina, Ricardo, Lauryn e Lorenzo deram vida a este projeto! Com dedicação, curiosidade e compromisso, participaram de uma construção coletiva na qual aprenderam, compartilharam conhecimentos, desenvolveram autonomia e fortaleceram suas vozes.
A formação ultrapassou os encontros presenciais. Os jovens também assumiram um papel ativo na comunicação do projeto, conduzindo as redes sociais do Elas em Rede e aprendendo sobre comunicação digital, produção audiovisual, acessibilidade, criação de conteúdos e estratégias para dialogar com outros adolescentes.
Aprenderam que comunicar também é uma forma de participação política. Produzir conteúdos, compartilhar informações sobre direitos, construir narrativas e pensar em acessibilidade são maneiras de ocupar espaços, ampliar vozes e enfrentar violências. A perspectiva anticapacitista esteve presente nessa construção, reafirmando que a comunicação precisa garantir diferentes formas de acesso, participação e expressão.
Julio Roberth, Valentina, Ricardo, Lauryn e Lorenzo não foram apenas participantes de uma formação. Foram jovens multiplicadores, comunicadores e protagonistas de uma experiência que também os transformou. São parte de um processo que reconhece adolescentes como sujeitos de direitos, produtores de conhecimento e agentes de transformação social.
Para o Movimento Feminista Inclusivass, o Elas em Rede representa um passo importante na ampliação de nossa atuação política e pedagógica. É a afirmação de que o enfrentamento à violência precisa estar presente na educação, que a prevenção exige investimento em formação e que adolescentes precisam participar das decisões e das transformações que dizem respeito às suas vidas.
Ao longo dos 21 Dias de Ativismo, seguiremos com rodas de conversa, formação com professoras e professores, homenagem aos jovens multiplicadores, lançamento da Cartilha Elas em Rede – Escola sem Violência e ações de comunicação e mobilização.
Mas queremos que essa construção vá muito além dos 21 dias. Queremos que o debate permaneça nas escolas, nas famílias, nas comunidades e nas políticas públicas. Queremos redes de proteção fortalecidas, educação comprometida com os direitos humanos e adolescentes reconhecidas como protagonistas de suas próprias histórias.
Nosso grito nestes 21 dias é por meninas LIVRES, VIVAS E SEM VIOLÊNCIA!
Queremos meninas que possam ocupar todos os espaços, inclusive o digital, sem medo, sem violência, sem discriminação e sem precisar abrir mão de sua liberdade para estarem protegidas.
Não queremos meninas fora das redes para estarem seguras. Queremos uma internet feminista, livre de misoginia, machismo, racismo, capacitismo e todas as formas de violência. Queremos escolas sem violência e uma sociedade onde meninas e mulheres possam viver plenamente, com autonomia, dignidade, liberdade e direitos.
Porque proteger também é educar. Prevenir é transformar. E enfrentar a violência é uma responsabilidade coletiva.
**Este é um artigo de opinião e não necessariamente representa a linha editorial do Brasil de Fato.

https://gothamist.com/news/mayor-mamdani.title: Mayor Mamdani signs NYC's carriage horse ban after decades of animal rights activism
https://gothamist.com/news/mayor-mamdani.author: Liam Quigley
https://gothamist.com/news/mayor-mamdani.text:
Animal rights activists who fought for decades to ban the city’s 160-year-old horse-drawn carriage industry were handed a major victory on Thursday when Mayor Zohran Mamdani signed a bill banning the practice.
A turning point in the push to ban the industry came over the summer when an 18-year-old visiting from India with his family was thrown from a carriage in Central Park after its driver lost control of the animal. Romanch Mahajan was killed in the crash, which left the smashed-up carriage in the middle of the park’s drive. The horse was uninjured. But other horses have died on the streets of the city, their deaths captured in gruesome viral videos that were fodder for animal rights groups.
The bill to ban the industry passed the City Council last month.
The carriage horse industry maintains that the animals are well cared for and beloved by the 200 or so people who drive and care for them. Drivers now face an uncertain future with their careers set to come to an end by June 2028, when the law requires the industry to be banished from the park.
Carriage owners have city-issued medallions to operate, much like taxi drivers.
The city plans to buy back medallions from the carriage owners and launch a training program for the drivers and stable hands. Details on the buybacks and job training aren't due until April 2027.
“As New York City moves to bring the horse-drawn carriage industry to a close, we have a responsibility to the workers who have built careers in this industry,” the mayor wrote in a statement accompanying a Tuesday announcement. “This administration will not leave them behind.”
The Transport Workers Union has bitterly fought the move to ban the industry. They argue the city’s promises are unfunded and have vowed to file a lawsuit the moment the mayor signed the law.
The union's president, John Samuelesen, said in a statement that the law is unconstitutional.
“The City Council passed a horrifically flawed and unconstitutional anti-worker bill that abolishes an entire industry without any funding, mandates, or guarantees,” he wrote. He added that if the city faces a fiscal crisis, the whole plan could easily be abandoned.
“That would leave hundreds of horse-carriage workers, owners, and family members on the curb with nothing at all.”

https://www.propublica.org/article/tarif.title: We’re Publishing the Tariff Refunds the Government Has Refused to Disclose
https://www.propublica.org/article/tarif.author: Kevin Uhrmacher, Nick McMillan
https://www.propublica.org/article/tarif.text:
After President Donald Trump’s “emergency” tariffs were overturned by the Supreme Court in February 2026, the government began processing billions in refunds to importers, including many recognizable public companies.
The Trump administration has not publicly detailed which companies are getting roughly $170 billion in refunds or how much they’ve asked for. ProPublica requested the information, but U.S. Customs and Border Protection denied our requests. (We’re appealing.)
So our reporters found another way: analyzing the financial disclosures of thousands of publicly traded companies.
Today, ProPublica published “Cash Back,” a database of figures on refunds for tariffs paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. The database includes 343 public companies for which we found mentions of refunds, amounting to more than $28 billion recovered or expected.
At least nine companies have disclosed that they are using their refunds not to pay back the cash-strapped consumers who generally covered much of the tariff costs through higher prices, but to give bonuses, according to a ProPublica analysis published earlier this week.
Recognizable businesses include the tool company Stanley Black & Decker and the owners of discount department stores TJ Maxx and Marshalls, and the golf equipment brand Titleist.
Many other firms have said little about how they plan to use the money.
ProPublica’s examination of tariff refunds was limited to publicly traded companies, which are required to disclose detailed financial information. None of the companies that said they are using the money for bonuses have ever said they planned to refund customers. How private companies are using their refunds is unclear because they aren’t normally required to disclose such information.
Explore the Cash Back database here.
What’s included in the database?
The Supreme Court ruled on Feb. 20, 2026, that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act doesn’t authorize the president to impose tariffs. The U.S. Court of International Trade ordered U.S. Customs and Border Protection to refund the duties it had collected.
This tracker covers refunds on those tariffs disclosed by publicly traded companies. Public companies must disclose events that affect their finances, such as tariff payments and refunds, on earnings calls and in regular reports filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission. We collected information from these public sources through Oct. 7, 2026.
Before publishing, we contacted all companies shown here to check the accuracy of the numbers we had found.
We grouped companies by industry using a combination of designations from Morningstar.
How did we determine refund amounts?
ProPublica searched through securities filings and earnings calls using key phrases to isolate companies that mentioned tariff refunds. For each company, we created a document that included the extracted text around each phrase. For SEC filings, that included parsed Extensible Business Reporting Language when available.
We then used an open-weight artificial intelligence model for a first pass at identifying refund amounts. ProPublica reporters reviewed each company by hand to make sure our database is accurate and contacted all companies to confirm the amounts.
Companies normally record tariff refunds in their financial statements under two accounting models:
- Gain contingency: when the refund has been received or recovery is essentially certain.
- Loss recovery: when the refund is probable and can be reasonably estimated.
To determine a company’s recovered refund, we added up the amounts it recorded that were essentially certain or probable (sometimes known as “receivable”), plus the amounts it disclosed as having been received.
The government is required to pay interest on tariff amounts it is returning, at rates determined by the IRS on a quarterly basis. Companies disclosed that interest in different ways. Some reported the refund and the interest separately, while others reported a single amount that included both. When a company reported them separately, we added the interest to the refund to capture the full amount of money that a company was receiving from the government.
Some companies reported only their net refund instead of the full amount received. For example, a company might report only what was left of the tariff refund after reinvesting into its business or after passing part of the refund onto customers. In these cases, we reported the net amount. When companies reported a range, we used the lower end. In both cases, we noted that information on the company page.
The specific security filings reviewed were: 8-K, 10-Q, 10-K, 8-K/A, 10-Q/A, 10-K/A, 6-K, 6-K/A, 20-F, 20-F/A, 40-F, 40-F/A and any associated exhibits.
Can I get a refund?
Only importers or the authorized custom brokers who filed the entries can submit a request for a refund. That means that even if companies passed tariff costs on to customers through higher prices, the refund goes to the company, and it is up to the company to determine how the money is used.
UPS and FedEx are itemizing how much customers paid in tariffs and reimbursing them. The companies have set up online portals for customers to track their refunds. Though the firms are technically importers of record, they imported goods on behalf of businesses and individuals who paid them to ship products.
Other companies have said that they will be splitting at least some of their refund checks with their customers, though these companies’ customers are generally other businesses. Trade experts say these business-to-business vendors likely have detailed contracts that itemize tariff costs.
Some companies have described vague plans to pay the money forward by, for example, “returning tariff refunds to our members through pricing,” though they generally don’t say whether that involves price cuts or limiting future increases.
How do I report incorrect information?
If you see information that may be incorrect, please email [email protected].
We will periodically update our database by pulling information from newer filings, as well as correcting or adding new information when companies reach out to us.
Can I download the data?
Yes, you can download the data here. We ask that you credit “ProPublica analysis of financial disclosures” and link to this tracker.
Do you have information you can share about how a company is using tariff refunds?
ProPublica’s investigative journalists are reporting on tariff refunds and how, or if, companies are giving money back to consumers. You can reach our tip line or contact us on Signal at 917-512-0201. Please be as specific, detailed and clear as you can.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120400.title: Rassismus / Pseudowissenschaft | Nach dem Tod Jason Ardays lädt Oxford Nathan Cofnas ein
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120400.author: Julian Daum
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120400.text:
- Politik
- Rassismus / Pseudowissenschaft
Nach dem Tod Jason Ardays lädt Oxford Nathan Cofnas ein
Professor Jason Arday wurde in den Rücktritt und möglicherweise in den Tod getrieben. Sein Ankläger Nathan Cofnas darf rassistische Vorträge in Oxford halten.
Professor Jason Arday hat nicht mehr miterlebt, wie sein Ankläger Nathan Cofnas an der Universität Oxford sprach und dort am Dienstag seine rassistischen Thesen verbreitete. Träfen die Ansichten Cofnas’ zu, wäre Arday in einer Welt ohne vermeintlich künstlich konstruierte Gleichheitsvorstellungen als Schwarzer Mann wahrscheinlich kein Professor in Cambridge geworden. Denn Cofnas hält Schwarze Menschen im Durchschnitt für weniger intelligent und führt das in seiner Lehre fernab und entgegen wissenschaftlicher Erkenntnisse darauf zurück, dass eben nicht alle Ethnien (auf Englisch oft »race«) dieselben Voraussetzungen mitbrächten.
Heute ist Soziologie-Professor Jason Arday tot. Cofnas hatte ihm im Sommer Plagiarismus und verfälschte Studienergebnisse vorgeworfen, woraufhin eine riesige Welle auch internationaler Berichterstattung losbrach, die – flankiert von Politiker*innen und Social Media – in erheblichen Teilen von Anfeindungen durchsetzt war. Anfang August trat Arday von seinem Posten in Cambridge zurück, begründete das mit den »unerbittlichen Vorwürfen, Spekulationen und öffentlichen Kommentierungen«, die »für mich und diejenigen, die ich liebe, zu einer erheblichen Belastung geworden sind.« Neun Tage später wurde er tot aufgefunden. Von den Vorwürfen wurde Arday mittlerweile durch mehrere Untersuchungen entlastet.
Der selbsternannte »Rassenrealist« Nathan Cofnas scheint all diese Vorgänge nicht auf sich zu beziehen, er wolle sich auch bei der Familie Ardays nicht entschuldigen. Denn das bedeute ja, dass man mächtige Personen nicht kritisieren dürfe. Seiner eigenen Deutungsmacht und Einflusskraft unbewusst, sagte er das auf der Veranstaltung in Oxford, zu der er auch aufgrund seiner in den vergangenen Monaten gewonnenen Bekanntheit eingeladen worden war. Die Einladung ausgesprochen hatte die studentische Vereinigung »Oxford Reform«, die mit der Rechtsaußen-Partei »Reform UK« verbunden ist.
Titel des Vortrags: »Untergräbt DEI die Hochschulbildung?« DEI steht für Vielfalt, Chancengleichheit und Inklusion. Laut »Guardian« war der Saal mit etwa 40 Personen gefüllt, die einer Art Zusammenfassung seiner vergangenen Arbeit zuhörten: Es ging um die angeblich vorherrschende Ideologie der »Gleichheit aller Ethnien« und seine Argumente dagegen.
Ohne Mikrofon wäre er wohl schwer zu verstehen gewesen, so laut waren Hunderte Protestierende vor dem Oriel College. Sie brachten vor der Tür ihre Wut darüber zum Ausdruck, dass Cofnas an der Universität seine rassistischen Thesen verlautbaren dürfe, als seien es gleichberechtigte Argumente in einem wissenschaftlichen Austausch und dass Oxford das zugelassen hatte. Die Universität sagte in einem Statement etwas dünn, dass es sich um keine offizielle Univeranstaltung gehandelt habe. Die Protestierenden begrüßten Cofnas daraufhin in der Nähe des Eingangs mit einer Puppe in Ku-Klux-Klan-Optik, die ein Schild hält mit der Aufschrift: »Rassisten sind hier willkommen«.
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.
Keine Paywall, kein Kleingedrucktes, nur ein Ziel: dass nd bleibt.

https://www.thenation.com/article/politi.title: How College Students Helped Turn Texas Blue
https://www.thenation.com/article/politi.author: Lajward Zahra
https://www.thenation.com/article/politi.text:
How College Students Helped Turn Texas Blue
After years of Republican dominance, Texas Democrats won statewide with overwhelming support from young voters.
By the time Beto O’Rourke arrived at Sam Houston State University in Huntsville, Texas on October 14, Alyssa Rodriguez had spent weeks preparing for his visit. “My phone at one point was overheating from all the calls I had,” she recalled.
Rodriguez, a campus organizing intern for O’Rourke’s political advocacy group, Powered by People, and president of the university’s revived College Democrats chapter, helped coordinate his visit. She worried that only 100 students would attend the event, located in deep-red Walker County. People often think “no one’s gonna change that county,” said Rodriguez. But then an estimated 600 attendees turned up, a harbinger of student turnout at the polls the next month.
Three weeks later, Texas Democrats won their first statewide elections in more than three decades. James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton for the US Senate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Governor Greg Abbott, becoming the state’s first Latina governor. Young voters overwhelmingly backed the Democratic candidates. According to the ABC News Voter Poll, 79 percent of Texas voters ages 18 to 29 supported Talarico, and only about half supported Democratic Senate candidate Collin Allred in 2024.
O’Rourke, the former El Paso congressman who came within three percentage points of unseating Republican Senator Ted Cruz in 2018, spent much of the year traveling to college campuses across Texas. He founded Powered by People in December 2019, shortly after ending his presidential campaign, to mobilize volunteers and support Democratic candidates across the state. The organization began focusing on college campuses in 2024 and relies on volunteers to register students to vote.
At Rice University, Matteo Devries, a junior studying political science and a campus intern for Powered by People, spent the semester staffing voter registration tables and helping organize O’Rourke’s October 22 visit to Rice in Houston.
When Democrats swept Texas’s statewide races on November 3, Devries watched the results with his cousin, who worked on political organizing in Texas, and other family members. “Oh my God, it was exhilarating. I felt incredible,” he recalled.
O’Rourke described Powered by People’s organizing strategy as one centered on maintaining personal contact with voters. Rather than passing newly registered voters’ information to a campaign or political party, volunteers ask permission to stay in touch directly, he said. They help students determine what identification they need, locate polling places, and make plans to vote.
During this midterm election cycle, Powered by People scheduled more than 130 events across 22 Texas cities.
“I’ve been on the road every single week of this semester and every week of the last semester,” O’Rourke said. “I’m there to answer students’ questions, to engage in conversations,” he added.
Those conversations, O’Rourke told me, ranged from rising prices and college tuition to the war in Iran and the difficulty of determining what information to trust on social media. He emphasized the importance of meeting young voters in person, describing those interactions as a critical alternative to the isolation and polarization of online political discourse.
Before the election, O’Rourke presciently pointed to a changing political environment for Texas Democrats. “I think the level of interest on the part of young voters is as high as I’ve ever seen it,” he said. “I also just think that the conditions are different and better for Democrats than I’ve ever seen them.”
He pointed to frustration with the Trump administration and high prices, alongside the slate of promising Democratic candidates, including Talarico and Hinojosa.
For the 2026 elections, Democrats recruited candidates for all 150 Texas House districts, including seats where Republicans had previously run unopposed. In 2018, by comparison, Democrats left 20 state and federal races uncontested.
Early voting numbers offered signs of heightened political participation. More than 7.7 million Texans cast ballots during early voting, setting a new midterm record. In Harris County, more than 104,000 people voted in person on the first day of early voting; only 63,188 voted on the opening day in 2018, when O’Rourke challenged Ted Cruz for the Senate.
At Rice, Gretchen Soika, 19, met the former congressman during his October 22 visit. Soika said reproductive healthcare and abortion access were at the top of her mind when she cast her midterm ballot. Soika remembers O’Rourke’s 2018 Senate run as one of her earliest introductions to Texas politics. His campaign signs and stickers seemed to be everywhere. “It’s inspiring to see that these people are still around and still trying to flip Texas eight years later,” she said.
Before the election, Soika described a renewed sense of optimism among her classmates, many of whom were voting for the first time That optimism persisted even among students who recognized the possibility of another Republican victory. Soika described conversations in which classmates expressing doubts about Democratic prospects were quickly interrupted by friends unwilling to entertain defeat. “Don’t say that. It needs to happen,” she recalled students responding to expressions of pessimism.
At Sam Houston State, Rodriguez described a similar sense of urgency, though her conversations with students often center on the financial pressures they face. For Rodriguez, those concerns are particularly personal. She attended Title I public schools and grew up in a low-income family that relied on SNAP and Section 8 housing assistance.
Affordability and uncertainty about life after graduation have emerged as major concerns among her classmates. “I might have to live with my parents forever because there seems to be no other option for me right now,” Rodriguez said, describing a fear among young people confronting rising costs and a difficult job market.

But political organizing has given Rodriguez opportunities she once struggled to imagine. As a child, she dreamed of entering politics and wanted to feel important enough for elected officials to speak with her. Now she had helped bring those conversations to students at her own university.
“I think he brought so much of that passion and of the optimism that’s been so clearly missing from this campus when it came to midterm elections, or any elections for that matter,” Rodriguez said of O’Rourke’s visit.
Devries described a similar sense of optimism surrounding O’Rourke’s visit to Rice. “A lot of people that came out were super excited to go vote. They were super excited to meet Beto,” he said.
At the weekly voter registration tables he staffed, Devries encountered students who increasingly believed their votes could make a difference in Texas. “I think the atmosphere was more lively than I’ve ever seen it before,” he said.
In a follow-up after the election, O’Rourke said Powered by People had 113,000 voters in its program this year. According to its preliminary figures provided by O’Rourke, about 70 percent of the participating voters aged 18 to 29 cast ballots, compared with 35 percent of young voters statewide.
“We made a significant difference in close state house races,” O’Rourke said, pointing to the organization’s work in 12 Texas House districts that flipped Democratic. “I feel great about it. It’s about people power, literally thousands of volunteers taking the time to meet and help turn out more than 100,000 young Texans.”
And on election night, as the first results from Texas came in, Devries was watching intently. “Damn,” he recalled thinking. “It’s actually happening.”

https://www.theguardian.com/technology/n.title: Anthropic keeps the AI party swinging, but the atmosphere is bubbly | Nils Pratley
https://www.theguardian.com/technology/n.author: Nils Pratley
https://www.theguardian.com/technology/n.text:
Roll up, roll up, who wants to buy shares in a company whose technology “could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”, as the prospectus had it? Virtually everybody, as it turned out. Anthropic flew out of the blocks on its first day as a listed company.
From the point of view of the promoters, the result was as good as it gets. The final pricing for the shares at $83 apiece was meaningfully higher than the indicated range of $70 to $78, but still left room for a big initial “pop”. There were positive vibes all round – especially for the battalion of investment banks collecting $550m of underwriting fees.
And, to be fair, it wasn’t nailed-on that the show would go so swimmingly. There was a late risk that investor sentiment towards the AI universe could be jinxed – or Jensened – by the soap opera at Nvidia. More generally, there was a worry that the AI bubble, if that’s what it is, could burst when somebody tried to unload too much stock on the stock market in one go.
Anthropic, though, has set records by raising $107bn. It is an extraordinary sum, especially for a business founded five years ago. At the listing price, Anthropic was valued at $1.5tn. When shares began trading at £111.50, its market capitalisation was up to $2tn. Only 14 months ago, it raised money at a valuation of a “mere” $183bn.
The feat, though, is not wholly inexplicable. Some $26bn of the listing proceeds were virtually in the bag, thanks to the cornerstone placement to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC. That assembly of AI and AI-adjacent names fed worries about the industry’s circular financing.
But, on the other hand, every fund manager knew he or she would be betting against the crowd by saying no. Momentum can carry a stock a long way, even before the index funds and index-hugging funds are obliged to buy (Nasdaq entry will be quick; the S&P 500 will take at least a year).
Take a step back, though, and ask whether Anthropic – loss-making and with projected revenues in 2026 of $50bn-ish – can possibly be worth $1.5tn-plus.
The short, and unhelpful, answer is that virtually any valuation could be made to sound plausible if you believe, first, that AI is a generational technology that will be adopted at never-seen-before speed and, second, that “frontier” pioneering firms, of which Anthropic is the leader, will capture an outsized slice of the commercial value for years and years.
Consider the assumptions behind that thesis, however. Can Anthropic really improve from $50bn-ish of revenue this year to $600bn in 2030, which is roughly what tech analysts have pencilled in? Given the current rate of growth, perhaps it can. But sustaining the pace, or something like it, for another 16 quarters simply won’t be straightforward or mechanical.
What is the real level of demand from corporate users for frontier models? Nobody doubts that AI adoption is still in the early stage, but does everybody need the finest product from Anthropic’s Claude suite? Already executives grumble that their IT budgets are finite and that nine-month-old versions, or cheaper “open weight” models from rivals, do the job for basic work. Lasting pricing power in AI is simply unclear. “Commoditisation risk”, in the jargon, could be the next year’s valuation debate.
Then there is the investment bill to make it all happen – $900bn of spending commitments were detailed in the prospectus for computing power and infrastructure. The listing proceeds help, as does the visibility and credibility that comes with being on a public market. But debt, not just equity, will be a crucial part of this story.
“Obviously, at some point in the future we’re hoping to be investment grade,” said co-founder Dario Amodei as trading in the shares started. You bet: the price at which Anthropic borrows matters fundamentally.
Away from the party atmosphere, the European Central Bank has its eye on financial stability in the eurozone. This week, it issued one of those fuddy-duddy reminders about how much capital is being bet on the AI revolution, and how little transparency there is around the funding of hyperscalers and other suppliers to the boom.
“Big tech firms are estimated to have total off-balance-sheet commitments of more than $4tn as of the second quarter of 2026,” its report said, warning of “historical parallels with the dotcom and sub-prime bubbles”.
It is not the only one to see warning signs. Anthropic is an astonishingly successful company already and is plainly at the forefront of a significant technological shift. But it has been listed in an environment that looks – to most of us who remember the late 1990s and the subsequent bust – to have bubbly characteristics. AI technology, like the internet, is gamechanging. But it doesn’t mean today’s share prices are right.

https://taz.de/Mehr-Elektrifizierung-weg.title: Mehr Elektrifizierung wegen Nahostkrise: Der größte Energieschock der Weltgeschichte
https://taz.de/Mehr-Elektrifizierung-weg.author: Kai Schöneberg
https://taz.de/Mehr-Elektrifizierung-weg.text:
Mehr Elektrifizierung wegen Nahostkrise: Der größte Energieschock der Weltgeschichte
Erstmals wird in diesem Jahr mehr Energie fürs Kühlen als fürs Heizen verwendet: Klima- und Nahostkrise wandeln die Märkte weltweit radikal.
Klimawandel und Nahostkonflikt verändern die Energiemärkte weltweit in bislang unbekanntem Ausmaß. Die Öl- und Gaskrise infolge der Blockade der Straße von Hormus beschleunigt die Energiewende jetzt schon, analysiert die Internationale Energieagentur (IEA) in ihrem Energy Outlook 2026, der am Donnerstag vorgestellt wurde. Es handele sich um den „größten Energieschock, mit dem die Welt je konfrontiert war“, er „sehe keinen glaubhaften Weg, wie die Energiewelt wieder so sein könnte wie früher“, sagte IEA-Chef Fatih Birol. Die IEA ist eine zwischenstaatliche Organisation mit Sitz in Paris. Sie berät über 30 Mitgliedstaaten in Energiefragen, auch Deutschland.
Durch den Irankrieg sind bislang laut IEA 2,8 Milliarden Barrel Öl und 60 Milliarden Kubikmeter Gas „ausgefallen“. Zum Vergleich: Die Menge entspricht etwa dem Ölverbrauch der Welt von einem Monat und beim Gas etwa 70 Prozent des deutschen Jahresverbrauchs. Auf der Suche nach sichereren, günstigen Energiequellen wird die Welt künftig ihre Versorgung verstärkt diversifizieren, neue Lieferketten finden, den Energiemix verändern – und elektrifizieren.
Die IEA registriert ein Wachstum bei Photovoltaik, Batteriespeichern und Elektrofahrzeugen in zahlreichen Ländern gegenüber dem Vorjahreszeitraum. Bei der Suche nach alternativen Energiequellen würden stärker heimische Ressourcen genutzt. Global werde auch die Nutzung von Atomkraft zunehmen. Derzeit hat Strom etwa 23 Prozent Anteil an der globalen Endenergieversorgung, 2035 sollen es bei Beibehaltung der aktuellen weltweiten Politik 30 Prozent sein.
Diese Prognose liegt 5 Prozentpunkte unter dem Ziel, das aktuell bei der UN-Klimakonferenz im türkischen Antalya verhandelt wird, die regulär an diesem Freitag endet. Die Elektrifizierung spare viel Geld, hat die IEA ausgerechnet. Bei einer beschleunigten Energiewende könnten die Importrechnungen großer Einfuhrländer 2035 zusammen um mehr als 400 Milliarden Dollar jährlich unter dem Niveau von 2025 liegen.
Nur 40 Prozent der Haushalte verfügen über Klimaanlage
Die Erderhitzung hat großen Einfluss auf die Nutzung von Energie. Erstmals in der Geschichte wird laut IEA 2026 der Energiebedarf für die Kühlung von Gebäuden den fürs Heizen übersteigen. Seit 2015 habe der Kühlbedarf wegen steigender Temperaturen und mehr Einwohner*ìnnen in heißen Regionen weltweit um 55 Prozent zugenommen, bis 2035 erwartet die Energieagentur ein weiteres Plus von 60 Prozent. Derzeit leben etwa 80 Prozent der Weltbevölkerung in Regionen, wo zeitweise Bedarf an Kühlung besteht – doch nur rund 40 Prozent der Haushalte verfügen aktuell über eine Klimaanlage.
Bis 2035 soll etwa die Hälfte aller Haushalte weltweit damit ausgestattet sein. Das habe enorme Auswirkungen auf den Strombedarf. Von derzeit 3.000 werde er 2035 auf 4.900 Terawattstunden ansteigen – etwa so viel Strom, wie Deutschland in 10 Jahren benötigt. Durch Elektromotoren etwa für Autos oder Maschinen oder für die Kühlung von Rechenzentren steigt der Strombedarf weltweit bis 2035 sogar um etwa das Doppelte.
There is no planet B
Die Klimakatastrophe braucht unsere volle mediale Aufmerksamkeit. Dafür bündelt die taz seit Jahren ihre Kräfte und begleitet Konflikte und Fortschritte auf allen Kanälen. Und das schon lange: Die taz hat über radikale Klimaveränderungen berichtet, als andere Medien noch treu von unendlichem Wachstum sprachen. Und sie macht weiter, wenn andere ihre Berichterstattung zurückfahren. Unsere Artikel sind und bleiben frei zugänglich – ohne Paywall, dank über 52.000 freiwilliger Unterstützer*innen. Wir sind der Überzeugung, dass es kritische Informationen im Netz geben muss, die nicht kostenpflichtig sind. Gerade zum Thema Klimaschutz. Nur wenn unser Journalismus so viel wie möglich gelesen wird, kann er gesellschaftliche Veränderungen bewirken. Aber das geht nur, wenn sich unsere Leser*innen an dieser Idee beteiligen und den taz-Journalismus mittragen. Sind Sie schon dabei? Jetzt unterstützen

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: ‘Enquanto eu for presidente, não haverá diminuição de direitos’, diz Lula ao assinar decreto que regulamenta escala 5×2
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva assinou, nesta quinta-feira (19), o decreto que regulamenta a Emenda Constitucional 141 de 2026. O ato consolida a extinção da escala 6×1 e estabelece os parâmetros operacionais para a jornada 5×2 em todo o país.
Na cerimônia no Palácio do Planalto, Lula respondeu sobre a pressão do mercado financeiro e de setores empresariais por cortes no orçamento público e garantiu que não haverá retrocesso nas conquistas trabalhistas. “O dado concreto é o seguinte: enquanto eu for presidente da República, não haverá diminuição dos direitos que o povo brasileiro conquistou nesse país”, afirmou
O presidente contextualizou a afirmação ao relatar que, durante recente viagem oficial às Filipinas para encontro de cúpula internacional, acompanhou as discussões no Senado sobre a tramitação de projeto de ajuste fiscal enviado ao Congresso pelo governo. Lula frisou que o rigor nas contas públicas é um compromisso direto da gestão, e não uma concessão ao setor financeiro.
“O mercado quer que a gente tenha um controle fiscal, mas não é o mercado que deseja o controle fiscal. Quem deseja controle fiscal sou eu. Quem tem que ter responsabilidade fiscal é o governo. E nós já temos muita experiência para mostrar que nós temos responsabilidade fiscal nesse país”, afirmou.
O ganho tecnológico retido pelas empresas
Ao tratar especificamente da transição para a jornada 5×2, Lula apontou que as críticas patronais à redução das horas de trabalho ignoram as profundas transformações ocorridas no sistema produtivo nas últimas quatro décadas, desde a promulgação da Constituição de 1988, que baixou o teto de 48 para 44 horas semanais.
O presidente argumentou que a modernização digital multiplicou os ganhos corporativos sem a devida partilha com a classe trabalhadora.
“As pessoas que estão reclamando não levam em conta o que aconteceu nesses últimos 40 anos depois que nós aprovamos as 44 horas semanais. Os ganhos que o mundo digital trouxe para o comércio e para as empresas, a facilidade de muitas coisas que antigamente eram muito difíceis. Só isso justifica reduzir a jornada sem garantir nenhum prejuízo. Porque esses ganhos que os empresários tiveram com a modernidade, com a evolução tecnológica, com a evolução digital, não foram repassados aos trabalhadores. Na verdade, aumentou o ganho dos empresários”, disse.
O presidente defendeu que a garantia de dois dias semanais de folga repara esse descompasso histórico e assegura dignidade elementar para a convivência familiar e o lazer.
Lula ressaltou que o tempo livre viabiliza o usufruto da cidade e de políticas públicas voltadas ao bem-estar coletivo, como as gratuidades no transporte coletivo aos finais de semana e feriados: “Na medida em que as mulheres, os homens tenham mais tempo de descanso, todo mundo sabe que uma pessoa descansada rende mais”.
Calendário de transição
O detalhamento técnico e operacional do decreto foi apresentado pelo ministro do Trabalho e Emprego, Luiz Marinho. A regulamentação fixa a entrada em vigor da nova regra geral a partir de 16 de dezembro de 2026, data em que passa a ser obrigatória a concessão de dois dias de descanso semanal remunerado para empregados urbanos, rurais, domésticos e trabalhadores avulsos.
O cronograma de redução da jornada máxima semanal estabelece duas etapas sem qualquer prejuízo salarial:
- 16 de dezembro de 2026: redução da jornada máxima de 44 para 42 horas semanais, assegurando dois repousos na semana;
- Dezembro de 2027: redução definitiva da jornada máxima para 40 horas semanais.
Segundo dados apresentados pelo ministro, a medida beneficia diretamente 14,8 milhões de trabalhadores com carteira assinada que atualmente estão submetidos à escala 6×1, além de alcançar outros 21,7 milhões de vínculos que já cumprem a jornada 5×2, mas desempenham 44 horas semanais e terão a carga reduzida progressivamente.
Marinho detalhou ainda a alteração nos divisores utilizados para calcular a remuneração da hora de trabalho, o que impacta o valor pago por horas extraordinárias:
- Na jornada de 44 horas, o divisor é 220;
- Na jornada de 42 horas (a partir de 16 de dezembro), o divisor cai para 210;
- Na jornada de 40 horas (em dezembro de 2027), o divisor passa a ser 200.
“Isso significa que um trabalhador que recebe hoje R$ 3 mil na sua remuneração continuará recebendo os mesmos R$ 3 mil, mas o valor de referência de sua hora passará, em 16 de dezembro, de R$ 13,64 para R$ 14,29. E em dezembro de 2027, passará para R$ 15”, exemplificou Marinho.
O ministro advertiu que a elevação do valor da hora extra visa desestimular a sobrecarga de trabalho e impulsionar a geração de empregos: “Os empresários falam: ‘Poxa, mas vai impactar’. É só não convocar hora extra, é só substituir por contratações que não terá nenhum impacto”.
Próximos passos
O ministro do Trabalho esclareceu que o fim da escala 6×1 não acarreta o fechamento de estabelecimentos comerciais, hospitais ou indústrias aos finais de semana.
“A atividade econômica precisará trabalhar os 365 dias do ano, 24 horas por dia. O que nós estamos discutindo é o direito à folga de trabalhadores e trabalhadoras. As atividades poderão continuar funcionando; o que deverá mudar é a organização das escalas de trabalho, garantindo dois dias de repouso para cada trabalhador”, disse.
Em setores com regimes contínuos que comprovem inviabilidade técnica de conceder os dois descansos rigorosamente dentro da mesma semana, a negociação coletiva poderá permitir o agrupamento das oito folgas mensais no período de 30 dias. A escala 12×36, comumente utilizada na saúde e segurança patrimonial, continuará existindo, mas precisará se adequar aos novos limites de carga semanal e compensações via acordos coletivos.
Marinho destacou ainda que os acordos e convenções coletivas vigentes permanecem válidos em quase sua totalidade. Apenas as cláusulas que contrariarem o descanso de dois dias e a nova carga horária perderão eficácia a partir de 16 de dezembro.
A partir de segunda-feira (23), o Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego publicará portarias com orientações complementares para regimes especiais de transporte, aviação, trabalho marítimo e setor petrolífero, além de disponibilizar um manual de perguntas e respostas para orientar empresas, trabalhadores e sindicatos. Equipes de inspeção e relações do trabalho do ministério atuarão em todo o país para fiscalizar a aplicação da lei e mediar conflitos.
Mobilização popular
O deputado federal Guilherme Boulos destacou a relevância política do ato normativo do Executivo, ressaltando que a regulamentação confere certeza jurídica e data estipulada para a transformação da rotina operária.
“O Congresso já havia aprovado a Emenda Constitucional, mas, a partir de hoje, nós estamos dando os caminhos de como ela entra em vigor. E tem dia e tem hora: a partir do dia 16 de dezembro, a trabalhadora e o trabalhador do Brasil vão ter dois dias de descanso semanal”, pontuou Boulos.
O criador do movimento Vida Além do Trabalho (VAT), Rick Azevedo, eleito deputado federal, relembrou a gênese popular da campanha contra a 6×1. “Hoje é um dia histórico para a classe trabalhadora, uma luta que surgiu no balcão da farmácia como forma de reivindicação, como forma de viver, de ter vida além do trabalho, de ter saúde física e mental, que é uma luta também sobre direitos humanos”, disse.
Representando o setor de comércio e serviços, o presidente da União Geral dos Trabalhadores (UGT), Ricardo Patah, classificou a data como o marco laboral mais importante desde a Constituição de 1988.
Patah recordou levantamento da Associação Brasileira de Supermercados (Abras) que apontou 340 mil vagas não preenchidas no último ano, reflexo do afastamento dos jovens de postos marcados pela ausência de descanso. “Nós gostamos de trabalhar, mas queremos viver. Essa conquista de ter dois dias é uma conquista cidadã”.
A dimensão sanitária da jornada exaustiva foi corroborada pelo presidente do Tribunal Superior do Trabalho (TST), ministro Aloysio Corrêa da Veiga, que refutou a ideia de que salvaguardas trabalhistas obstaculizam a produção. “Avaliamos em uma pesquisa durante dez anos: foram 106 milhões de dias de ausência ao trabalho por motivo de doença decorrente dessas jornadas exaustivas. As leis trabalhistas são emancipatórias”, destacou.
Dívida histórica com o povo
Ao final da cerimônia, Lula avaliou a dimensão política da eleição que garantiu ao petista o quarto mandato presidencial. O presidente expressou gratidão às parcelas da população que asseguraram sua vitória nas urnas e se mobilizaram contra o retrocesso democrático, citando em especial as mulheres, os estudantes e a população idosa.
“O papel que os idosos jogaram nessa campanha com o apelo que nós fizemos para que eles fossem votar por eles, pelos filhos deles, pelos netos deles. Aquela cena de filho carregando avô, de filho carregando pai e mãe no colo para votar, não tem dinheiro no mundo que possa pagar a gratidão que eu tenho por essa gente”, disse Lula.
“Eu quero terminar esse mandato elevando o Brasil ao patamar de um país desenvolvido, com a classe trabalhadora vivendo melhor, ganhando melhor, estudando melhor, morando melhor. E eu vou dizer uma coisa: esse é o mandato da minha vida. Se no primeiro mandato eu dizia que não podia errar, nesse eu não apenas não posso errar, eu só tenho que acertar, porque essa é a dívida que eu tenho com o povo brasileiro”, finalizou.

https://gothamist.com/news/builder-facin.title: Builder facing bankruptcy will lead environmental review of controversial NJ ICE warehouse
https://gothamist.com/news/builder-facin.author: Mike Hayes
https://gothamist.com/news/builder-facin.text:
Residents of Roxbury, New Jersey, have expressed alarm because the Trump administration selected a company run by a Boston real estate developer with a troubled financial record to lead a court-ordered environmental review of plans to convert a local warehouse into one of the country's largest immigration detention facilities.
Gothamist confirmed that developer James Grossmann’s company Rudiarius, Inc. has been subcontracted to conduct the environmental review, according to a company spokesperson. The firm’s selection has not been previously reported and may indicate that the White House remains committed to opening the facility, despite Republican losses in this month’s midterm elections and a lawsuit from New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill to stop it.
The Trump administration agreed earlier this year to conduct the environmental review before moving ahead with its plans. In May, a federal judge ordered the project put on hold pending the completed review.
Grossmann ran a separate development company in Boston, Rise Construction Management, that is currently facing a $27 million bankruptcy and several lawsuits claiming he failed to pay development partners and subcontractors.
Rudiarius is a partner firm of Nashville, Tennessee-based SK2, LLC, which received a $31.8 million contract to convert the warehouse into an ICE detention facility if the environmental assessment clears the path for the project to proceed, according to USAspending.gov, posing a potential conflict of interest.
Grossmann managed at least one other environmental assessment for the Department of Homeland Security at a similar warehouse in Surprise, Arizona, that ICE plans to use as a detention facility. The review found that the facility would have no significant impact on the surrounding area. Critics called the review lax and said it ignored serious environmental concerns. Local lawmakers have also pushed back against the plan.
Brian Kiernan, a Roxbury resident, said he feared the environmental review would not be done properly because of the connections between Rudiarius and SK2.
“Is the study going to be a true study, or is it going to be lip service to get the results that his client desires and to get a fee?” he said.
David Broderick, an attorney representing Project No ICE North Jersey Alliance, a local activist group formed last year to oppose the Roxbury project, said he’s concerned about Grossmann’s financial troubles.
“It sounds like [DHS officials] have picked someone and a company which is uniquely unqualified to perform this,” Broderick said.
In an interview, Rudiarius’ spokesperson Jessica Tocco defended Grossmann’s track record and Rise Construction’s bankruptcy proceedings. She said the company is a “completely different LLC” from Rudiarius.
“Some businesses work, and some don't,” she said, adding that the environmental review in Roxbury is “not officially underway.” She did not provide a timeline for the review to start.
In a House Homeland Security Committee hearing Wednesday, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin also said he could not provide a timeline for the environmental review or the administration’s plans to begin construction work at the Roxbury site.
SK2’s representatives did not respond to multiple requests to be interviewed or provide comment on its connection to Grossmann and Rudiarius.
In a court filing Tuesday, the New Jersey attorney general’s office said that after “repeated requests over 11 days,” DHS provided it with a copy of the $31.8 million contract with SK2, LLC. Attorney General Jennifer Davenport said in the filing that she “continues to be concerned” that DHS is violating the judge’s court order by “pressing ahead with steps” to convert the warehouse.
A copy of the contract with SK2 does not mention Rudiarius or any other subcontractors. It states that DHS intends to spend $650,000 on the environmental review.
Roxbury Township Mayor Shawn Potillo said in an emailed statement that the township council plans to contact Roxbury’s legal counsel, the New Jersey attorney general’s office, and their federal representatives about the selection of Rudiarius to manage the environmental review.
“The Township has no authority or involvement in the federal government's decisions regarding the qualifications or suitability of contractors retained to perform federal work,” the statement said. “Regardless of those decisions or the contractors involved, our position remains unchanged; Roxbury Township opposes the proposed ICE facility.”
$27 million in bankruptcy debt
By his own account, Grossmann rose through the ranks at nationally renowned Suffolk Construction for more than two decades before starting his own company, Rise Construction Management, in 2019.
Court records show the company became mired in legal disputes within two years of being founded.
In 2020, Parks Plus, Inc., a New Jersey-based company that specializes in manufacturing and installing elevated parking systems, entered into a nearly $1 million contract at a new condo development under construction by Grossmann’s company in the Brighton section of Boston, according to Parks Plus’ Senior Vice President Ryan Astrup.
He said Rise Construction was “difficult from the get go” and failed to pay more than $50,000 it owed Parks Plus.
“It kind of fizzled out from there. We made several attempts to collect, and they went unanswered,” Astrup told Gothamist.
His company is one of more than 50 firms with debt claims against Rise Construction, according to an August 2026 Chapter 7 bankruptcy filing. According to the filing, several claims — including the one from Parks Plus — are in dispute due to litigation.
Two developers who worked on projects with Rise Construction are suing the company for more than $2 million. Each claims that Rise failed to pay subcontractors. The Lever previously reported Grossmann’s financial troubles.
Tocco said Rise and Grossmann’s troubles can be attributed to market headwinds and a “very tough time for developers.”
“He's doing the right thing,” she said. “He's closing that company with his partners through a legal bankruptcy process.” She added that Rise is one of “dozens” of companies that Grossmann has started during his career in the construction industry.
“To be out there for thirty years and have as many businesses as he had and had one not work out, that's a pretty good track record,” she said.
‘Uniquely unqualified’
News that the federal government signed the $31.8 million contract with SK2 to renovate the warehouse has sowed confusion about the project’s status.
Kiernan, the Roxbury resident, and his wife live about a three-minute drive from the warehouse site off Route 46 in the Ledgewood section of the township. He said he had not gotten clarity from his local elected officials on whether the project is still on hold as the court ordered. And he said he was alarmed that Grossmann’s company would conduct the environmental review.
“This is the individual through a new company who's supposedly going to perform this environmental study, that raises real concern,” he said.
Rudiarius’ environmental assessment of the proposed ICE facility in Arizona has also faced local scrutiny. DHS released the report on November 9.
The environmental group, Partner Engineering and Science, Inc., which conducted the study on Rudiarius' behalf, found that the facility would not have a significant impact on the surrounding area. As in New Jersey, Arizona’s attorney general sued the Trump administration over the conversion project. Local officials and activists have lashed out at the review’s findings.
Brent Peak of Northwest Valley Indivisible, a local grassroots political organization opposed to the facility, criticized the 81-page report for only briefly mentioning a nearby warehouse storing hazardous materials.
“It is completely ridiculous, negligent and derelict that this is one of the primary concerns brought up in the attorney general’s lawsuit,” Peak told AZFamily.com. “And they give it one paragraph out of those 81 pages.”
