https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), ministro Edson Fachin, enviou à Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) os relatórios que tratam da relação entre os ministros da Corte, Alexandre de Moraes, Kassio Nunes Marques, Dias Toffoli e André Mendonça, com ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, que era dono do Banco Master.
Nos casos envolvendo esses quatro ministros, há indicativos de potenciais impactos jurídicos e criminais na relação de cada um deles com o ex-banqueiro. Foram produzidos documentos com as citações referentes aos demais magistrados, mas, por serem feitas por terceiros ou se tratar de simples menções, foram arquivados.
Os gabinetes de todos os integrantes da corte receberam uma cópia dos respectivos relatórios nesta quinta-feira (19), por determinação de Fachin. Ele fixou grau máximo de sigilo.
A PGR terá 15 dias para analisar o material e decidir se são necessárias novas diligências ou se é possível apresentar denúncia contra algum dos magistrados do STF.

https://inthesetimes.com/article/whats-n.title: This Better Not Be What’s Next for the Democrats
https://inthesetimes.com/article/whats-n.author: Hamilton Nolan
https://inthesetimes.com/article/whats-n.text:
This Better Not Be What's Next for the Democrats
After a historic midterms, let’s go inside the great battle for the Democratic Party’s future.
Hamilton Nolan
DENVER—The Democrats! Like migratory birds they descend upon this swagless Western city, seeking warmth among the microbreweries. After years of dark political winter they are emerging into the light, peeking out of their Uber Black Escalades, giddy with the scent of opportunity. They have come to Set the Agenda, to Write the Narrative, to revel in their sudden ascendance. But like all gathering flocks, they are conscious that they must, before anything else, establish their new pecking order.
Their confidence drips from their strange and audacious plumage! This species, native to the sterile government buildings and imperial nighttime restaurants of Washington, D.C. has its own uniform — repugnant to outsiders, but a sign of beauty in their isolated culture. For these men, there is nothing more suave than neatly pressed blue jeans, a blazer, and sneakers. Sneakers! With a blazer? This is the devil-may-care rakishness they bring to their serious work, a way to allow their complex personalities to shine through during their dreary days of policymaking.
The rascals! Those blazers are not just blue. Some are checked. Some carry even more exotic and abhorrent patterns. Most men undo one or even two of the buttons on their shirts, exuding a studied casualness. And around their necks? Nothing at all! With their bold lack of ties, the modern Democrat strikes a blow against conformity. They retain the barest form of the business suit while remixing it with all of the cutting-edge style that D.C. is known for. This is a party of Regular Folks, not stuffed suits. Like all regular folks, they wear sneakers and blazers and lanyards and think about kitchen table issues like working hard to support their families as was promised to them by the American Dream.
Here we all were, in Denver, at the Mission Ballroom, for What’s Next, an event that brought together the professional spine of the Democratic Party to try to lay down exactly what should and will be happening for the next two years. The wi-fi password was “NineDaysLater,” a nod to the midterm wipeout that had the hearts of all the attendees throbbing like a big shot of cocaine. The surface-level theme of the event was unity, coming together as one big tent, but make no mistake: This was the first organized effort to establish exactly which faction will control this party for the next term. The smiles and lack of ties and complimentary Brandi Carlisle concert did not mean that this event was not, in its essence, cutthroat.
The event was put on by Majority Democrats, a moderate-ish group that seeks to build a majority caucus inside the party. It explicitly distinguishes itself from those three apocalyptic horsemen, “The Gerontocratic Establishment,” the “Activist Left,” and “The Maga Right.” Majority Democrats is funded by a hedge fund billionaire, and you could really tell in the event’s production values. Get a bunch of the Activist Left together and you’re looking at janky PA systems and unruly stacks of fliers. But here at What’s Next, there was unlimited free snacks and professional execution and a wondrous lighting display on stage that looked like a sculpture of huge lamps of all colors turned on their side, hypnotizing and soothing the crowd as some Congressman drones on. If I were a billionaire dark money funder I would take a hard look at how much of my political money is being spent on lighting. I guess they can afford it, though.
The money also bought graphic design, and it was an atrocity. Any normal human would step back and clutch their chest in agony at the sight of the posters that adorned the hallways. They were all done up in the style of classic concert posters, like something you might see hanging on a telephone pole to advertise a Grateful Dead or Bob Marley show, except they featured the most aggressively uncool politicians in the United States. There was Hakeem Jeffries, wearing shades; there was an ad for Cory Booker & The Revolution; there was a four-peat of Josh Shapiro’s head in four different colors; there was a hand drawn picture of CIA agent-turned-governor Abigail Spanberger as a hippie with flowing blond hair holding a batch of flowers.
Prowling the hallways between these posters were Majority Democrats staffers wearing custom-made Dickies jackets with “Majority Democrats” in yellow cursive and a sewn-on name tag like a genuine working class person somewhere might wear. (Or so they’ve heard.) Wherever you turned you would be faced with this sort of visual assault, physical manifestations of the way that culture is ingested and destroyed by capital. Like the cheeky blazers and the Adidases worn with suits, you can be sure that the people involved in this would wink and say that they were in on the joke, without knowing that their comedy is actually a horror film.
The public believes that politics is about politicians, and movements believe that politics is about people, but What’s Next was an event centered on the real heroes: the consultant class. This vision of politics is one in which good political decisions emanate from a small group of ultra-smart nerds immersed in data, who tell the party what it should be doing. Deviations from this path — whether to the right or (more likely) the left — are treated as verifiable errors, juvenile indulgences, refusals to face facts about what voters really want.
Thus, the consultants that took the stage in Denver delivered lectures to the assembled functionaries about What Voters Are Thinking. And what they are thinking is: Affordability. Affordability, affordability, affordability. The economy, stupid. Prices of things. They’re high, and they should be lower, for the sake of affordability. “I hope you’re very excited to hear someone repeat the phrase ‘cost of living’ for seven minutes and 45 seconds,” joked Charlotte Swasey, director of analytics for the Searchlight Institute. Searchlight is a sort of companion think tank for the Majority Democrats project, funded by the same billionaires, whose schtick is “we serve up centrism but from a guy with long hair.” That guy is Adam Jentleson, the bearded and man-bunned former Harry Reid and John Fetterman staffer who has now found himself a secure perch in the lucrative Telling The Left To Shut Up industry.
Jentleson is a fascinating figure. Besides his personal appearance, which is that of a bartender at a craft cocktail speakeasy in 2007, it is unclear to me what makes him so alluring to the political establishment. His ideas are standard, rehashed Clintonism. He’s not much of writer. He’s a workmanlike speaker. He glanced down at his notes continually while instructing the crowd about the “messy” political beliefs of Americans. “They want a stronger safety net, but also want fiscal discipline,” he revealed. “They think private enterprise is good, but also want to raise taxes on the wealthy.”
Gadzooks! Stop the presses! It is very hard to conclude that Adam Jentleson’s position of power is not due in large part to his haircut. It is exactly the sort of thing — like, say, a concert-style poster of Pete Buttigieg — that a billionaire might imagine would lend a rock-n-roll frisson to the project of producing a stable regulatory environment conducive to capital growth. Searchlight sponsored a welcome reception in an adjacent bar the first day of the event, and adorned the tables with QR codes that would allow you to take a quiz to determine your own “Political Neighborhood.” The first question was about how you feel about trans people in bathrooms. I clicked off at that point. There were free Searchlight-branded tote bags and hats that said “tax-and-spend liberal” available, but I left them there. Couldn’t think of anyone who would get the irony of the souvenir.
Amid all of the lectures from pollsters and consultants, two anecdotes stood out to me. The first was a remark from Sarah Longwell, a political strategist and former Republican who grew disgusted with Trump and founded The Bulwark, the center-right anti-MAGA news outlet. Longwell is very much a DC creature. (Earlier this year, she stopped the Bulwark from publishing an in-depth investigative story critical of Democratic fundraising practices because she couldn’t imagine what was wrong with fundraising spam.) She spoke enthusiastically of her desire to “Burn MAGA to the ground and salt the earth.” But as her speech unfolded, it became clear that all of her conclusions, all of her recommendations, all of her insights into What Voters Want, came from listening to focus groups. “I listen in the shower, and I listen on the treadmill, and I listen when I’m walking places,” she said of focus group recordings. “I have voters in my ear all the time, and the disconnect between what we talk about in rooms like this and the way they sound is enormous.”
This was disconcerting. Here was a person who was paid to be an expert on what regular people want, and was invited to instruct the Democratic Party on what regular people want, whose own alleged expertise on what regular people want was not drawn from actually knowing any regular people. Not at all! Regular people were convened to sit in rooms and be questioned and recorded by professionals, and this woman listened to those recordings while on the treadmill, and from these data events she is now prepared to declare herself an expert on the will of regular people. Equally disconcerting is the fact that when this group, the “Majority” Democrats, went to seek out an expert on regular people for its big event, it did not to think to invite any regular people, nor even anyone who personally associates with regular people, but rather a political consultant who listens to a lot of focus groups that are presumably made up of regular people.
The second, and related, remark that struck me came from Daniel Squadron, an intellectual liberal consultant who gave an interesting talk on the long, pernicious influence of right wing thinkers like Ayn Rand and Carl Schmitt. He was making the point to the audience that Democrats will need more than a catchy slogan to succeed. “You can’t ask what your slogan is until you ask a different question: What do you believe?” he said. “Why are you doing this? It’s a question that I bet many of you have never been asked in a real way.”
Squadron, a man who has spent his entire career in Democratic politics, was speaking to a room full of professional Democratic functionaries, and he casually voiced that it was his working assumption that these people — the people who were there to determine the future of progressive politics — have never been asked the question, “What do you believe?” This smart and experienced man, a man intimately familiar with this milieu, took it for granted that this audience of thousands had probably never encountered a question so tawdry, so elementary, as “What do you believe?” For the hardnosed, data-driven consultants in the room, such a question would, I guess, be a waste of time.
Remarks like these are a little unnerving, because if you are a more or less regular person who holds unforgivably childish ideas like “I believe we must help the working class break the power of capital,” you start to realize that you are in a big tent that is owned and controlled by a whole other set of people who don’t have time to think about stuff like that because they are too busy listening to recordings of focus groups of people like you saying cute things like “my rent is too expensive.” You are supposed to take your marching orders on political action from these people. These are the majority Democrats. What that makes all the rest of us, I do not know.
Spending some time in this setting will help you understand why the Democratic Party is so perpetually frustrating. In this consultant-centered model, the politicians themselves become little more than actors, sent out to convincingly perform the script that the consultants have devised. The best politicians are not the ones who have their own ideas but rather the ones who can sound winning and likable while repeating back to voters the things that voters themselves have said in various focus groups just a short time ago. Listening to the parade of national politicians take the stage at What’s Next, it was hard not to notice that most of them — the brightest stars of the non-left wing of the Democratic Party — did, if you paid attention to their actual words rather than their charming faces and aw-shucks jokes, seem to be doing exactly this.
“We must bridge the divide between us,” said James Talarico, in jeans, a blazer, and no tie. “We must repair the ties that bind us.”
“Working hard every day. Building a home, starting a family, sending their kids to a good public school,” said Colorado Congressman Joe Neguse, in a blue suit and no tie. “That type of opportunity is what makes me believe in America. It’s why I refuse to abandon my bone-deep commitment to expanding opportunity.”
“I tell people the political system is broken, because it is,” said Iowa governor-elect Rob Sand, sporting the impassive face of the male model he used to be. “I tell them, too often it feels like two private clubs who are more interested in beating up on each other than they are in solving anyone’s problems.”
“For too long, we’ve been afraid to talk like normal people,” said burly Arizona Senator Ruben Gallego. “Big-ass truck politics is what unites Democrats like never before.”
“Affordability. That’s what we ran on,” said New Jersey governor Mikie Sherrill.
“Affordability,” said Colorado governor-elect Phil Weiser.
“Affordability,” said Virginia’s Abigail Spanberger.
“Affordability is front and center,” argued Alaska governor-elect Jonathan Kriess-Tomkins, by contrast.
Presented in this rapid-fire manner, the impression that all of the elected officials are just reading their lines is unavoidable. Nobody embodies that robotic discipline like Hakeem Jeffries, the man that leftists in the party fear is about to become Speaker of the House. Jeffries has the gift of moving his mouth without moving any other portion of his face, which gives him a flinty, imperturbable air that serves him well amid chaos. When he sat down for a chat on stage with Fox News token Democrat Jessica Tarlov, he was quickly interrupted by not one, not two, but three protesters, each of whom stood up and started shouting at him as soon as the one before had been escorted out by police. They yelled that he didn’t listen to young people, that he had aided genocide in Gaza, that we need a Green New Deal. Jeffries sat still, totally unmoved, for a few seconds of this, and then proceeded to just carry on with his applause line about the Knicks winning the championship (the very same line that he used in a video clip played during his introduction).
The final protester, as he was being pulled past me, burst out in frustration, “Fuck you all!”
“Fuck you too, bitch!” hollered an older black man who was sitting in front of me, purely out of reflex. On stage, Jeffries continued talking about how he enjoyed seeing himself portrayed on Saturday Night Live recently. Tarlov, on the other hand, was flustered. “I’m nervous, compared to like, The Five,” she sputtered.
Jeffries immediately began talking about the need to get permitting reform done. This is his power. He may be corrupt, and an obstacle to true progress, but he has achieved total unflappability. He cannot be disturbed, and he also cannot be made to answer a question with truth or clarity, two qualities which are effectively superpowers for a man in his position. He would say things like, “We have to get dark money out of politics,” without defining it in a way that might get him into trouble. When asked something he didn’t want to answer at all, like whether he supports term limits, he would say, “It’s the right conversation to have.” He would say things that are vaguely reassuring to people of all political persuasions, like, “We’re going to be guided by the Constitution.” If you didn’t press hard, he can leave you thinking he agrees with you on everything. If you do press hard, he slips out to the side, like trying to snatch a quick fish underwater. Even if you don’t like him, you must admit that he is a perfect leader for the Democratic Party: a human bowl of Jell-O, capable of holding a shape for a while, but always ready to ooze into any new container as necessary.
The one firm claim that everyone at What’s Next hastened to make was that the Democratic Party is not divided. Is this billionaire-backed convention of centrists somehow a sign that there is a divide between the left and the centrists in the party? Not at all! Nothing could be further from the truth, the officials invited to this gathering proclaimed.
“This isn’t about middle, left, or right. It’s about up versus down,” said former New Orleans mayor Mitch Landrieu. “Insiders who take everything, and leave everybody else out.”
“There is no so-called moderate Democratic Party. There is no so-called progressive Democratic Party,” said former attorney general Eric Holder. “There is one Democratic Party.”
“We need to think bigger now,” said New Jersey Senator Cory Booker, channeling a preacher. “We need to call left and right together to show them that the lines that divide us are not nearly as strong as the ties that bind us.”
“The new generation is not gonna be defined by progressive versus moderate,” said Michigan Senator Elissa Slotkin. “That new generation is, quite simply, are you on team fight, or team flight?”
Notably, the one genuine left winger who spoke on stage, Congressman Ro Khanna, struck a different tone. He knew he was in the minority here. Unlike almost every other speech, his contained actual policy prescriptions. He called for Medicare for All (not to be confused with “universal health care,” a term that sounds kind of like Medicare for All but is not the same, and which was in widespread use among newly elected Democrats here). He called for a wealth tax. He called for a $25 minimum wage. He called for an end to aid for Israel, and no more foreign wars. These are all common things to hear when you are at leftist events. But among the Majority Democrats, Khanna’s directness only served to highlight the absence of real policy positions from most of the other speakers.
Let me try to be fair. Let me try not to piss on the parade. Democrats just won their biggest midterm victory in decades and they seem to agree that they need an agenda that they can act on, which is certainly better than no agenda. By listening to the moderates here and combining it with what we know the left wants, you can begin to see the outline of some agreed-upon things: Building more housing, ending gerrymandering, some modest expansion of Medicare to either the young or the old, a ban on stock trading for members of Congress, more green energy, some sort of AI regulation, aggressive investigations of Trump administration crimes. These things have broad appeal, and could well get passed quickly. They would be good. Sure. They would be an improvement from what we have now. They would live up to the underlying tone of the Majority Democrats’ oxymoronic platform: Big, Bold, and Moderate.
The truth is, though, that no matter how big a tent you put over the Democratic Party, it will still be divided. Why? Because that is the nature of politics. Factions are not inherently bad. They exist because people genuinely disagree on substantial things. You can say “let’s all come together in unity,” but when we propose a wealth tax and you say no, there is no unity there. There is just a fight. When we ask for Medicare for All and you say no, there is not common ground. There is a fight.
Policy differences matter. Party unity is important in general elections, but when it comes to governing, it is more instructive to think of politics as a battle. The left has more common ground with the moderates in Denver than it has with the fascists in Trumplandia, yes. But what the moderates and the fascists have in common is that they are both trying to ensure that the left does not gain power. The hand of friendship that centrists extend to the newly ascendant left wing of their party comes with a tacit agreement that the left will remain the minority partner in this coalition. If you are on the left and you actually want to change the structural problems that brought us to this point, the holes in the big tent are easy to spot.
The morning of the last day of What’s Next, about 20 protesters gathered a couple of blocks outside of the venue, holding signs for a Green New Deal and chanting about dumping Chuck Schumer. In response to this small crew, the Denver police deployed dozens of riot cops in full tactical gear, helmets, and body armor. They even sent an armored SWAT team vehicle that would have looked far more appropriate navigating the IED-strewn streets of Fallujah than parked on the curb just down from the Chubby Unicorn Cantina. The whole scene would have been laughable, were it not for the presence of so many heavily armed men. Majority Democrats staffers stood out there looking worried, thanking the police for their work. I spoke to one older man holding an Indivisible sign who had come to protest. He was jealous of my press pass. “I wish I was in the press,” he said. “Getting into that event costs five thousand bucks.”
That afternoon, Georgia Senator and rumored presidential hopeful Raphael Warnock took the stage. He is a real live preacher, a gifted speaker, a man who knows how to call forth the spirit of the civil rights movement. He told a story about watching his grandmother chop the head off of a snake in her garden when he was a child. “As I witnessed the traumatic and menacing movements and convulsions after she decapitated it, I thought we were really in trouble. What I didn’t understand as a six year-old kid is that that snake was moving not because it was living, but because it was dying,” he said. “This is now the last gasp of an old order that knows it is on its way out!”
It is a neat metaphor — the snake, as evil, writhing in its death throes. Yet the other quality of snakes is that they shed their skin. They change their outer appearance and are reborn. Sometimes, they slither right inside of your big tent, curl up beside you, and try to make friends.

La réalisatrice israélienne Tamara Erde met en scène une histoire de Gaza qui ne commence ni au 7 octobre 2023 ni au plan de partage de la Palestine de 1947, mais rétablit l’idée d’un territoire millénaire.
Israélienne, Tamara Erde aurait pu garder les yeux fermés. Mais après son service militaire au Mossad puis dans le renseignement militaire, elle a choisi la voie des arts. Scénariste et réalisatrice, elle documente depuis des années (This Is My Land, Par nos yeux) le malaise de son pays autour de la question palestinienne.
Dans la lignée de ses précédentes œuvres, ce film en deux parties efface l’image imposée par Israël d’un peuple de terroristes menaçant ses voisins, prétexte à une guerre d’épuration : « Le Hamas est toujours là, c’est Gaza qui est détruite. » Elle entend aller « à la racine des choses » pour humaniser les Gazaouis et leur histoire.

https://taz.de/Pistorius-besucht-Auschwi.title: Pistorius besucht Auschwitz: Minister für Verteidigung und Antifaschismus
https://taz.de/Pistorius-besucht-Auschwi.author: Kersten Augustin
https://taz.de/Pistorius-besucht-Auschwi.text:
Pistorius besucht Auschwitz: Minister für Verteidigung und Antifaschismus
Bei seinem Besuch in Auschwitz präsentiert sich Boris Pistorius als Kämpfer gegen rechts. Verteidigungspolitik spielt nur eine Nebenrolle.
Langsam schreitet Boris Pistorius durch das Lagertor von Auschwitz. Neben ihm läuft der stellvertretende Gedenkstättenleiter. Mit der monotonen Stimme des Museumsführers führt er den deutschen Verteidigungsminister an diesem Donnerstag über das Gelände. Er zeigt auf die Baracken aus rotem Backstein: Hier waren die ersten polnischen und sowjetischen Gefangenen untergebracht. Dann zeigt er auf ein Gebäude, in dem Kinderschuhe, Koffer, Brillen der Ermordeten ausgestellt sind. Eigentlich soll Pistorius jetzt weitergehen, ein Besuch der Baracke ist nicht geplant. „Das würd’ ich gern sehen“, sagt Pistorius zu dem Museumsleiter und dreht sich zu seinen Mitarbeitern um. „Wir haben doch Zeit, oder?“
Es ist lange her, dass ein deutscher Verteidigungsminister öffentlichkeitswirksam Auschwitz besuchte. 1999 war das, als die Währung in Deutschland noch D-Mark hieß und der Minister Rudolf Scharping. Scharping war der Erste, der mit einer Delegation deutscher Soldaten nach Auschwitz reiste. In Zeitungsberichten kann man nachlesen, wie ein junger deutscher Soldat des Panzerbataillons 393 aus Thüringen den Tag erlebte. Dass die alten Menschen „komisch geguckt“ hätten, als sie die deutschen Uniformen in Auschwitz sahen.
Heute, 27 Jahre später, fallen die deutschen Soldaten, die in Begleitung von Pistorius hier sind, kaum einem Besucher auf. Auf den Stufen vor den Baracken sitzen Jugendgruppen, die die Gedenkstätte besuchen. Viele sind aus Israel. Ein paar Meter weiter, an der Todeswand, erschossen SS-Soldaten tausende Gefangene. Pistorius legt hier einen Blumenkranz ab und streicht die schwarz-rot-goldene Schärpe glatt. „Hast du gesehen? Das ist der deutsche Verteidigungsminister“, sagt eine israelische Schülerin zu ihren Freundinnen. Sie runzeln kurz die Stirn, dann laufen sie weiter.
Während Pistorius nach Auschwitz gereist ist, trifft sich in Berlin die Koalition der Willigen, um über die Unterstützung der Ukraine zu verhandeln. Auch das verbindet Pistorius’ Besuch in Auschwitz mit dem seines Vorgängers Scharping: Sie reisen an den Ort des deutschen Verbrechens, während in Europa ein Krieg geführt wird.
Keine rhetorische Verbindung zur Ukraine
Scharping nutzte seine Reise, um den Einsatz deutscher Soldaten im Ausland zu rechtfertigen. Ähnlich wie der damalige Außenminister Joschka Fischer („Ich habe nicht nur gelernt, nie wieder Krieg, sondern auch: Nie wieder Auschwitz“) sagte Scharping über die Verpflichtung aus der deutschen Geschichte: „Wo die Menschenwürde mit Füßen getreten wird, da dürfen wir nicht schweigen. Darum ist die Bundeswehr in Bosnien, und darum wird sie wohl auch in das Kosovo gehen.“ Einen guten Monat später begann der Krieg der Nato gegen Serbien. Scharping und Fischer wurde vorgeworfen, die deutsche Geschichte für die Rechtfertigung eines Kriegs zu instrumentalisieren.
Pistorius wählt bei seinem Besuch andere Worte. Er zieht keine rhetorische Verbindung zur Unterstützung der Ukraine. „Meine Reise nach Polen dient dazu, klarzumachen: Wir Deutschen sind uns unserer Verantwortung bewusst“, hatte Pistorius vor dem Abflug gesagt, „gerade jetzt, da rechtsextremistische Strömungen in Europa lauter werden.“
Nicht mit der Verteidigung der Ukraine, sondern mit dem Kampf gegen rechts begründet der Verteidigungsminister also seinen Besuch.
Womöglich hat Pistorius zuletzt Gefallen gefunden an antifaschistischen Auftritten. Erst einen Monat ist es her, dass er auf dem Bebelplatz in Berlin auf eine Getränkekiste stieg. Am Ort der Bücherverbrennung drückte Pistorius seine Wut aus über die Wahl eines Rechtsextremen zum Landtagspräsidenten von Sachsen-Anhalt. Sein Auftritt ging viral – und schenkte seiner Partei, die nicht gerade verwöhnt ist mit Applaus, einen seltenen leuchtenden Moment.
Lange war Pistorius nicht als Vorkämpfer gegen die AfD bekannt. Seit dem Sommer aber setzt er sich für die Prüfung eines Parteiverbots ein, spricht über die Gefahr für die Demokratie von innen, die eigentlich nicht in seine Zuständigkeit fällt. Und nun der Besuch von Auschwitz.
Kein Interesse an SPD-Vorsitz
In der SPD würden viele gern häufiger von Pistorius’ Strahlkraft profitieren: In Umfragen ist er der beliebteste Politiker des Landes. Interesse am SPD-Parteivorsitz, der im Januar gewählt wird, hat Pistorius aber nicht. Er sei mit seiner Aufgabe, die Sicherheit des Landes zu garantieren, „wirklich ausgelastet“.
Die nächste Station seines Rundgangs führt Pistorius zum Appellplatz. Hier ließ die SS ihre Gefangenen 19 Stunden lang stillstehen, nachdem einem Mann die Flucht gelungen war. „Und, hat er es geschafft?“, fragt Pistorius den Gedenkstättenleiter und klingt dabei ein bisschen hoffnungsvoll. Nein, Tadeusz Wiejowski hat es nicht geschafft, er wurde einige Monate nach seiner Flucht erschossen.
Als Pistorius mit seiner Delegation eine Gaskammer und ein Krematorium besucht, muss eine Schülergruppe vor dem Eingang warten, Sicherheitsmänner halten sie zurück. Die Schüler, es sind Israelis, sind empört. So lange sind sie hierhergefahren, und jetzt müssen sie warten, auf einen deutschen Minister? „Schickt ihn raus, ich rede mit ihm“, sagt eine Teenagerin selbstbewusst.
Als Pistorius etwas später in Birkenau ankommt, ist es bereits dunkel. Im gelben Licht kann man gerade noch die Schienen erkennen. Hier, an der Rampe, fand die Selektion statt. 20 Prozent kamen ins Lager, 80 Prozent direkt in die Gaskammer, erzählt der Gedenkstättenleiter. In den Krematorien konnten 4.500 Leichen am Tag verbrannt werden. Mehr als eine Million Menschen, die meisten von ihnen Juden, wurden hier von den Deutschen ermordet.
Pistorius sagt nun nichts mehr. Er schüttelt nur langsam den Kopf. Dann fragt er, etwas hilflos und vielleicht, um irgendetwas zu sagen: „Und das sind die original Gleise?“
Eigentlich war in Auschwitz kein Statement für die Presse geplant, nun will Pistorius doch ein paar Worte sagen: „Auch wenn wir alles wissen – hier zu stehen, das ist etwas anderes.“ Pistorius erzählt, dass er als junger Student zum ersten Mal die Gedenkstätte besucht hat, 1981. Er sei „voller Scham für das, was Deutsche hier anderen Menschen angetan haben“.
Dann kommt Pistorius schnell in der Gegenwart an. Das ist der Ton, den er heute setzen will. Auschwitz zeige, wohin Ausgrenzung führe. „Wir leben in einer Zeit, in der das wieder eine Renaissance erlebt, in der rechtsextreme Parteien wieder stark werden.“ Angefangen habe es aber früher, mit dem Beschreiben von unwürdigem Leben, mit der Aufteilung nach Rasse, Herkunft, Glauben, sexueller Orientierung. Es sei die deutsche Verantwortung, zu verhindern, dass sich etwas wie Auschwitz wiederhole.
Und dann noch ein bisschen Verteidigungspolitik
Die Verteidigungspolitik spielt bei der Reise des Verteidigungsministers nur eine Nebenrolle. Von Auschwitz reist Pistorius am Donnerstagabend weiter nach Warschau zu einem kurzen Treffen mit dem polnischen Verteidigungsminister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. Fragen der Presse sind nicht zugelassen. Die deutsche Seite wollte wohl ein längeres gemeinsames Programm. Aber für polnische Minister, zumal von einer konservativen Partei, gibt es mit Bekenntnissen zu Deutschland weiterhin wenig zu gewinnen, auch wenn das Verhältnis in den vergangenen Jahren besser geworden ist, seit Donald Tusk Premier und die PiS-Partei in der Opposition ist und seit Deutschland die osteuropäische Angst vor einem russischen Angriff ernst nimmt.
„Boris, ich danke dir für dein Engagement für die Unterstützung Polens und für die gemeinsame Sicherung der Ostflanke der Nato“, sagt Kosiniak-Kamysz zu Pistorius. Zu viele Menschen auch in Polen würden immer noch nicht verstehen: „Unsere Feinde sind im Osten, unsere Freunde sind im Westen.“ Er kündigt an, die Zusammenarbeit in der Rüstungsindustrie zu verbessern, damit die europäische Verteidigung unabhängiger werde.
Pistorius nennt es ein „Privileg“, dass beide Länder heute so eng zusammenstehen. „Der deutsche Überfall auf Polen, die Besatzung und der Völkermord an Millionen von Juden haben unendlich viel Leid über Europa gebracht.“ Er verweist auf das deutsch-polnische Verteidigungsabkommen, das im Juni unterzeichnet wurde, und auf die Regierungskonsultationen, die im Januar in Warschau stattfinden sollen.
Während Pistorius Polen besucht, finden zwei große Nato-Übungen mit deutschen Soldaten statt. Bei der Operation „Grand Eagle“ wird geübt, 2.000 Soldaten, Panzer und Fahrzeuge möglichst schnell nach Litauen zu verlegen, zum Teil über den Landweg. Deutsche Soldaten, die durch Polen marschieren, und ein polnischer Minister, der darüber dankbar ist – das zeigt, wie viel sich in Europa verändert hat.
Gemeinsam für freie Presse
Die taz gehört zu 100 Prozent ihren Leser:innen und ist damit nicht nur konzernfrei, sondern auch kostenfrei zugänglich. Alle Artikel stellen wir frei zur Verfügung, ohne Paywall. Gerade in diesen Zeiten müssen Einordnungen und Informationen allen zugänglich sein. Unsere Leser:innen müssen nichts bezahlen, wissen aber, dass kritischer, unabhängiger Journalismus nicht aus dem Nichts entsteht. Dafür sind wir sehr dankbar. Damit wir auch morgen noch unseren Journalismus machen können, brauchen wir mehr Unterstützung für taz zahl ich. Dank Ihnen haben wir nun die 50.000 erreicht. So viele unterstützen freiwillig und regelmäßig. Noch nicht dabei? Werden Sie jetzt Teil der Community! Jetzt unterstützen

Introduction: Asian stocks headed for worst week since 2020
Good morning, and welcome to our rolling coverage of business, the financial markets and the world economy.
Anthropic’s historic IPO yesterday certainly lived up to the hype, ending the day at a whopping $1.7tn valuation – but it looks like has failed to allay investor concerns around an AI bubble.
Asian stock markets have sold off overnight, led by falls at big chip companies, and are now on track for their worst week since 2020.
In Taiwan, stocks dropped 6.7% to hit their lowest point since mid-April, deepening its weekly loss to more than 16%, and putting them on track for their worst five-day rout since 1990. TSMC, a leading chip manufacturer and by far the most valuable company in Taiwan’s stock market, fell by about 6%.
South Korean stocks also fell more than 5% to their lowest in more than nine months, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix both falling by about 7%. The falls have pushed the MSCI EM Asia equity index down more than 4% to levels last seen in early April – the index has lost nearly 9% this week, and is on track for its worst week since mid-March 2020.
Meanwhile Anthropic itself has fallen by 4.7% in after hours trading to $92.60, below its lowest level yesterday.
Its IPO has failed to ease worries around the AI trade, as investors increasingly question whether companies can deliver the returns necessary to justify the billions of dollars being poured into the AI buildout.
Jim Reid, of Deutsche Bank, notes that Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index is now also approaching bear-market territory as it is down almost 20% from its peak in January.
 The CSI 300 (-1.85%), Shanghai Composite (-2.10%), and Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 (-1.58%) are also posting notable declines. The downward momentum is continuing in futures with contracts on the S&P 500 (-0.50%), Nasdaq 100 (-0.98%) and Stoxx (-1.70%) all notably lower with Europe catching down.
The risk-off tone has also weighed on a wide variety of other asset classes, with gold (-2.68%) sliding to a 14-month low of $3,625/oz yesterday and down another -2.2% this morning. Bitcoin (-1.25%) has fallen to its lowest level since early July, and US HY credit spreads (+6bps) reaching their widest level since May at 344bps.
Matters haven’t been helped by the latest geopolitical headlines, which helped push energy prices higher and added to fears about inflationary pressures.
Among others, Axios reported that the White House had asked the Pentagon and intelligence experts for their view on how Iran would respond to the different strike scenarios prepared by the US military. So that echoed the previous evening’s report in the New York Times that President Trump was considering plans for further strikes on Iran.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.title: Islam set to be the largest religion by 2035: Where will most Muslims live?
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2.text:
Islam set to be the largest religion by 2035: Where will most Muslims live?
Pew Research projects the Muslim population in Pakistan will overtake Indonesia by 2070, with India second and Nigeria third.
Muslims are projected to outnumber Christians worldwide by 2035, according to projections released by the Pew Research Center.
Both religions will keep growing. Between 2020 and 2070, the number of Muslims is expected to rise by 80 percent, from 2.02 billion to 3.64 billion. Christians are projected to grow by 30 percent to 2.96 billion, roughly in step with the world population.
Which religions are growing fastest?
Muslims are projected to grow faster than any other major religious group. Hindus and Jews are expected to grow more slowly than the world population, while the number of Buddhists and people with no religion is projected to shrink.
The main reason is birth rates. Between 2020 and 2025, Muslim women had an average of 3.1 children, compared with 2.5 for Christian women and 1.6 for all other women. A population needs about 2.1 children per woman to replace itself.
Births minus deaths are projected to add 1.6 billion Muslims and 792 million Christians by 2070.
Which countries will have the most Muslims?
Most of the growth will happen where Muslims are already the majority. The 53 Muslim-majority countries are expected to gain 1.2 billion Muslims by 2070, 74 percent of the global increase.
Indonesia had the world’s largest Muslim population in 2020, at 239 million. Pakistan, just 12 million behind, is projected to take the top spot. Pew’s figures compare 2020 with 2070, so they do not say exactly when, but with Pakistan’s Muslim population set to double to 461 million while Indonesia’s grows 15 percent, the switch is likely to come well before 2070.
By 2070, India’s Muslim population is projected to rise from third to second, growing from 213 million to 334 million. Nigeria jumps from fifth to third, more than doubling to 282 million and pushing Indonesia to fourth.
Four of the top 10 in 2070 are in Africa: Nigeria, Egypt, Ethiopia and Sudan. Ethiopia and Afghanistan join the list, replacing Iran and Algeria, while Sudan’s Muslim population more than doubles to 116 million and climbs above Turkiye.
Pew’s projections cover 201 countries and territories, home to 99.98 percent of the world’s population. They assume current trends in fertility, mortality and religious switching continue, and could change with wars, disasters or economic shifts.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120402.title: Verkehr | Neue Straßenbahnen, aber marode Gleise
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120402.author: Andreas Fritsche
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120402.text:
- Berlin
- Verkehr
Neue Straßenbahnen, aber marode Gleise
Brandenburgs Landtag soll den Doppelhaushalt 2027/28 ändern. So könnten Fördermittel gesichert werden, erläutert der Infrastrukturminister.
»Die Straßenbahnen in Cottbus müssen immer wieder ihr Tempo drosseln. Der Grund: Das Schienennetz ist marode.« So berichtete die »Lausitzer Rundschau« Anfang November. Angesichts dessen will die BSW-Fraktion am Donnerstag im Infrastrukturausschuss des brandenburgischen Landtags über den Handlungsbedarf und Fördermittel vom Land sprechen – unter anderem für die kommunale Cottbusverkehr GmbH, aber auch für andere Verkehrsbetriebe im Bundesland, die Straßenbahnen haben.
Schließlich sei erst im vergangenen Jahr die Anschaffung neuer Straßenbahnen der tschechischen Škoda-Werke für Cottbus und Frankfurt (Oder) bezuschusst worden, erklärt die BSW-Abgeordnete Jenny Meyer. Da wäre es doch besonders ärgerlich, wenn die wegen des Streckennetzes nicht verkehren könnten.
Bevor Infrastrukturminister Robert Crumbach (SPD) der Abgeordneten ihre Fragen beantwortet, will er erst einmal wissen, ob dieser Tagesordnungspunkt vielleicht überflüssig geworden sei. Denn der Ausschuss beschloss unmittelbar zuvor einen Änderungsantrag zum Doppelhaushalt 2027/28. Aber der Landtag muss noch zustimmen, worum Crumbach inständig bittet, damit Zuschüsse tatsächlich fließen können.
»Die Straßenbahn ist ein unverzichtbarer Teil des Lebens vieler Brandenburgerinnen und Brandenburger«, erklärt der Minister. Sie verbinde Wohngebiete mit Arbeitsplätzen und Schulen und ermögliche bezahlbar Mobilität. Grundsanierungen der Gleise seien nicht allein in Cottbus erforderlich. Das sei teuer, und »wir wissen, in welcher finanziellen Situation unsere Kommunen sind«.
Förderprogramme werde es wie in der Vergangenheit auch künftig geben, versichert der Minister. 50 Prozent der Investitionssummen schieße bis vorerst 2030 der Bund zu. 25 Prozent gebe das Land dazu, damit die Verkehrsbetriebe lediglich 25 Prozent selbst finanzieren müssen. Auch Brandenburg/Havel und Potsdam sowie die Schöneicher-Rüdersdorfer Straßenbahn nutzen diese Möglichkeit oder haben es vor, sagt Crumbach. Auch in Strausberg verkehren Straßenbahnen.
Es sei jedoch zu bedenken, dass auch die Deutsche Bahn Fördermittel benötige, um ihre Bahnhöfe zu sanieren. Deswegen sei der finanzielle Spielraum nicht unbegrenzt. Wenn der Landtag an dieser Stelle einer Änderung des Doppelhaushalts zustimmt, wären die Mittel für die kommenden zwei Jahre gesichert, verspricht Crumbach.
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.
Keine Paywall, kein Kleingedrucktes, nur ein Ziel: dass nd bleibt.

https://gothamist.com/news/polluting-tra.title: Polluting trailers at Hunts Point market would be banned under new NYC Council bill
https://gothamist.com/news/polluting-tra.author: Elizabeth Kim
https://gothamist.com/news/polluting-tra.text:
A new City Council bill would ban idling diesel-powered refrigerated trailers in New York City warehouses, targeting a major polluter in the South Bronx: Hunts Point Produce Market.
The measure, which will be introduced Thursday by City Councilmember Justin Sanchez of the Bronx, seeks to force an end to the trailers that have long been a symbol of the environmental injustice that helped the South Bronx earn the nickname “asthma alley.” Gothamist reported in September that a $650 million deal to redevelop Hunts Point — and eliminate the need for the trailers — had collapsed amid concerns from the co-op of produce operators at the market, which supplies as much as 60% of the city’s produce.
The market, which sits on city-owned land, has for years relied on transport refrigeration units, also known as TRUs, to store produce because the facility’s 1960s-era warehouses are at capacity. The rumbling trailers are known for operating 24/7 at the site. Each trailer produces emissions equivalent to 330 truck trips on the Cross Bronx Expressway every day, according to the governor’s office.
In his final days in office, previous Mayor Eric Adams announced the plan to modernize the Hunts Point market facility. But the deal fell apart this summer under Mayor Zohran Mamdani after market operators raised questions about whether the project might disrupt their operations.
Sanchez’s bill applies to all stationary diesel-powered transport refrigeration units in large warehouses, food distribution centers, marine terminals and railyards across the city. Violators would face fines of up to $5,000.
“There is no reason why Hunts Point needs to suffer at the behest of being the food distribution hub of the city,” Sanchez said. The neighborhood, which is heavily trafficked by trucks, has some of the highest asthma rates in the country.
Joel Fireman, a third-generation Hunts Point produce operator and co-president of the co-op, disputed the extent of the pollution and said the bill would only wind up hurting a major employer in the Bronx. He said the site currently has around 800 trailers, many of which run on both diesel and electric.
But he said the market’s old infrastructure prevents operators from accessing more electricity. That is one of the major reasons city officials have encouraged the co-op to redevelop the facility.
“Environmentally we’re all in favor of cleaning up the market,” Fireman said. “Don’t put obstacles in our way. Come up with a solution.”
The bill comes ahead of a Dec.16 City Council hearing, when members are expected to grill administration officials on why the Hunts Point deal collapsed.
Mamdani has blamed his predecessor Eric Adams for rushing a deal before all parties agreed to the terms. He said the city is looking to “create a new path forward” but has not said whether the city can salvage the funding, which included $370 million in federal loans and grants.
Officials, including city Comptroller Mark Levine, have urged City Hall to try to resurrect the project, saying, “We cannot let this fail.”
Sanchez said his proposed legislation is intended to put pressure on everyone at the bargaining table. “We're not going to just let folks pollute our air indefinitely,” he said.
The current lease between the city and Hunts Point co-op operators expires in 2039. If passed, the legislation would take effect two years after it becomes law.
Sanchez said other U.S. municipalities have passed similar legislation. He said he is currently recruiting other council members to co-sponsor the bill.
Cassio Mendoza, a spokesperson for Mamdani, said the mayor’s office would review the legislation.
“The Mamdani administration remains committed to working with local stakeholders to identify solutions that reduce harmful emissions and improve the quality of life for Hunts Point residents,” he added in a statement.
A spokesperson for Council Speaker Julie Menin’s office said she will review the bill once it is introduced.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: ‘O racismo não é uma ideologia. O racismo estrutura o mundo’, afirma Carlos Moore
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Fabiana Reinholz
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
“É impossível mudar qualquer sociedade se a problemática racial e da racização do mundo não for enfrentada.” A afirmação do etnólogo, pesquisador e escritor cubano Carlos Moore sintetiza uma das principais teses de seu pensamento: o racismo não é apenas uma ideologia ou uma manifestação de preconceito, mas um fenômeno histórico que estrutura as relações sociais, políticas e culturais em escala global.
Moore esteve em Porto Alegre nesta semana, cumprindo uma agenda de atividades alusivas ao Novembro Negro. A iniciativa foi da Frente Negra Gaúcha, com apoio do Instituto Caminho, Ministério da Igualdade Racial, Odabá e Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS). Com uma trajetória marcada pela pesquisa sobre a história e as diferentes manifestações do racismo, percorreu 65 países e esteve ao lado de importantes referências da luta antirracista e do pensamento negro, como Malcolm X, Aimé Césaire, Cheikh Anta Diop, Fela Kuti e Lélia Gonzalez.
Em entrevista ao Brasil de Fato RS, o pesquisador questiona as explicações tradicionais sobre a origem do racismo, critica as estratégias de enfrentamento que, em sua avaliação, não alcançam a raiz do problema e defende que a compreensão de sua gênese histórica é indispensável para qualquer projeto de transformação social. As reflexões integram seu livro “Racismo Global – Última Fronteira do Ódio”.
Brasil de Fato RS: Em seu livro “Racismo Global – Última Fronteira do Ódio”, o senhor investiga as origens históricas do racismo e sua permanência como sistema de poder nas sociedades contemporâneas. Como esse sistema foi construído historicamente e quais mecanismos permitem que ele continue se reproduzindo, mesmo diante dos avanços legais e das conquistas dos movimentos negros?
Carlos Moore: O problema é que a maioria das pessoas que estudam a questão do racismo há mais de 60, 80 anos tem se concentrado nas repercussões do racismo, naquilo que ele é. Eu não me concentrei nisso, porque acho que há milhares de livros sobre o assunto. Queria entender como ele surgiu. As explicações que recebi nos 65 países que pesquisei, nas universidades de todas as partes do mundo, eram de que o racismo seria resultado do tráfico de escravizados do século 16 ou uma questão psicológica de pessoas brancas que queriam se sentir superiores. Para mim, isso não é explicação. É muito leviano.
Todas essas explicações tinham um problema que eu considerava mortal: utilizavam elementos que já estavam dentro do sistema para explicá-lo. Aí estamos em plena tautologia. Para explicar um fenômeno, você tem que sair dele; não pode explicá-lo desde dentro. É a questão do ovo e da galinha: quem veio primeiro?
Foi isso que me levou tanto tempo nesse trabalho. As pessoas me perguntam por que levei cinco décadas para escrever um livro assim. Porque tive que pesquisar muito. Saí da lógica acadêmica que explicava o racismo dentro do próprio racismo. Quando saí, encontrei um mundo muito complicado.
Não vou falar de todas as pesquisas agora, porque tudo isso estará no dia 30 de março, quando o livro sair em quatro línguas, simultaneamente, em nível mundial, e ficará disponível on-line. Decidi não publicar o livro individualmente. Assim, o planeta inteiro poderá ter acesso a ele, porque esse conhecimento não me pertence, pertence a toda a humanidade.
É por isso que abri mão de todo tipo de direito. Não recebo nenhum centavo. Só exijo que aqueles que vão lucrar, as livrarias e os editores, não vendam esse livro por mais de R$ 35. Não vou permitir que lucrem. Esse livro não é meu. Escrevi para o meu povo e para aqueles que são aliados do meu povo.
E demonstro que o racismo não é uma ideologia. É por isso que os movimentos negros têm falhado uma, duas, três, dez, 20, 25 vezes e seguirão falhando milhares de vezes, porque estão lutando contra o inimigo errado.
O planeta inteiro estava povoado por pessoas pretas, de cabelos lisos, como encontramos no sul da Índia e entre os aborígenes da Austrália
O racismo não é algo composto intelectualmente, não é uma construção monstruosa que vem da cabeça de um monstro. É algo processual, uma consciência histórica que surge ao longo de milhares de anos, por meio de processos simbólicos e de diferentes ressignificações.
O racismo surge de um imaginário que se concentrou e se consolidou em uma região específica, que identificamos e que não é a Europa. Sua gênese não vem da Europa, não tem nada a ver com ela. Todas essas coisas são o que a academia diz, mas o racismo não surgiu na Europa. Ele surgiu em uma faixa de território muito ampla, do norte da Índia até o sul do Irã. Foi ali que surgiu, pela primeira vez, uma população despigmentada.
As pessoas brancas não vêm da Europa. O continente era povoado por populações melanizadas, fortemente melanizadas, pessoas pretas, inclusive com olhos azuis e cabelos lisos. A humanidade sempre teve cabelos lisos; os cabelos crespos são uma variação que surgiu nos últimos 100 a 150 mil anos. A humanidade moderna surgiu há 300 mil, 350 mil anos. Já a humanidade nasceu na África há 2 milhões, 2,5 milhões de anos: uma humanidade preta, de cabelos lisos, dividida em muitas espécies diferentes que já se extinguiram.
O planeta inteiro estava povoado por pessoas pretas, de cabelos lisos, como encontramos no sul da Índia e entre os aborígenes da Austrália. Essas populações representam os primeiros africanos que saíram da África e povoaram o mundo. Não estou falando da diáspora recente, formada por pessoas que, nos últimos 500 anos, foram violentamente arrancadas da África, mas daqueles que saíram primeiro e povoaram o planeta.
Essas eram pessoas bem pretas, de cabelos lisos. Povoaram todo o planeta, até a Argentina. O Brasil foi um grande centro dessa população africana. Aqui, Walter Neves, que é daqui, foi o primeiro a questionar que o Brasil estivesse povoado por pessoas indígenas. Ele encontrou os crânios de Lagoa Santa, em Minas Gerais, e afirmou que aquelas feições não eram indígenas.
Os americanos o atacaram e disseram que ele era um mentiroso. Então, ele mandou o material para a Grã-Bretanha e, por meio de tomografia moderna, reproduziram a face dessa pessoa, que chamaram de Luzia. Era uma pessoa de pele preta e traços da Melanésia, porque estive na Melanésia pesquisando e conheço essas populações. Eram melanésios, pretos, de cabelos lisos. Todos ficaram espantados. Os jornais daqui trouxeram isso na capa: Luzia, o Brasil foi povoado por negros.
Mas de onde surgiram essas populações? Isso demonstra que a academia já havia intoxicado as pessoas com a ideia de que os negros vieram com a última chuva, de que as primeiras populações eram brancas. É isso que a academia sempre sustentou. Da mesma maneira, sustentou que as primeiras civilizações eram formadas por pessoas brancas, até no Egito, em plena África. Diziam que os negros não eram negros, que eram brancos que tinham vindo de outro lugar. Mas de que lugar? Porque em todo o Irã, no Oriente Médio e nessas regiões não havia pessoas brancas.
A genética e a paleogenética estão acabando com os mitos da academia, com as mentiras que vêm sendo contadas há dois séculos.
A equipe de genética da Universidade da Filadélfia demonstrou que o primeiro branco surgiu no Oriente Médio, entre a Índia e o sul do Irã, há 7 mil ou 8 mil anos. O ser humano surgiu há 2,5 milhões de anos na África, e o primeiro despigmentado era um africano, não um alienígena. Era um africano que nasceu despigmentado: um bebê inteiramente branco. Isso aconteceu, é algo que a genética demonstrou.
O primeiro bebê branco é o ancestral de todos os brancos europeus. Não há como brincar mais com esse assunto.
Então, o que aconteceu? É aí que está o problema, onde o Racismo Global entra. Passo a explicar o que aconteceu com esse bebê branco. Quando chegou aos 16, 17 anos, ele se casou com outra pessoa, uma mulher preta. Se esse primeiro bebê branco se casa com uma mulher bem preta, o filho não pode ser totalmente branco. Então, ele vai ser reabsorvido pela maioria. Como uma pessoa branca pode sobreviver sem ser reabsorvida e sem que o traço branco desapareça?
A genética demonstra que o traço da pele branca existe há 25 mil, 28 mil anos nas populações pretas daquela região, mas não se expressava geneticamente. Esse traço viveu adormecido nessa mulher negra, que foi espalhando-o. Todos eram pretos, mas carregavam esse traço adormecido dentro de si.
Ele somente despertou há 7 mil anos, com esse bebê. A partir daí, as pessoas daquela região que carregavam o traço foram se reproduzindo. O bebê se casou com outra mulher preta, que também tinha o traço. Os dois traços se combinaram e reproduziram uma pessoa de pele novamente branca. Com os casamentos que aconteceram durante mil ou dois mil anos, uma população branca surgiu normalmente.
Mas ela não surgiu, como diziam os biólogos e antropólogos, por uma despigmentação progressiva de 30 mil, 40 mil anos, de pessoas pretas que vão branqueando porque estão no frio. Isso já não é possível sustentar. Desde 2005, ninguém pode sustentar essa explicação. O primeiro branco surgiu por mutação, repentinamente. Em 24 horas, uma mulher que estava grávida havia nove meses deu à luz um bebê branco.
É a partir desses fatos, que considero cientificamente provados, que acumulei minha pesquisa de 30, 40 anos. Aquilo que eu já havia descoberto em Papua-Nova Guiné, na Austrália, nas Filipinas, na Indonésia e em todos esses países onde passei era que a cor branca havia sido disseminada pelas populações africanas pelo planeta inteiro como a cor dos ancestrais.
Esse bebê branco foi imediatamente acolhido como um enviado dos ancestrais. Não foi agredido, porque poderia ter sido destruído. Se tivessem visto nele algo maléfico, teriam destruído imediatamente. Não haveria nenhuma pessoa branca no planeta.
Mas os africanos que saíram da África há 60 mil, 70 mil anos saíram com uma visão ampla, uma explicação do mundo na qual ele estava dividido em três partes. Uma era a das pessoas físicas, que morriam; outra, a das pessoas que viviam em um centro, com um pé de um lado e outro pé do outro lado; e, do outro lado, estavam os ancestrais.
Aqueles que viviam deste lado eram pessoas que tinham a cor da terra. Os que viviam do outro lado, em outro domínio, eram pessoas que não tinham nenhuma cor, porque eram invisíveis. Eles identificaram a invisibilidade com a cor branca. Espalharam a visão de que os ancestrais são invisíveis. Portanto, a única coisa que se pode assemelhar à invisibilidade é a cor branca.
Em toda a Melanésia, comprovei que todos diziam que seus ancestrais eram dessa cor. É por isso que, quando os primeiros europeus chegaram a essas sociedades, foram acolhidos como ancestrais. Vi que, na África, grupo após grupo, todos contavam a mesma história. Os europeus não foram hostilizados, foram recebidos de braços abertos. Diziam: são nossos ancestrais que estão voltando.
Aí compreendi que essa situação era muito complexa. O racismo não surge de uma visão ideológica. Surge de muitas coisas que provocam um conflito sério dentro da sociedade. Esse conflito, que era social, envolvia duas populações: uma de cor branca e outra de cor preta. Era um conflito entre duas elites: uma elite espiritual e uma elite política. Essas elites se desgarraram, certamente ocorreram guerras civis em muitos lugares, e dessas lutas intensas pelo poder interno nessas sociedades surgiu uma linha de cor, que foi a única maneira pela qual o conflito se fixou no fenótipo.
Então, é algo processual. Dessas lutas surgiu uma consciência coletiva de origem histórica, não ideológica. Isso é o que estou demonstrando em Racismo Global.
Ao longo de sua trajetória como pesquisador, o senhor percorreu cerca de 65 países e conheceu diferentes realidades da população negra. Quais são as principais semelhanças entre as formas de manifestação do racismo nesses diferentes contextos? É possível falar em um sistema global de dominação racial que assume características próprias de acordo com a história de cada sociedade?
A primeira coisa que devemos esclarecer é que o racismo não surge de um lugar específico. É um fenômeno multimodal. Surge em lugares diferentes, em épocas distintas e sem conexão uns com os outros.
Essa visão tradicional de que o racismo surgiu na Europa e, de lá, fez uma metástase, como se fosse um câncer, não tem nada a ver com a realidade histórica. O racismo não surgiu na Europa, nem dos europeus. A população branca chegou ao continente por invasão.
Sabemos hoje que essas invasões vieram do Oriente Médio, pelo sul e pela região da Ucrânia e da Rússia, pelo norte. Eram duas populações brancas que vieram do mesmo lugar. As populações que povoaram originalmente a Europa eram pretas, muito pretas, algumas com olhos azuis e cabelos lisos.
A Europa não tem nada a ver com a origem do racismo. É no norte da Índia e no Oriente Médio que surge a população branca. Ela é recente, se comparada à população africana, que surgiu há mais de 2 milhões de anos.
O que acontece é que, a partir do século 16, a Europa, já ocupada por populações brancas, começa a se expandir. Há cerca de 3 mil anos, as invasões Yamnaya eliminaram e substituíram as populações europeias originais, nativas, que eram de pele preta. Com essas invasões, a Europa começou a se transformar. Foi daí que surgiram os aqueus, os dórios, povos ancestrais dos gregos, os romanos e os ilírios, povos de pele branca.
Os brancos não são outra coisa senão africanos despigmentados. Não vieram de Marte, não vieram de outro planeta, não têm uma existência diferente da sua e da minha.
Essa narrativa que criaram, de que eram um povo especial, vindo de outro lugar especial, é a base do racismo. Ela se formou em vários lugares, onde povos despigmentados entraram em conflito com povos pigmentados.
O racismo é uma visão histórica, escatológica e missional. Não é uma ideologia construída por alguém, por um monstro ou por um louco que decidiu criar isso
O racismo se converte em algo centralizado mais recentemente, porque houve uma planetarização da economia. E essa planetarização aconteceu a partir de fatos catastróficos. A Europa saiu da Europa e dizimou praticamente todos os povos do mundo. Em todas as partes, os europeus caíram sobre as populações e cometeram genocídios.
Esses genocídios não são coisas que aconteceram por acaso. Há uma história por trás. A visão desses povos que saíram da Europa era uma visão que já existia havia milhares de anos, de conflitos em torno de recursos e de poder político entre populações pigmentadas e despigmentadas.
As populações despigmentadas sempre foram pequenas minorias, que viviam em uma ecologia humana fechada. Porque é lógico: se elas se misturam com as maiorias, desaparecem. É uma população que vê o mundo em termos de segregação e de eliminação do outro.
O racismo é uma visão histórica, escatológica e missional. Não é uma ideologia construída por alguém, por um monstro ou por um louco que decidiu criar isso. Não é o capitalismo que criou, como diz a esquerda. Não tem nada a ver com capitalismo, comunismo ou socialismo. O racismo está lá, surgiu processualmente. Não foi algo que surgiu imediatamente. Surgiu de muitas coisas.
É possível construir um projeto efetivamente emancipatório sem colocar a questão racial no centro da transformação da sociedade?
É impossível. O racismo não é uma ideologia. O racismo estrutura o mundo. Estrutura as relações sociais, as relações políticas, as relações culturais e, inclusive, o casamento das pessoas. O racismo está em todas as dimensões.
Não é possível mudar qualquer sociedade se a questão da origem, a gênese do racismo, não for compreendida e combatida da maneira como deve ser. Não como ideologia, mas compreendendo que há uma população, um segmento da população mundial, que é de origem africana, mas que construiu historicamente uma narrativa dizendo que não vinha da África, que não tinha nada a ver com os africanos, por causa de um ódio escatológico à pele negra.
É impossível mudar qualquer sociedade se a problemática racial e da racização do mundo não for enfrentada
Ao cortar-se da história, esse grupo se cortou do mundo e construiu um mundo irreal, que não existe. E partiu para a conquista do planeta, para purificá-lo, para eliminar tudo aquilo que era maléfico e tudo aquilo que era inverdade, porque a verdade estava unicamente nas mãos desse grupo especial, enviado especialmente como grupo eleito por forças que nós sabemos quais são, para introduzir a ordem e a civilização.
Olha, não é aquilo que se está ensinando nas escolas e nas universidades: que a civilização veio da Grécia e que todo o planeta era habitado por bárbaros, selvagens, até os gregos. Os primeiros pensadores, inclusive, não eram gregos. Não é essa a história que se conta?
Então, é impossível mudar qualquer sociedade se a problemática racial e da racização do mundo não for enfrentada. Porque o mundo foi racizado, não racializado. As estruturas são racializadas, mas os seres humanos são racizados. Essa é outra coisa.
Se você não coloca o problema da racização no centro do debate, não saímos nunca do problema, nunca.

https://www.humanite.fr/sciences/cellule.title: Un consortium français crée une peau artificielle prête à la greffe : une première mondiale
https://www.humanite.fr/sciences/cellule.author: La rédaction avec AFP
https://www.humanite.fr/sciences/cellule.text:
C’est une avancée qui pourrait devenir « une révolution médicale ». Un consortium, composé d’acteurs publics et privés, a annoncé, vendredi 20 novembre, avoir réussi à créer en laboratoire de la peau artificielle conçue pour être « prête à greffer ». L'expérimentation doit encore faire ses preuves en essais cliniques.
« Pour la première fois au monde, on a réussi, en laboratoire, à créer de la peau artificielle prête à greffer. » Cette expérimentation, dont s’enthousiasme, vendredi 20 novembre auprès de l’AFP, Guirec Le Lous, président du groupe Urgo, doit encore faire ses preuves en essais cliniques.
Elle n’en est pas moins « un exploit technologique » réalisé par un consortium qui réunit, outre le groupe spécialiste de la cicatrisation et du pansement, le CNRS, Lyon 1 Université, le Centre d’Étude des Cellules souches, l’Établissement français du sang et Dassault Systèmes. Et il pourrait ouvrir la voie à « une révolution médicale ».
Une découverte profitable au privé ?
Actuellement, l’autogreffe est la technique chirurgicale la plus souvent utilisée. Elle consiste à prélever de la peau saine du patient pour ensuite la poser sur des zones brûlées.
Là, l’ambition, à terme, est de mettre à la disposition des chirurgiens une peau artificielle produite à l’avance, sans prélèvement de cellules du patient, conservée à -150 °C et une fois décongelée, disponible immédiatement au bloc opératoire pour des patients qui ont des plaies sévères comme les grands brûlés. « Après décongélation, ses cellules restent vivantes et fonctionnelles », explique le consortium dans un communiqué.
« Cette avancée 100 % française » prépare la voie à une étude clinique prévue « dès 2030 » dans les installations pharmaceutiques de l’EFS et à un « passage à l’échelle industrielle pour une commercialisation à l’horizon 2040 », selon le communiqué.
Urgo, de son côté entend bien tirer profit de la découverte. Le groupe, qui « fait désormais partie de la dizaine d’entreprises dans le monde » à disposer de sa propre « banque de cellules » pour la peau artificielle, prévoit de se doter des moyens industriels pour produire à grande échelle, « à l’issue de cette première étude clinique à l’horizon 2032 ».
La science et la conscience
Nous avons besoin de vous pour porter dans le débat public la voix d’un média libre, qui porte haut les combats du monde de la recherche, partage ses découvertes.
- Ainsi, l’Humanité Magazine est partenaire de l’Académie des sciences depuis 2015 pour révéler chaque mois le meilleur de la recherche scientifique.
- Sur Humanité.fr, dans l’Humanité magazine et chaque mardi dans l’Humanité, retrouvez l’actualité scientifique décryptée par nos journalistes spécialisés.
Aidez-nous à alimenter la réflexion sur les enjeux éthiques, politiques et sociétaux qui accompagnent le progrès scientifique.
Je veux en savoir plus !

Internationaler Gen-Z-Protesttag: Gewerkschaften rufen zu Demonstrationen in Frankreich auf
Dem breiten Bündnis gehören auch linke Jugendverbände an. Proteste soll es in mindestens 16 Städten geben.
„Die Welt brennt“, schreibt die Gewerkschaft Solidaires Étudiant·e·s in einem Instagram-Beitrag vom 15. November. Gemeinsam mit einem großen Bündnis ruft die studentische Gewerkschaft für Freitag erneut zu Schüler*innen- und Studierendenprotesten in Frankreich auf und fordert Bildung ohne Militarismus, öffentliche Investitionen in den Bildungs- und Gesundheitssektor, bezahlbaren Wohnraum und Klimagerechtigkeit. Der Instagram-Beitrag ist hinterlegt mit dem Lied: „No war, but class war“ von JJ Demon.
In Frankreich waren im September Schüler*innen für bessere Bildung auf die Straßen gegangen. Ihnen schlossen sich Studierende an, und schließlich schwappten die Proteste auch auf andere europäische Staaten über.
Seitdem brechen die Proteste in Frankreich nicht ab. Am Dienstag erlebte das Land einen weiteren landesweiten Protest- und Streiktag, an dem Hunderttausende für höhere Gehälter und bessere Bildungsbedingungen auf die Straßen gingen. Nach Angaben der Gewerkschaft CGT (Confédération Générale du Travail) nahm eine halbe Million Menschen an den Protesten teil, 175.000 davon in Paris. Das Innenministerium zählte seinerseits 146.000 Demonstrant*innen in ganz Frankreich, die Pariser Polizeipräfektur gab die Teilnehmerzahl in der Hauptstadt mit 28.000 an. Die französische Regierung will mit einem harten Sparkurs das Haushaltsdefizit wieder in den Griff bekommen.
Für Freitag haben das europäische Bündnis Youth Strike aus den drei studentischen Gewerkschaften L’Union Étudiante, Solidaires Étudiant·e·s und Mouvement National Lycéenne sowie der Organisation Young Struggle zu Protesten in mindestens 16 französischen Städten aufgerufen. Für Paris geht das Mouvement National Lycéenne von 10.000 Protestierenden aus. Sie hofft außerdem, dass die Proteste auch über das Wochenende hinaus aufrechterhalten werden.
Auch einer der einflussreichsten französischen Gewerkschaftsbünde ruft zum Streik auf. Die CGT fordert sogar zu einem neuntägigen Streik auf, beginnend mit dem 20. November, der gleichzeitig Internationaler Tag der Kinderrechte ist. Die CGT fordert von der Regierung, den Arbeitgeberverbänden und den Fraktionen im Parlament, auf die sozialen Forderungen einzugehen.
Den Streikaufruf unterzeichneten an die 20 weitere Organisationen, darunter Guerre à la Guerre, La Jeunesse Communiste, Zora France. In Paris startet der Streik am Freitag, den 20. November, um 14 Uhr auf der Avenue de l’Observatoire an der Haltestelle Port Royal. Nicht nur in Paris, auch in Lyon, Rennes, Grenobles, Marseille, Montpellier, Toulouse und Pontivy wird zum Streik aufgerufen. Die französische Zeitung Le Monde berichtet, dass die internationalen Vertreter der Organisationen hoffen, im Rahmen der gemeinsamen Mobilisierung, die in ihrem Ausmaß beispiellos ist, „Millionen“ Menschen auf die Straße zu bringen.
Nicht alle können sich an den Demonstrationen beteiligen. Von einer Schule im Banlieue 93, nicht weit von dort, wo die Proteste ihren Ausgang genommen hatten, berichtet ein Lehrer, seine Schüler*innen könnten nicht teilnehmen, weil sie keine Papiere haben.
